READ FIRST

How to Use This Atlas

A theme page explains a recurring research pressure. A paper-atlas entry explains the concept inside one publication. The useful unit is not the abstract or title. It is the paper's chosen mathematical object: a verifier, a graph, a distribution, a quotient space, a feasible set, a trajectory, an activation direction, a compute budget, or a latent representation.

The same publication can appear in several themes because one technical idea often answers multiple questions. CyberGym is a security benchmark, an agent-process diagnostic, and an executable evaluation method. Quotient-Space Diffusion is a generative model, a geometry paper, and a sampler-correctness paper. The atlas keeps those connections visible while giving each paper one first-principles read.

FAMILY 01

Agents and Executable Evaluation

CyberGym

ICLR 2026

CyberGym's core concept is executable vulnerability evidence. A security agent has not solved a vulnerability task merely by naming a bug class or writing a plausible explanation. The first-principles object is a program-state distinction: the exploit should succeed against the vulnerable version and fail against the patched version. CyberGym turns that object into an executable benchmark with real projects, proof-of-concept tests, patches, and validators. The important evidence is therefore a working action trace in code, not a verbal claim about security. This makes the benchmark a direct test of whether an agent can connect diagnosis, exploit construction, patch semantics, and execution feedback.

Mathematical object
A verifier over program versions: exploit passes on pre-patch state and fails on post-patch state.
Approach
Builds 1,507 real-vulnerability tasks across 188 projects and validates generated PoCs by executing them.
Themes
LLM agents and process diagnostics; evaluation and measurement; robustness and security impact.

OpenApps

ICLR 2026

OpenApps' core concept is environment variation as a robustness variable. A UI agent can appear competent when every button, label, layout, and content item stays fixed, but that success may come from memorized cues rather than workflow understanding. The first-principles object is a distribution over app states, not one screenshot. OpenApps makes apps configurable and evaluates agents across many variants, so the measured behavior is whether the agent can preserve the task plan when appearance and content change. The failure modes are concrete: success swings across variants, repeated loops, hallucinated actions, and brittle grounding where the agent clicks the wrong object because the surface shifted.

Mathematical object
A task distribution over app configurations, not a single deterministic UI state.
Approach
Evaluates multimodal agents across thousands of app variants and tracks success swings, loops, and hallucinated actions.
Themes
UI-agent reliability; environment variation; grounding failures under distribution shift.

MedAgentGym

ICLR 2026

MedAgentGym's core concept is biomedical data science as an executable agent environment. A biomedical agent should not be judged by whether it can describe an analysis plan; it must manipulate files, write code, inspect feedback, and improve a measurable scientific result. The first-principles problem is to turn biomedical reasoning into a closed loop where actions have consequences. The benchmark provides sandboxed coding tasks with ground truth and task feedback, so the object being evaluated is a trajectory of code actions, observations, and outcomes. This matters because scientific-agent claims need executable evidence: the analysis either runs and improves the task, or it does not.

Mathematical object
A trajectory of code actions with ground truth, feedback, and task outcome.
Approach
Provides 72,413 sandboxed biomedical coding tasks and trains Med-Copilot with offline and online RL.
Themes
Executable biomedical agents; scientific discovery; healthcare ML.

SandboxEscapeBench

ICML 2026

SandboxEscapeBench's core concept is the sandbox boundary as the object of evaluation. A tool-using model can run commands, chain observations, and exploit accidental permissions, so safety cannot be measured only through text refusals. The first-principles problem is reachability: can an agent starting inside a restricted environment obtain host-level evidence that should be outside its authority? The benchmark turns that question into concrete escape tasks across misconfiguration, privilege, runtime, orchestration, and kernel layers. The evidence is not whether the model explains an attack, but whether its executed action trace crosses the boundary and retrieves the protected object.

Mathematical object
A reachability condition: can the agent obtain host-level evidence such as a protected flag from inside a nested sandbox?
Approach
Covers public escape tasks across misconfiguration, privilege, runtime, orchestration, and host/kernel layers.
Themes
Agent infrastructure risk; CTF-style evaluation; sandbox safety.

EditBench

ICLR 2026

EditBench's core concept is code editing under real context. A code assistant is not usually asked to write an isolated function from a clean prompt; it receives a cursor position, highlighted text, surrounding files, and an instruction whose meaning depends on that local state. The first-principles problem is conditional editing: the same words can require different patches depending on where the user is working. EditBench evaluates wild code-edit tasks and measures how success changes when realistic context is present. The evidence boundary is whether the assistant produces the intended patch without changing unrelated code or ignoring the active editing surface.

Mathematical object
A conditional edit function from instruction and local code context to a patch.
Approach
Evaluates 40 LLMs on 545 wild code-edit tasks and measures how realistic context shifts success.
Themes
Evaluation; coding assistant reliability; developer tools.

OmniVerifier

ICLR 2026

OmniVerifier's core concept is visual outcome verification. A visual model may produce an image, edit a scene, answer a question, or follow an instruction, but the claim is incomplete until the result is checked against the requested visual condition. The first-principles problem is to turn visual satisfaction into a reusable function over instruction, image, and expected outcome. OmniVerifier builds a verifier across many task categories and uses it for iterative refinement, making evaluation part of the generation loop. The failure boundary is a verifier that rewards surface plausibility while missing the object, relation, count, edit, or spatial fact the task actually required.

Mathematical object
A verification function over image, instruction, and expected visual outcome.
Approach
Builds ViVerBench and OmniVerifier-7B across 16 task categories, then uses verification for iterative refinement.
Themes
Evaluation; test-time scaling; visual verification.

Rational Agents

ICLR 2026

Rational Agents' core concept is information-gain-guided interaction. An agent that can ask questions should not choose questions by politeness, surface relevance, or similarity to the final answer. It should choose the query that most reduces uncertainty about the hidden state that controls the next action. The first-principles object is expected information gain over possible worlds and future decisions. The paper uses Monte Carlo inference in dialogue-style games such as Battleship and Guess Who, where each question has a measurable value because it changes the posterior over hidden states. The evidence is whether interaction improves decisions under a real query budget.

Mathematical object
Expected information gain over possible hidden states and future actions.
Approach
Uses Monte Carlo expected-information-gain inference in dialogue-style games such as Battleship and Guess Who.
Themes
Reasoning, planning, tool use; resource-rational dialogue.

TRACE Effort

ICLR 2026

TRACE Effort's core concept is reward hacking detected through reasoning effort. A model can sometimes satisfy a verifier before it has performed the work that should be necessary for the task. The first-principles problem is to distinguish real reasoning progress from low-effort verifier passing. The paper treats verifier success as a function of truncated chain-of-thought: if reward appears early, before task-specific reasoning has enough information to justify the answer, the high score is suspicious. This makes effort a diagnostic variable, not a style preference. The evidence is whether the timing of reward exposes shortcuts that final-answer accuracy would hide.

Mathematical object
Verifier success as a function of progressively truncated chain-of-thought.
Approach
Flags low-effort verifier-passing behavior by measuring when reward appears along a reasoning trace.
Themes
Reward hacking; process diagnostics; evaluation reliability.
FAMILY 02

Inference Control and Alignment

Steer Like the LLM

ICML 2026

The core concept is activation-space steering. Prompting changes behavior by adding words to the input, but the behavior finally travels through hidden states. The first-principles question is whether a prompt's effect can be separated from the prompt text and represented as a controllable internal intervention. The paper learns position-specific steering replacements that reproduce prompt-induced behavior, making the control object a direction and coefficient inside the model rather than an external instruction string. The evidence boundary is whether the intervention changes the intended behavior without broadly damaging unrelated capabilities.

Mathematical object
A direction or position-specific coefficient in hidden-state space.
Approach
Trains Prompt Steering Replacement models that mimic prompt effects with interpretable activation interventions.
Themes
Interpretability as intervention; inference-time model control.

The Tell-Tale Norm

ICML 2026

The core concept is an internal scalar as a compute-allocation signal. A model's hidden state is not only a carrier of content; its magnitude can reveal something about the model's current reasoning state. The first-principles problem is whether the system can decide when to think more by reading its own internal evidence rather than relying on a separate controller. The Tell-Tale Norm treats hidden-state L2 norm as an endogenous statistic for recursion, steering, and response selection. The claim is useful only if norm changes predict when extra computation changes the answer, and if routing by that signal improves decisions without turning every hard-looking prompt into wasted inference.

Mathematical object
The L2 norm of hidden states as an endogenous statistic.
Approach
Uses norm signals to allocate or steer test-time computation without additional training data.
Themes
Interpretability; test-time scaling; reasoning control.

Enhancing Reasoning for Diffusion LLMs via DMPO

ICML 2026

The core concept is distribution matching for non-autoregressive reasoning. Autoregressive RL post-training treats generation as a left-to-right action sequence, but a diffusion language model revises a noisy sequence through denoising steps. The first-principles problem is that the policy object is different: the update must improve the distribution over completed outputs and denoising paths, not a next-token chain that the model does not use. DMPO builds the reward-tilted target distribution directly and corrects small-batch coverage errors, so reasoning improvement is framed as moving one generation distribution toward another under reward evidence.

Mathematical object
A reward-tilted target distribution over diffusion LM outputs and denoising paths.
Approach
Uses distribution matching policy optimization and baseline corrections for small-batch mode-coverage errors.
Themes
Diffusion language models; test-time scaling; RL post-training.

RAGEN-2

ICML 2026

The core concept is reasoning collapse as low mutual information with the task. Long reasoning is not automatically useful; it can become a reusable template that changes little when the input changes. The first-principles problem is dependency: a reasoning trajectory should carry information from the specific problem into the chosen action or answer. RAGEN-2 measures collapse with a mutual-information proxy between input and reasoning trajectory and explains why weak within-input reward variance can let template reasoning pass. The important boundary is that entropy or length can look healthy while task dependence has already failed. The evidence must show reasoning changes with the problem.

Mathematical object
A mutual-information proxy between input and reasoning trajectory.
Approach
Explains collapse through weak within-input reward variance and detects template reasoning that entropy misses.
Themes
Agentic RL diagnostics; reward signal quality; process failure.

AuxDPO

ICLR 2026

The core concept is preference optimization under model-class misspecification. Preference data may come from a reward structure that the available policy class cannot represent exactly. In that case, a direct preference objective can push the model in a direction that looks locally justified but reverses the intended preference once the geometry of the policy class is respected. The first-principles problem is to update within the model's feasible behavior space, not in an imagined reward space. AuxDPO adds auxiliary variables that approximate natural-gradient policy updates around the local RLHF solution, making preference training a question of update geometry under constraints.

Mathematical object
Preference objective geometry and auxiliary variables approximating natural-gradient policy updates.
Approach
Shows DPO can reverse preferences under unrealizable rewards and adds auxiliary variables to correct the update geometry.
Themes
Alignment; preference optimization; theory unifying RLHF practice.

ScaleRL

ICLR 2026

The core concept is predictable scaling for RL post-training. A large RL run is expensive because the system pays for rollouts, reward evaluation, optimizer steps, and failed exploration before knowing whether the run will keep improving. The first-principles problem is to turn that risk into a measurable curve: how quickly performance rises, when it saturates, and whether more compute changes the ceiling or only reaches it sooner. ScaleRL fits sigmoidal compute-performance curves and uses them to extrapolate larger runs, making RL post-training a budgeted forecasting problem rather than a blind bet on more compute.

Mathematical object
Sigmoidal compute-performance scaling curves for validation performance.
Approach
Fits predictive curves and demonstrates extrapolation up to a 100,000 GPU-hour RL run.
Themes
RL scaling; alignment; inference-control recipes.

Gaussian certified unlearning in high dimensions

ICLR 2026

The core concept is deletion as a hypothesis-testing guarantee. Unlearning is not just lowering accuracy on one example or editing a checkpoint after a request. The claim is stronger: after deletion, an observer should have little statistical power to tell whether the model came from the original training run plus unlearning or from retraining without the deleted point. In high dimensions, the amount and shape of added noise matter because small-looking perturbations can still leave recoverable influence. The paper frames deletion through Gaussian certifiability, using a Newton-style update plus calibrated noise and measuring the utility cost of making residual information hard to recover.

Mathematical object
Epsilon-Gaussian certifiability and hypothesis-testing privacy under calibrated Gaussian noise.
Approach
Uses one Newton step plus noise and measures prediction-level degradation after deletion.
Themes
Certified unlearning; privacy definitions; deployment-driven theory.

Catch-22

ICML 2026

The core concept is the watermarking trilemma. A useful text watermark wants three things at once: survive paraphrase or edits, remain hard to notice without the key, and remain easy for the owner to detect. The first-principles conflict is that detectability requires a distributional signal, while stealth asks that the same signal be hard to distinguish from normal text. Robustness then asks that the signal persist after an adversary changes the text. Catch-22 studies this as hypothesis testing between watermarked and unwatermarked distributions, showing why provenance claims must state which of the three demands is being weakened.

Mathematical object
KL-based hypothesis testing between watermarked and unwatermarked text distributions.
Approach
Characterizes tradeoffs among robustness, stealth, and reliable verification.
Themes
Watermarking; safety bounds; information-theoretic governance.
FAMILY 03

Generative and Physical Structure

Quotient-Space Diffusion Model

ICLR 2026

The core concept is generation modulo symmetry. A molecule rotated or translated in 3D is not a new molecule; it is the same physical object under a different coordinate frame. If diffusion runs in raw coordinates, the model can spend probability mass learning arbitrary pose variation instead of chemical structure. The first-principles problem is to sample the object that matters, not redundant descriptions of it. The paper places the generative process on the quotient space and then lifts samples back, so symmetry is handled as part of the state space rather than patched by post-hoc alignment that can change the target distribution.

Mathematical object
The quotient space R^{3N} / SE(3).
Approach
Derives lifted quotient-space diffusion and contrasts it with alignment heuristics that may alter the sampling target.
Themes
Structured generative modeling; scientific-domain generation; sampler correctness.

Protein Autoregressive Modeling

ICML 2026

The core concept is coarse-to-fine physical structure generation. A protein backbone is not a bag of coordinates; local geometry is constrained by a larger fold, and the larger fold is constrained by physical and biological function. The first-principles problem is choosing a generation order that respects this hierarchy. A flat generator can produce locally plausible fragments that do not form a coherent backbone. This paper makes scale part of the model: it predicts structure from coarse global shape toward finer detail and uses a flow decoder so motif-conditioned and backbone generation preserve the physical object across resolutions.

Mathematical object
A multiscale protein backbone representation with next-scale prediction.
Approach
Combines coarse-to-fine autoregression with a flow-based decoder for robust backbone and motif-conditioned generation.
Themes
Scientific and physical generation; structured generative modeling.

Latent Spherical Flow Policy

ICML 2026

The core concept is sampling feasible structured actions through a solver. In combinatorial reinforcement learning, the agent cannot choose any vector it likes; actions must satisfy discrete constraints such as routes, matchings, assignments, or schedules. The first-principles problem is to explore a rich policy distribution without wasting probability on invalid decisions. The paper learns a continuous spherical latent flow and composes it with a combinatorial solver, so samples become valid structured actions after decoding. This separates diversity from feasibility: the flow provides stochastic search pressure, while the solver preserves the action constraints that define the task.

Mathematical object
A spherical latent flow distribution composed with a combinatorial solver.
Approach
Uses flow matching to learn expressive stochastic policies in compact latent space.
Themes
Hybrid neural-symbolic systems; generative modeling for decision-making.

Spherical Watermark

ICLR 2026

The core concept is watermarking without breaking the latent prior. In diffusion generation, the initial noise distribution is part of the model's contract: if the watermark makes the noise statistically unnatural, image quality or stealth can fail. The first-principles problem is to encode provenance while preserving the distribution the generator expects. Spherical Watermark uses spherical mapping, orthogonal rotation, and chi-square radius scaling to place bits inside latent Gaussian geometry, then reconstructs a multivariate Gaussian prior. The evidence is whether detection works while samples still behave like they came from the intended noise law rather than a visibly distorted source.

Mathematical object
Latent Gaussian noise with spherical mapping, orthogonal rotation, and chi-square radius scaling.
Approach
Embeds watermark bits into diffusion latent noise while reconstructing a multivariate Gaussian prior.
Themes
Diffusion media provenance; distribution-preserving watermark design.

FALCON

ICLR 2026

The core concept is likelihood-usable molecular flow sampling. In molecular equilibrium estimation, generating plausible structures is not enough because downstream thermodynamic inference often needs probabilities for importance weighting. The first-principles problem is to produce samples and know how much probability mass the sampler assigned to them. A fast few-step generator that lacks usable likelihoods can give attractive molecules while failing as an inference instrument. FALCON trains continuous flows with invertibility pressure so samples arrive quickly and likelihood estimates remain accurate enough for reweighting. The claim is therefore not only generative quality, but usable probability accounting for molecular science.

Mathematical object
A continuous flow with invertibility pressure and usable likelihood estimates.
Approach
Trains flows that provide fast samples and likelihoods accurate enough for importance sampling.
Themes
Scientific generation; probabilistic inference; molecular flows.

PRISM

ICLR 2026

The core concept is structured semantic mediation between brain signals and images. fMRI is a noisy measurement of brain activity, not a direct pixel code. The first-principles problem is to choose an intermediate representation that preserves what the person perceived while discarding measurement noise and scanner-specific detail. PRISM maps brain signals into object, attribute, and relation text before reconstruction, so the bridge between brain and image carries interpretable scene structure. The test is not only whether the image looks sharp, but whether the reconstruction keeps the objects and relations that the neural signal supports.

Mathematical object
A structured text latent space of objects, attributes, and relations.
Approach
Projects brain signals into structured text and uses object-centric diffusion to reduce perceptual reconstruction loss.
Themes
Multimodal models; scientific/physical generation; neural reconstruction.

FlashVID

ICLR 2026

The core concept is video understanding as token-budget allocation. A long video cannot be treated as unlimited evidence, because every frame and patch competes for attention memory and inference cost. The first-principles problem is deciding which visual tokens remain distinct, which can be merged, and which temporal changes must stay visible for the task. FlashVID builds a representative-token selection and merging operator across space and time, trying to keep action-relevant and event-relevant evidence while discarding redundant pixels. The failure boundary is clear: compression is wrong when the removed tokens carry the detail needed to answer, localize, or reason over the video.

Mathematical object
A representative-token selection and merging operator over spatiotemporal visual tokens.
Approach
Merges video redundancy across space and time, preserving performance with a small fraction of tokens.
Themes
Efficiency; multimodal long-video understanding.

CompSLOT

ICLR 2026

The core concept is object-centric memory for continual learning. A model forgets when new training pressure overwrites the internal pieces that old tasks still need. The first-principles problem is to decide what unit should be remembered. If memory is stored only as a broad parameter update, old concepts can be blended or erased. CompSLOT uses object-centric slots, primitive selection, and concept-similarity distillation so memories remain compositional: parts can be reused, compared, and protected. The evidence is whether the learner can absorb new concepts while retaining older object structure rather than trading plasticity for collapse.

Mathematical object
Object-centric slots, primitive selection, and concept-similarity distillation.
Approach
Adds concept-compositional memory mechanisms to reduce catastrophic forgetting in foundation-model continual learners.
Themes
Continual learning; interpretability as intervention.
FAMILY 04

Causality and Uncertainty

BRCD

ICML 2026

The core concept is root-cause inference under graph uncertainty. In a microservice incident, many components can fail together, and correlation alone does not say where repair should start. The first-principles problem is intervention priority: which component is most likely to be upstream of the observed failure pattern given only partial causal structure and sparse incident data? BRCD uses a pre-failure CPDAG, samples compatible directed graphs, and ranks root-cause candidates under a Bayesian posterior. The value is that uncertainty is kept visible: the system does not pretend to know the true graph, but still produces an actionable distribution over causes.

Mathematical object
A pre-failure CPDAG and posterior over compatible DAGs and root-cause candidates.
Approach
Uses Bayesian inference and uniform DAG sampling to rank causes from sparse failure data.
Themes
Causal discovery; software intelligence; production RCA.

Local Covariate Selection

ICML 2026

The core concept is effect identification without global causal discovery. Many causal questions are local: the user wants the effect of one treatment on one outcome, not a complete map of every cause in the system. The first-principles problem is to find the covariates that block the wrong paths while leaving the target effect visible. Latent variables and missing pretreatment guarantees make this hard because a bad adjustment set can add bias instead of removing it. The paper searches for valid local adjustment information under weaker graph knowledge, so causal estimation becomes a question of what must be known nearby, not what must be solved everywhere.

Mathematical object
Valid adjustment sets under latent variables and local graph conditions.
Approach
Finds adjustment sets without requiring global causal discovery, pretreatment assumptions, or causal sufficiency.
Themes
Causality; theory unifying practical adjustment.

Structure Learning CI

ICML 2026

The core concept is reducing graph recovery to conditional-independence testing. A learned graph is only as reliable as the statistical tests that decide which variables are independent after conditioning on others. The first-principles problem is to identify the primitive that controls sample complexity: not the drawing of the graph, but the ability to tell when an edge is absent. The paper studies restricted graph families such as poly-forests and derives minimax rates for Bernoulli, Gaussian, and nonparametric settings. That makes structure learning readable as a testing problem with clear data requirements and clear limits on what sparse samples can prove.

Mathematical object
Conditional-independence tests and minimax structure-learning rates for poly-forests.
Approach
Derives optimal rates for Bernoulli, Gaussian, and nonparametric graphical-model settings.
Themes
Causality; theory and optimization.

Latent Hawkes Causal Discovery

ICLR 2026

The core concept is causal discovery when some event-generating subprocesses are hidden. In temporal point processes, one event can raise the chance of later events, but visible event streams may share an unobserved driver. The first-principles problem is separating direct influence from common hidden excitation. A causal edge should mean that changing one subprocess would change another's future intensity, not only that their timestamps correlate. The paper studies Hawkes processes with latent subprocesses and connects them to shrinking-interval discrete-time causal representations, giving conditions under which edges and hidden subprocess structure can still be identified from partial observation.

Mathematical object
Hawkes processes with latent subprocesses and shrinking-interval discrete-time causal representations.
Approach
Establishes identifiability conditions for edge and subprocess recovery under partial observation.
Themes
Scientific discovery; probabilistic inference; temporal causality.

Robust Contextual Optimization with Missing Covariates

ICML 2026

The core concept is decision robustness under incomplete context. A decision rule often needs covariates that are missing at deployment time: price, weather, patient detail, demand signal, or sensor state. Filling in a single guessed value can hide the fact that several worlds are still possible. The first-principles problem is to optimize while preserving uncertainty created by missingness. The paper builds distributionally robust ambiguity sets conditioned on the observed covariate subset, so the optimizer chooses decisions that remain defensible across compatible completions instead of pretending the completed dataset is known. The failure boundary is overconfidence caused by imputation.

Mathematical object
Distributionally robust ambiguity sets conditioned on observed covariate subsets.
Approach
Optimizes directly against uncertainty induced by missing covariates instead of completing the dataset first.
Themes
Robust decision-making; data quality and missingness-aware optimization.

Rare Event Analysis of LLMs

ICML 2026

The core concept is tail behavior as a measurable deployment risk. A harmful or surprising model behavior can be absent from small test sets and still occur often enough to matter when the system is used at scale. The first-principles problem is estimating a small probability with uncertainty, not collecting anecdotes after failures occur. The paper frames rare-event analysis as event definition, probability estimation, and structure exploration, using Monte Carlo, MCMC, transition paths, importance sampling, and error analysis. This gives evaluators a way to ask how often a bad behavior occurs, what paths lead to it, and how reliable the estimate is.

Mathematical object
Low-probability event estimation with Monte Carlo, MCMC, transition paths, and importance sampling.
Approach
Defines rare-event analysis as event setup, probability estimation, and structure exploration with error analysis.
Themes
Evaluation; robustness; deployment-scale risk.

Micro-Benchmarking Reliability

ICLR 2026

The core concept is ranking confidence under limited evaluation budget. Small benchmark subsets are tempting because they are cheap, but their value depends on whether they preserve the model comparisons a user will act on. The first-principles problem is pairwise decision reliability: how many examples are needed before saying model A beats model B is more than noise? The paper meta-evaluates small subsets and shows that close model pairs can require much larger sample sizes than casual micro-benchmarking assumes. The important output is not a single score, but uncertainty over rankings as a function of sample size and effect size.

Mathematical object
Pairwise model ranking reliability as a function of benchmark sample size.
Approach
Meta-evaluates small subsets and finds close model pairs often need around 250 examples.
Themes
Evaluation; measurement; sample-size limits.

DiReCT

ICML 2026

The core concept is data selection as curvature-aware control. Late in pretraining, examples do not only add information; their gradients push the model through a validation landscape with flat and stiff directions. The first-principles problem is to choose data by the movement it causes, not only by topic or source. A sample can help if it moves the model along useful flat directions and hurt if it injects energy into directions where validation loss is sensitive. DiReCT projects per-sample gradients against validation-Hessian eigendirections and selects annealing data under that geometry. Data becomes an intervention on training dynamics, not a passive corpus slice.

Mathematical object
Per-sample gradients projected against validation-Hessian eigendirections.
Approach
Selects annealing samples with constrained gradient energy in stiff directions.
Themes
Optimization dynamics; data governance; data as control.
FAMILY 05

Systems, Optimization, and Representation

Differentiable MPC on GPU

ICLR 2026

The core concept is making a classical control optimizer accelerator-native. Model predictive control is useful because it chooses actions by looking ahead through dynamics and constraints, but a slow solver cannot sit inside modern reinforcement learning or imitation loops. The first-principles problem is to keep the control object intact while changing the hardware regime: solve constrained trajectory problems quickly, expose gradients, and avoid turning the planner into an offline bottleneck. The paper uses sequential quadratic programs with custom preconditioned conjugate gradients and GPU parallelism, making MPC a differentiable layer that can be trained around rather than called as a separate slow tool.

Mathematical object
Sequential quadratic programs solved with custom preconditioned conjugate gradients.
Approach
Uses tridiagonal preconditioning and GPU parallelism to speed differentiable MPC for RL and imitation learning.
Themes
Robotics and control; systems infrastructure.

Optimal MoE Sparsity

ICLR 2026

The core concept is sparse scaling as compute allocation. A mixture-of-experts model can contain many parameters, but only a subset is active on each token. The first-principles problem is to choose sparsity so the model gets useful specialization without starving experts of data or reducing active computation too far. More total parameters are not automatically better if each parameter sees too few tokens, and dense computation is not automatically better if it wastes budget on irrelevant capacity. The paper studies active FLOPs and tokens per parameter under fixed compute, separating reasoning and memorization behavior as sparsity changes. The real object is useful computation, not headline parameter count.

Mathematical object
Active FLOPs and tokens per parameter under a fixed compute budget.
Approach
Analyzes reasoning and memorization performance as sparsity and training-token allocation vary.
Themes
Sparse computation; theory of MoE scaling.

Cost-aware FedOpt

ICLR 2026

The core concept is federated optimization with priced information. In federated learning, a client update is not only a gradient estimate; it also costs bandwidth, time, battery, or coordination. The first-principles problem is to decide which clients are worth querying when some provide similar information and some are expensive to contact. Treating all updates as equally priced can waste the system budget. The paper studies variance-reduced gradient estimators with explicit communication costs, comparing random, full, and hybrid strategies while using functional client similarity. The optimizer's object is no longer just descent direction; it is descent per unit communication cost.

Mathematical object
Variance-reduced gradient estimators with client communication costs.
Approach
Prices random, full, and hybrid communication strategies and improves estimators through functional client similarity.
Themes
Federated learning; theory and optimization.

SpineFL

ICML 2026

The core concept is heterogeneous federated architecture. Different clients may have different memory, compute, network quality, and data distributions, so forcing one full model onto every device can exclude weak clients or waste strong ones. The first-principles problem is to define what must be shared for learning to remain one system and what capacity can vary locally. SpineFL splits each layer into a mandatory shared spine and optional dynamic neurons. Historical activation frequency guides submodel selection, so the architecture adapts to device constraints while preserving enough shared representation for aggregation and enough diversity for client-specific capacity.

Mathematical object
A layer decomposition into shared backbone neurons and optional dynamic neurons.
Approach
Uses historical activation frequency to select submodels for heterogeneous device constraints while preserving diversity.
Themes
Federated learning; efficient adaptation; device heterogeneity.

Pi-net

ICLR 2026

The core concept is feasibility by construction. Some predictions are only useful if they satisfy constraints: resource limits, safety bounds, conservation laws, or convex decision sets. A model that predicts first and repairs later can fail when the repair changes the meaning of the output or breaks the gradient path used for training. The first-principles problem is to make feasibility part of the network's computation. Pi-net turns projection into a differentiable operator-splitting layer with implicit differentiation, so outputs are constrained while the surrounding model can still learn. The evidence is whether feasibility is maintained without making optimization too slow or brittle.

Mathematical object
Operator-splitting projection layers with implicit differentiation.
Approach
Enforces convex output constraints and uses feasible networks as fast constrained optimization proxies.
Themes
Theory and optimization; reinforcement learning; constrained planning.

GraphGlue

ICLR 2026

The core concept is graph-domain transfer as manifold gluing. Graph datasets can describe different domains with different local geometry: molecules, citations, users, roads, or biological interactions. A single shared Euclidean coordinate system may force unrelated neighborhoods to overlap or tear apart related structure. The first-principles problem is to connect domains while respecting their local frames. GraphGlue builds a glued Riemannian manifold with adaptive orthogonal frames and EMA prototypes, giving each domain local geometry while creating a smooth path for transfer. The proof signal is cross-domain graph performance without losing the relational structure that made each graph meaningful.

Mathematical object
A glued Riemannian manifold with adaptive orthogonal frames and EMA prototyping.
Approach
Integrates multi-domain graph data and improves cross-domain graph foundation model transfer.
Themes
Graph learning; representation geometry.

Temporal Superposition

ICLR 2026

The core concept is memory as feature packing. A recurrent network has a limited hidden state but may need to carry many temporal features forward. If every feature required a clean separate direction, memory would run out quickly. The first-principles problem is how features share representational space over time and when sharing becomes interference. The paper studies dense and sparse packing regimes, angular phase transitions, and the role of spectral radius in recurrent memory. It makes temporal memory visible as geometry: which features can coexist, which overwrite each other, and when a hidden state becomes too crowded to preserve the future-relevant signal.

Mathematical object
Dense and sparse RNN feature-packing regimes with angular phase transitions.
Approach
Links feature geometry and spectral radius to temporal interference and memory capacity.
Themes
Representation geometry; interpretability; recurrent memory.

Why Deep Jacobian Spectra Separate

ICML 2026

The core concept is depth-induced spectral organization. The Jacobian says how changes in parameters or inputs move the network's output, but in a deep model that movement is not spread evenly across all directions. The first-principles problem is to explain why some singular modes dominate while others shrink, and when those modes align enough to make training decomposable. The paper analyzes fixed-gates masked products and shows how depth can create separated singular values and singular-vector alignment. This matters because low-rank Jacobian structure changes optimization: the model may learn through a few strong directions before weaker directions become visible.

Mathematical object
Jacobian singular values and singular-vector alignment in fixed-gates masked products.
Approach
Analyzes spectral separation mechanisms that recover deep-linear-like decoupled dynamics.
Themes
Theory and optimization; theory unifies engineering practice.

Softmax Turing

ICLR 2026

The core concept is transformer computation as formal language machinery. A transformer can fit finite training lengths without truly implementing an algorithm that works at longer lengths. The first-principles problem is length-generalizable computation: what operations can softmax attention and chain-of-thought traces carry out when the input grows? The paper studies CoT C-RASP programs and transformer constructions, proving Turing-completeness under the right positional setup and showing that relative positional encoding extends universality to arbitrary languages. The practical reading is that positional representation is not bookkeeping; it can decide whether a model has an algorithm or only a length-specific pattern.

Mathematical object
CoT C-RASP programs and length-generalizable softmax transformer constructions.
Approach
Proves Turing-completeness and shows relative positional encoding extends universality to arbitrary languages.
Themes
Theory; sequence modeling; computation in transformers.

Language Generation in the Limit

ICML 2026

The core concept is separating formal computability from feasible learning. A generator can exist in principle while still requiring so much evidence that no realistic learner can recover it. The first-principles problem is the gap between possibility and sample cost. In formal-language generation, regular, context-free, and stricter classes can have clean mathematical descriptions, but learning the right generator from examples can be infeasible. The paper makes that distinction explicit, showing why an existence theorem is not the same as a practical recipe. The evaluation lesson is direct: a model may be theoretically capable under unlimited data while still failing under any usable training regime.

Mathematical object
Formal-language generation classes under computability and sample complexity constraints.
Approach
Shows regular, context-free, and stricter classes can be sample-infeasible despite computability.
Themes
Theory; evaluation; sequence generation feasibility.
BATCH 02

Data, Safety, Multimodal, and Theory Gaps

Common Corpus

ICML 2026

Common Corpus treats pretraining data as infrastructure. A corpus is not just fuel for a model; it determines what claims about reproduction, legality, provenance, filtering, and downstream quality can be checked. The concrete object is a documented training distribution with source constraints and mixture choices. The project assembles a very large public-domain and openly licensed text corpus, then studies how models behave when data is chosen under openness constraints rather than maximal scraping. The first-principles issue is comparability: model results are hard to interpret when the data-generating process is private, unstable, or legally unclear.

Mathematical object
A documented training distribution with provenance constraints and mixture weights.
Approach
Builds and evaluates an open corpus so data governance becomes measurable in downstream model behavior.
Themes
Data governance; reproducibility; open foundation-model infrastructure.

OpenThoughts

ICLR 2026

OpenThoughts treats reasoning traces as a public training artifact. Strong reasoning models are often improved through hidden teacher systems, private chains of thought, and unreleased data recipes. That makes it hard to know whether training teaches decomposition, search, checking, or only answer imitation. The concrete object is a supervised distribution over problems, intermediate reasoning traces, and final answers. The project releases open reasoning data and a training recipe so those effects can be inspected. The first-principles value is transparency of the learning signal: the path from problem to answer becomes something the community can test.

Mathematical object
A supervised distribution over problems, intermediate reasoning traces, and final answers.
Approach
Constructs open reasoning data and uses it to study how trace supervision changes downstream reasoning behavior.
Themes
Reasoning data; open science; post-training transparency.

Midtraining Bridges Pretraining and Posttraining

ICLR 2026

Midtraining Bridges Pretraining and Posttraining treats the middle of the training pipeline as its own learning problem. Pretraining gives a model broad statistical knowledge, while posttraining asks for instruction following, tool use, and preference-shaped behavior. Jumping directly between those regimes can ask the representation to change too abruptly. The concrete object is an intermediate data and objective distribution that reshapes the model before alignment-heavy training begins. The first-principles role of midtraining is preparation: change the model's internal habits enough that later posttraining is teaching behavior, not fighting the residue of generic next-token prediction.

Mathematical object
An intermediate training distribution that changes representation geometry before alignment objectives.
Approach
Studies curriculum, data mixture, and objective placement between pretraining and posttraining.
Themes
Training pipelines; data as control; foundation-model lifecycle.

BioX-Bridge

ICLR 2026

BioX-Bridge treats biological foundation modeling as translation across experimental views of the same system. Sequence, structure, perturbation, image, phenotype, and text annotation each reveal a different instrument's slice of biology. The concrete object is a shared latent representation over heterogeneous biological modalities. The model aligns those views so evidence from one assay can constrain prediction in another and support tasks that cross assay boundaries. The first-principles problem is cross-modal biological evidence: connect the views without pretending they are interchangeable, because each modality carries different limits, noise, and physical meaning.

Mathematical object
A shared latent representation over heterogeneous biological modalities.
Approach
Aligns biological inputs so sequence, structure, imaging, and annotation evidence can transfer across tasks.
Themes
Scientific foundation models; multimodal biology; representation interfaces.

MrRoPE

ICLR 2026

MrRoPE treats positional encoding as geometry, not bookkeeping. A Transformer needs position information so attention can reason about order, but long-context extrapolation fails when the learned coordinate system is stretched beyond the range where it behaves well. The concrete object is a rotary positional coordinate transform over attention features. The method changes that geometry so relative structure remains more stable across context scales. The first-principles problem is preserving order while changing length: the model should recognize the same relation between tokens even when inference sequences are longer than training sequences.

Mathematical object
A rotary positional coordinate transform over attention features.
Approach
Changes the positional geometry used by attention to improve length generalization and stability.
Themes
Long context; sequence geometry; efficient adaptation.

LiftQuant

ICLR 2026

LiftQuant treats quantization as error transport through the network, not as simple number replacement. Low-bit inference changes weights and activations, and each layer can amplify, rotate, or damp the local rounding error before later normalization and attention use it. The concrete object is layerwise quantization error and its propagation through the computation. Lifting and correction mechanisms target the places where damage concentrates. The first-principles problem is function preservation: reduce memory and bandwidth while keeping the compressed model close to the transformation the full-precision model would have computed.

Mathematical object
Layerwise quantization error and its propagation through network computation.
Approach
Uses targeted transformations to keep low-bit inference aligned with full-precision behavior.
Themes
Efficient inference; numerical systems; model compression.

SlaClip

ICLR 2026

SlaClip asks how much representation machinery is needed to keep image and text aligned. CLIP-style training learns a shared space by matching paired embeddings, but the full contrastive pipeline can be costly or brittle when moved to new settings. The concrete object is a contrastive embedding space relating image representations to text representations under a cheaper budget. The method changes how cross-modal information is selected, compressed, or aligned while preserving retrieval and recognition behavior. The first-principles problem is to keep the semantic matching function, not every expensive detail of the original alignment procedure.

Mathematical object
A contrastive embedding space relating image representations to text representations.
Approach
Reduces or restructures the alignment machinery while preserving cross-modal retrieval and recognition behavior.
Themes
Vision-language models; efficient adaptation; representation compression.

ETTFS

ICML 2026

ETTFS starts from a simple waste: a training example does not have the same value at every moment of training. Early on it may teach a basic pattern; later it may repeat what the model already knows or pull updates toward noise. The concrete object is the changing usefulness of each example as learning unfolds. The method turns training into a routing problem: give gradient steps to data that can still change the model in a useful direction, and spend less compute on data whose current signal is weak, redundant, or poorly timed.

Mathematical object
A time-varying example utility score inside the training loop.
Approach
Filters or schedules examples so compute follows current learning value instead of static dataset membership.
Themes
Training efficiency; data selection; optimization dynamics.

WAFT

ICLR 2026

WAFT treats fine-tuning as movement through the geometry of a pretrained model. Adaptation can improve a target task while pushing parameters into a region that forgets useful structure or becomes unstable. The concrete object is a fine-tuning update constrained by pretrained weight structure. Weight-aware adaptation shapes the update by what the base model already encodes rather than treating all directions as equally disposable. The first-principles problem is respectful change: add task-specific behavior while preserving the internal organization that made the pretrained model broadly useful.

Mathematical object
A fine-tuning update constrained by pretrained weight structure.
Approach
Modulates adaptation by weight geometry to reduce forgetting and preserve useful base-model behavior.
Themes
Efficient adaptation; continual learning; model stability.

FlashWorld

ICLR 2026

FlashWorld treats a world model as useful only if visual experience becomes cheap enough to reuse. For embodied or video agents, planning can fail because simulating enough frames costs too much, even when perception is accurate. The concrete object is a compressed transition model over visual states. The method accelerates dynamic visual modeling while preserving task-relevant scene evolution. The first-principles problem is affordable imagination: an agent needs a cheap way to ask what might happen next without spending all of its compute on raw pixels.

Mathematical object
A compressed transition model over visual states.
Approach
Accelerates dynamic visual modeling while preserving task-relevant scene evolution.
Themes
World models; embodied AI; efficient video reasoning.

Active Mind Avatars

ICLR 2026

Active Mind Avatars treats an embodied avatar as a closed perception-action loop. An avatar is not just an animated face for a language model; it must perceive the situation, keep internal state, decide, and act through a body or interface. The concrete object is a closed-loop policy over observations, latent state, and embodied actions. Perception, memory, planning, and motor output are tied into one interactive system. The first-principles problem is visible cognition: evaluate whether the agent's internal state actually drives behavior in the world, not only whether it speaks convincingly.

Mathematical object
A closed-loop policy over observations, latent state, and embodied actions.
Approach
Couples multimodal perception and agent policy into interactive avatar behavior.
Themes
Embodied agents; multimodal interaction; agent state.

MomaGraph

ICLR 2026

MomaGraph treats scene understanding as a graph of things and relations. In robotics and embodied tasks, the agent needs objects, affordances, spatial relations, and task constraints, not only a dense visual vector. The concrete object is a multimodal scene graph with nodes, edges, attributes, and task-relevant links. That representation lets downstream reasoning operate on entities and relationships that can support planning. The first-principles problem is preserving world state: if the representation hides which object is where and how it can be used, the agent may see the scene but fail to act in it.

Mathematical object
A multimodal scene graph with nodes, edges, attributes, and task-relevant relations.
Approach
Builds graph representations that expose object and relation structure for embodied decision-making.
Themes
Graph learning; embodied perception; structured world state.

BehaviorVLA

ICLR 2026

BehaviorVLA judges a robot model by behavior, not only by language or image recognition. A vision-language-action policy must connect what the camera shows, what the instruction means, and which motor command should happen next. The concrete object is a conditional policy from image and instruction history to action sequence. Behavior-level data makes grounding visible through what the robot actually does. The first-principles problem is that a model can describe a scene and parse a command yet still fail the task if those representations do not control useful embodied action.

Mathematical object
A conditional policy from image and instruction histories to action sequences.
Approach
Links visual-language grounding to robot action data and behavior-level evaluation.
Themes
Vision-language-action models; robotics; embodied evaluation.

HDFlow

ICLR 2026

HDFlow treats high-dimensional generation as an invertible transformation that must remain trainable and evaluable. Flow models are useful because they connect samples and likelihood through a tractable map, but structured high-dimensional data makes that map difficult to parameterize. The concrete object is an invertible transformation between a simple latent distribution and complex observations. The method designs flow structure or training constraints so density, sampling, and representation stay connected. The first-principles problem is control: generate rich outputs without losing the mathematical handle that makes a flow more than an unconstrained generator.

Mathematical object
An invertible map between a simple latent distribution and high-dimensional structured observations.
Approach
Builds flow architecture or training constraints for complex high-dimensional generation.
Themes
Generative modeling; dynamics; scientific or embodied structure.

Mind-Omni

ICLR 2026

Mind-Omni treats multimodal cognition as a shared reasoning interface across perception channels. A general model that receives text, images, audio, or other signals needs more than separate adapters attached to language; it needs a state where evidence from different forms can meet. The concrete object is a shared multimodal latent state with modality-specific encoders and cross-modal fusion. The system connects heterogeneous inputs to one reasoning and generation interface. The first-principles problem is evidence integration: preserve what each modality uniquely carries while allowing the model to combine them into one usable interpretation.

Mathematical object
A shared multimodal latent state with modality-specific encoders and cross-modal fusion.
Approach
Connects heterogeneous perceptual inputs to one reasoning and generation interface.
Themes
Multimodal foundation models; representation alignment; general perception.

Learning Biophysical Models for Neurostimulation

ICLR 2026

The core concept is scientific machine learning constrained by physical mechanism. Neurostimulation is not just prediction from patient records; an electrical input changes tissue and neural dynamics through biophysical laws. The first-principles problem is intervention modeling: learn from data while keeping the variables that make a stimulation choice meaningful. The approach builds a stimulation-response model tied to biophysical structure, so prediction can support design of new interventions rather than only fit old measurements. The evidence is whether the learned dynamics remain useful when stimulation parameters change, because clinical action depends on response under intervention.

Mathematical object
A dynamical biophysical response model conditioned on stimulation parameters.
Approach
Learns intervention-response dynamics with structure tied to neurostimulation physics.
Themes
Scientific ML; healthcare; dynamics and intervention.

IRNO

ICLR 2026

IRNO treats operator learning as learning a map between physical fields, not a table of grid outputs. In scientific computing, the reusable object is often the transformation from initial conditions, boundary conditions, or forcing terms to a solution field. The concrete object is an operator between function spaces. A neural operator should generalize across resolutions and physical configurations because it represents the transformation itself rather than one discretized instance. The first-principles problem is resolution independence: the model should learn the law-like map that produces fields, not memorize values attached to a particular mesh.

Mathematical object
An operator mapping input functions or fields to output solution fields.
Approach
Uses neural-operator structure to learn physical solution maps across conditions or discretizations.
Themes
Scientific machine learning; neural operators; physical dynamics.

Camera-Aware MLLM

ICLR 2026

Camera-Aware MLLM treats the camera as part of the visual evidence. A model may recognize objects while misunderstanding their scale, viewpoint, distortion, or spatial layout because the image-formation process is absent from its representation. The concrete object is a visual state conditioned on camera pose, intrinsics, or related geometry. Injecting camera-aware features lets multimodal reasoning respect how the scene was projected into pixels. The first-principles problem is perception with origin: pixels are not neutral facts; they are measurements produced by a camera, and spatial reasoning depends on that measurement process.

Mathematical object
A visual representation conditioned on camera pose, intrinsics, or image-formation geometry.
Approach
Adds camera-aware information to multimodal reasoning and evaluates spatial understanding under viewpoint variation.
Themes
Multimodal perception; geometry; embodied visual reasoning.

RALI

ICLR 2026

RALI treats language grounding as an alignment among words, state, and possible actions. In an interactive system, an instruction may be ambiguous, incomplete, or tied to an environment that changes while the agent acts. The concrete object is a latent alignment variable linking language, environment state, and actions. The method maps instructions into action-relevant representations and tests reference-following behavior. The first-principles problem is intended control: the agent must infer what the user means in a way that remains connected to observable state and allowed actions, not only to surface wording.

Mathematical object
A latent alignment variable linking language, environment state, and actions.
Approach
Maps instructions into grounded action-relevant representations and evaluates reference-following behavior.
Themes
Language grounding; agents; multimodal or interactive alignment.

SleepLM

ICLR 2026

SleepLM's core concept is physiological time series as a language-like sequence that still obeys medical structure. Sleep signals have stages, transitions, artifacts, and patient variation; treating them as generic tokens can erase the clinical meaning of state changes. The first-principles problem is sequence representation with domain constraints: capture temporal regularity while keeping sleep state interpretable. SleepLM adapts language-model machinery to sleep signals so learned representations can support staging, diagnosis, or patient-specific analysis. The evidence is whether the model improves medical sleep tasks without reducing physiology to pattern completion detached from clinical state.

Mathematical object
A temporal sequence representation over physiological sleep signals and latent sleep states.
Approach
Transfers sequence-modeling methods to sleep data with domain-aware evaluation.
Themes
Healthcare ML; time series; foundation models for physiology.

Veritas

ICLR 2026

Veritas treats truthfulness as a relation among a claim, the available evidence, and the answer a model gives. A response can sound careful while still making an unsupported statement, especially for rare, contested, or out-of-distribution questions. The concrete object is a verification function that judges whether a model's answer remains tied to facts and uncertainty rather than to fluent plausibility. The first-principles distinction is between confidence in language and correctness under evidence. Veritas belongs with evaluation and governance work because it asks what proof would make a claim acceptable.

Mathematical object
A factuality or verification function over claims, evidence, and model answers.
Approach
Evaluates truthfulness under conditions where style and confidence are insufficient proxies for correctness.
Themes
Safety; factuality; evaluation and governance.

Invisible Safety Threat

ICLR 2026

Invisible Safety Threat treats risk as something that may not appear in the final text. A response can look harmless while the prompt, intermediate steps, latent intent, or concealed trigger carries danger. The concrete object is a latent hazard variable weakly visible in prompts, traces, or intermediate actions. The benchmark constructs cases where surface filters miss the underlying threat and measures whether systems detect it anyway. The first-principles problem is early risk detection: safety systems must inspect context and process before harm becomes an obvious output violation.

Mathematical object
A latent hazard variable that may be weakly visible in prompts, traces, or intermediate actions.
Approach
Constructs safety cases where risk is concealed and measures whether systems detect the underlying threat.
Themes
AI safety; hidden failure modes; process-aware evaluation.

Trojan-Speak

ICLR 2026

Trojan-Speak studies backdoors whose trigger is ordinary language. That makes the safety problem harder than finding a rare token or malformed input, because the trigger lives in the same channel people use for normal instructions. The concrete object is a conditional behavior shift: under some phrase pattern, the model's output distribution changes in a hidden way. The paper treats natural-language trojans as learned rules over meaning, wording, and context. Detection has to ask whether a benign-looking phrase controls behavior, not merely whether the phrase looks suspicious by itself.

Mathematical object
A conditional behavior shift activated by a linguistic trigger.
Approach
Studies natural-language backdoors and evaluates whether detection methods find behavior changes tied to trigger phrases.
Themes
Security; model backdoors; language-model safety.

Pressure Reveals Character

ICLR 2026

Pressure Reveals Character treats stress as a way to reveal the policy a model actually follows. Ordinary prompts can hide problems because the situation is easy, the expected refusal is obvious, or no incentive conflict is present. The concrete object is a behavioral response distribution under increasing adversarial or social pressure. The benchmark changes pressure through authority, ambiguity, incentives, and conflict. The first-principles question is behavioral stability: does the model keep the same safety constraint when the situation becomes harder, or does it switch to opportunistic compliance, hidden preference following, or role-based drift?

Mathematical object
A behavioral response distribution under increasing adversarial or social pressure.
Approach
Evaluates model character by perturbing scenario pressure and observing policy changes.
Themes
Alignment evaluation; behavioral robustness; governance.

HATSolver

ICML 2026

HATSolver treats symbolic problem solving as search through valid actions, not free-form explanation. Mathematical and logical tasks require maintaining constraints, applying transformations, and reaching a proof or solution state where each step is allowed. The concrete object is a symbolic state space with permitted transformations and terminal targets. Learned guidance can help choose moves, but solver structure defines what counts as progress. The first-principles problem is navigation under rules: reasoning quality is measured by movement through a constrained space, not by how plausible the intermediate text sounds.

Mathematical object
A symbolic state space with valid transformation actions and terminal proof or solution states.
Approach
Combines learned guidance with solver-style search to produce valid reasoning trajectories.
Themes
Symbolic reasoning; agent planning; verification.

Difficult Examples Hurt Unsupervised Contrastive Learning

ICML 2026

Difficult Examples Hurt Unsupervised Contrastive Learning asks when hard training pairs stop helping and start lying. Contrastive learning builds supervision from a rule of thumb: bring some views together and push other samples apart. That rule is useful only when the pair labels match real meaning. Hard positives or hard negatives often sit near the boundary where the rule is most likely to be wrong. The paper's basic lesson is that difficulty is not the same as information. If the proxy label is mistaken, stronger pressure teaches the model the mistake more forcefully.

Mathematical object
A contrastive loss over positive and negative pair distributions with proxy-label noise.
Approach
Studies how hard examples change representation quality when unsupervised labels are imperfect.
Themes
Representation learning; data quality; contrastive objectives.

Base Models Know How to Reason

ICML 2026

Base Models Know How to Reason separates reasoning ability from the interface used to elicit it. A pretrained model may contain algorithmic or compositional patterns learned from raw data, but ordinary prompts may fail to call those patterns reliably. The concrete object is a latent capability distribution inside the base model before alignment tuning. Probes, interventions, prompts, or decoding procedures test whether reasoning behavior can be surfaced without adding the ability through post-training. The first-principles question is diagnostic: did the model lack the computation, or did the user-facing interface fail to activate it?

Mathematical object
A latent capability distribution inside the pretrained model before alignment tuning.
Approach
Tests whether reasoning emerges through elicitation methods without relying entirely on posttraining explanations.
Themes
Reasoning; pretraining representations; capability elicitation.

Beyond Log Likelihood

ICML 2026

Beyond Log Likelihood separates density fit from useful generation. A model can assign high probability to data while producing samples that fail structure, diversity, controllability, or downstream decision needs. The concrete object is the gap between a likelihood objective and the functional used to judge generated outputs. The paper studies cases where log likelihood misranks models and motivates complementary criteria. The first-principles issue is objective meaning: predicting average data well is not the same as producing an object that satisfies a purpose, constraint, or human-visible condition.

Mathematical object
A separation between density estimation objective and downstream sample-quality functional.
Approach
Analyzes failure cases where likelihood misranks models and introduces complementary criteria.
Themes
Evaluation; generative modeling; objective mismatch.

Transformer Circuits Can Realize Clustering Algorithms

ICML 2026

Transformer Circuits Can Realize Clustering Algorithms treats layers as implementable algorithms rather than opaque pattern matchers. Clustering has clear computational primitives: assign points, aggregate groups, update centers, and repeat. The concrete object is a transformer attention and MLP circuit corresponding to those update rules. By mapping clustering steps into realizable transformer computations, the paper gives a constructive account of what the architecture can do. The first-principles value is interpretability with mechanism: a circuit explanation should show how components carry out an algorithm, not only correlate activations with a behavior.

Mathematical object
Transformer attention and MLP circuits corresponding to clustering update rules.
Approach
Maps algorithmic clustering steps into realizable transformer computations.
Themes
Mechanistic interpretability; theory; representation learning.

Alignment-Sensitive Minimax Rates

ICML 2026

Alignment-Sensitive Minimax Rates treats statistical difficulty as shaped by how the target lines up with the data distribution. A worst-case rate over a broad function class can hide whether the relevant signal is easy to observe or poorly aligned with available directions. The concrete object is minimax risk with alignment-dependent complexity terms. The analysis separates information scarcity from misalignment of the target structure. The first-principles problem is sharper sample complexity: learning is hard not only because there is too little data, but because the useful direction may be weakly exposed by the observations.

Mathematical object
Minimax risk with alignment-dependent statistical complexity terms.
Approach
Refines estimation rates by tracking how target structure lines up with observed data directions.
Themes
Statistical theory; sample complexity; representation alignment.

Error Propagation in Quantized Diffusion Models

ICML 2026

Error Propagation in Quantized Diffusion Models treats generation as a chain where small numerical mistakes can accumulate. Quantization saves compute, but a diffusion sampler repeatedly feeds an imperfect intermediate state into the next denoising step. The concrete object is stepwise quantization error along a reverse diffusion Markov chain or ODE sampler. The analysis tracks when low-bit approximations remain bounded and when they change the generated distribution. The first-principles question is precision allocation: which stages or variables need more numerical care because their errors will be amplified downstream?

Mathematical object
Stepwise quantization error along a reverse diffusion Markov chain or ODE sampler.
Approach
Tracks error accumulation through denoising to guide precision allocation in compressed diffusion models.
Themes
Diffusion models; numerical analysis; efficient generation.

MF-GIA

ICLR 2026

MF-GIA treats graph attack as manipulation under model and feature constraints. Graph neural systems depend on relational structure, so small edge, node, or feature changes can propagate through message passing and alter many predictions. The concrete object is a perturbed graph with injected components under an attack budget. The method formulates attacks that reveal how adversarial changes move through graph representations. The first-principles problem is the adversary's control surface: know exactly what can be changed, what information the attacker has, and how those changes become prediction errors.

Mathematical object
A perturbed graph with injected nodes, edges, or features under an attack budget.
Approach
Constructs graph attacks and measures how message-passing representations amplify adversarial changes.
Themes
Graph learning; robustness; adversarial evaluation.

TACO

ICLR 2026

TACO treats tabular learning as reasoning over columns, rows, and their meanings, not as generic vector prediction. A table carries types, units, missingness, correlations, and task-specific column roles that disappear when cells are flattened. The concrete object is a table representation over rows, columns, metadata, and target variables. The method makes column semantics and dataset context part of the model. The first-principles problem is structured evidence: a row supports a decision because its fields relate to each other, not because the model saw a list of numbers.

Mathematical object
A table representation over rows, columns, column metadata, and target variables.
Approach
Models table structure directly so column relations and dataset context guide prediction.
Themes
Tabular foundation models; structured data; representation transfer.
BATCH 03

Safety, Evaluation, and Measurement

CounselBench

ICLR 2026

CounselBench treats mental-health evaluation as clinical judgment, not generic politeness. A counseling answer can sound warm and still be unsafe if it misses risk, gives false certainty, crosses professional boundaries, or fails to escalate when the user may be vulnerable. The concrete object is an answer span labeled by mental-health professionals for safety and quality. The benchmark uses adversarial open-ended questions to expose errors that broad helpfulness scores miss. The first-principles point is that safety depends on the role the model is allowed to play, the uncertainty it must preserve, and the harm a confident mistake can cause.

Mathematical object
Expert-labeled response spans with clinical safety and answer-quality dimensions.
Approach
Compares model and judge behavior against professional annotations on mental-health QA.
Themes
Healthcare safety; expert evaluation; judge reliability.

Gaia2

ICLR 2026

Gaia2 evaluates agents in worlds that keep changing while the agent works. A static question-answer benchmark waits for the model, but an agent environment has time, messages, external state, and actions that can become invalid if they happen too late or in the wrong order. The concrete object is an evolving environment state with verifier functions over individual write actions. The benchmark checks not only whether the final outcome is right, but whether each action was valid when taken. The first-principles gain is process evidence: verifiable rewards can train and judge the steps, not only the terminal result.

Mathematical object
A time-evolving environment state with verifier functions over individual write actions.
Approach
Builds dynamic scenarios and action verifiers for fine-grained agent training and evaluation.
Themes
Agent benchmarks; verifiable rewards; process diagnostics.

WebDevJudge

ICLR 2026

WebDevJudge treats the evaluator of a generated web app as something that must itself be tested. A web implementation is not only source text; it has rendered layout, interaction, responsiveness, and behavior that a text-only judge may miss. The concrete object is a pairwise or rubric judgment function over rendered web implementations. The benchmark compares text, visual, and agentic judges on static and interactive web tasks. The first-principles problem is judge validity: a confident natural-language verdict is not evidence unless the judge can inspect the properties that make the app work.

Mathematical object
A pairwise or rubric judgment function over rendered web implementations.
Approach
Benchmarks text, visual, and agentic judges against web-development comparison tasks.
Themes
LLM-as-judge reliability; web agents; evaluation methodology.

SGF

ICLR 2026

SGF looks at safety while a sample is still forming. In diffusion or flow generation, an unsafe image is not created all at once; the trajectory gradually commits to a region of the data space. Once that commitment is strong, late filtering or weak steering may be too little. The concrete object is a guided denoising path with an unsafe-region energy barrier. SGF recasts safe generation as energy-based guidance and studies when negative guidance should be strongest. The first-principles issue is timing: steer early enough to change direction, but not so hard that ordinary sample quality collapses.

Mathematical object
A guided denoising or flow trajectory with an unsafe-region energy barrier.
Approach
Schedules negative guidance during critical windows of generation to steer away from unsafe samples.
Themes
Generative safety; diffusion guidance; energy-based control.

CSPO

ICML 2026

CSPO treats safe reinforcement learning as recovery near a constraint boundary, not only as reducing violation counts. A policy can violate constraints rarely and still be unsafe if recovery is slow, unstable, or destroys reward. The concrete object is a constrained MDP with signed boundary distance and local constraint sensitivity. Policy corrections are scaled by distance to the boundary and by how sensitive the constraint is nearby. The first-principles problem is recoverable safety: judge whether the policy can return to the safe region quickly and usefully when it approaches or crosses the boundary.

Mathematical object
A constrained MDP with signed boundary distance and local constraint sensitivity.
Approach
Uses constraint-sensitive policy updates and recovery-focused safety metrics.
Themes
Safe RL; constraint optimization; evaluation beyond return.

DRPBench

ICML 2026

DRPBench treats code understanding as the ability to reason about interactions across concurrent executions. A program can look safe in a local snippet while shared memory, locks, and thread interleavings create a race elsewhere. The concrete object is a set of program paths, shared-memory accesses, and race predicates over concurrent executions. The benchmark uses verified concurrent-program examples to score static data-race prediction. The first-principles problem is semantic safety: a model understands this code only if it can track the execution conditions under which two accesses conflict.

Mathematical object
Program paths, shared-memory accesses, and race predicates over concurrent executions.
Approach
Benchmarks LLMs on static data-race prediction across verified concurrent-program examples.
Themes
Code evaluation; program semantics; software safety.

Copyright-Bench

ICML 2026

Copyright-Bench treats legal compliance as a workflow property, not only a rule the model can recite. An agent can know the law in abstract terms and still choose copyrighted material when the user pushes for speed, convenience, or commercial gain.
