A training recipe can win early because it optimizes quickly, yet still have a worse loss floor when compute is no longer the main constraint. The concrete object is a pretraining loss asymptote under compute-rich optimization. The comparison asks what remains after training is pushed toward its limit. The first-principles problem is separating speed from destination: budgeted performance measures how fast a method moves, while asymptotic loss measures where the data and objective allow it to end.

Mathematical object
A pretraining loss asymptote under compute-rich optimization.
Approach
Compares pretraining methods by irreducible asymptotic loss rather than fixed-budget wins.
Themes
Pretraining; compute scaling; asymptotic loss.

Grammar Substructure

ICLR 2026

Grammar Substructure treats language-modeling difficulty as something shaped by reusable source structure. Token count alone misses the fact that grammar pieces can be learned once and reused across many strings. The concrete object is a set of context-free grammar subgrammars and irreducible components contributing recursively to loss. The result shows loss can decompose linearly through that grammar structure. The first-principles problem is structured prediction cost: a model is not just memorizing a stream, it is learning reusable rules, and those rules change how scaling behaves.

Mathematical object
Context-free grammar subgrammars and irreducible components contributing recursively to loss.
Approach
Derives linear recursive loss structure over reusable grammar subcomponents.
Themes
Language modeling; grammar structure; compositional scaling.

Transformer Outputs

ICLR 2026

Transformer Outputs studies generation capacity as reachability under architecture. A model's possible outputs are shaped by data and decoding, but also by the structural constraints of attention, layers, width, and representation flow. The concrete object is the set of output sequences reachable from prompts under a given transformer architecture. The paper bounds that set using architectural characteristics. The first-principles question is what the model can express before any benchmark is run. Performance measures what happened on tasks; reachability asks which sequences the architecture could in principle make accessible.

Mathematical object
The set of output sequences reachable from prompts under transformer architectural constraints.
Approach
Bounds reachable output counts using architectural properties of the transformer.
Themes
Transformer expressivity; generation capacity; architecture limits.

Hallucination Rate-Distortion

ICLR 2026

Hallucination Rate-Distortion treats random factual hallucination as lossy storage under limited capacity. If a model cannot store or retrieve every sparse membership fact, some errors may be expected from compression rather than mysterious defects. The concrete object is a set of sparse facts encoded under a capacity constraint. Rate-distortion analysis describes which membership errors arise when factual storage is lossy. The first-principles problem is memory economics: hallucination can be analyzed as what a constrained system chooses to preserve, merge, or discard when exact fact retrieval is too expensive.

Mathematical object
Sparse membership facts encoded under limited-capacity lossy compression.
Approach
Uses rate-distortion analysis to characterize expected hallucination under constrained factual storage.
Themes
Hallucination theory; compression; factual memory limits.
BATCH 20

Efficiency and Systems as Capability Enablers

Why Low-Precision Transformer Training Fails

ICLR 2026

Why Low-Precision Transformer Training Fails treats numeric format as part of the training algorithm. BF16 is not only a smaller box for the same values; rounding can change attention probabilities and therefore change the update path. The concrete object is flash-attention softmax and value-product computation under BF16 rounding. The paper traces loss explosions to repeated pre-softmax maxima, probabilities rounded exactly to 1, and biased rounding accumulation in the attention value product. The first-principles contribution is a causal arithmetic path from precision choice to training failure, rather than a general warning that low precision is risky.

Mathematical object
Flash-attention softmax and value-product computation under BF16 rounding paths.
Approach
Tracks how repeated maxima and systematic rounding bias accumulate until the low-precision run diverges.
Themes
Efficiency; numerical ML systems; Transformer training stability.

Efficient Resource-Constrained Training of Transformers via Subspace Optimization

ICLR 2026

Efficient Resource-Constrained Training of Transformers via Subspace Optimization asks what must remain movable when memory is scarce. Full transformer training stores and updates too much state for many devices, but freezing almost everything can block useful adaptation. The concrete object is a smaller joint space of weights and activations where updates are allowed to move. The method trains inside that space so learning fits a resource budget while still touching behaviorally important directions. The first-principles boundary is simple: reduce trainable freedom only until the remaining directions can still express the needed change.

Mathematical object
A reduced weight-activation subspace used as the trainable update surface.
Approach
Optimizes Transformer training in a compact subspace to reduce memory and compute while preserving useful adaptation.
Themes
On-device training; efficient adaptation; resource-constrained optimization.

Solving Time-Dependent Differential Equations with Physical Dynamical Systems

ICML 2026

Solving Time-Dependent Differential Equations with Physical Dynamical Systems asks whether the solver can be moved into the physics of a device. Digital iteration can be too slow or energy-hungry when differential-equation solving sits inside control, optimization, or scientific search. The concrete object is a time-dependent equation solution represented by a continuous physical dynamical system. The method changes the substrate that performs the computation while preserving the equation-level target. The first-principles trade is not just a faster numerical trick; it is using a physical process whose own evolution performs part of the mathematical work.

Mathematical object
A time-dependent differential-equation solution represented by a continuous physical dynamical system.
Approach
Uses physical dynamics as the solver substrate while preserving the equation-level solution target.
Themes
Scientific computing; alternative compute substrates; efficient solvers.

Frozen-PINN

ICLR 2026

Frozen-PINN treats neural PDE solving as something that should reuse representation rather than retrain from scratch for every equation. Physics-informed neural networks preserve residual and boundary-condition evidence, but repeated optimization can be painfully slow. The concrete object is a PDE solution surrogate constrained by physical residual and boundary-condition checks. A frozen representation accelerates solving while keeping the PDE target visible. The first-principles problem is reusable physics computation: keep the equation constraints that make the solution meaningful while avoiding unnecessary relearning each time a related PDE is solved.

Mathematical object
A PDE solution surrogate constrained by physical residual and boundary-condition checks.
Approach
Uses a frozen representation to accelerate physics-informed solving while preserving the PDE evidence target.
Themes
Scientific computing; efficient PDE solvers; physics-informed learning.

RealUID

ICLR 2026

RealUID treats fast generative distillation as a promise to preserve real data, not only to imitate a teacher cheaply. A fast generator can learn teacher shortcuts that look plausible while drifting away from the data distribution people actually care about. The concrete object is a distilled generator constrained by both teacher behavior and real-data supervision. Real examples are brought into distillation without adversarial discriminator training. The first-principles problem is faithful compression: generation can be made cheaper only if the compressed process still respects the real distribution it is supposed to sample from.

Mathematical object
A distilled generator constrained by both teacher behavior and real-data supervision.
Approach
Adds real-data guidance to fast generator distillation without adversarial discriminator training.
Themes
Efficient generation; distillation; real-data distribution preservation.

FOCUS & RePAIR

ICML 2026

FOCUS & RePAIR treats compression damage as a change in generation dynamics that average scores may hide. Pruning can preserve perplexity and task accuracy while making the model more likely to enter or remain in repetition loops. The concrete object is repetition-loop behavior separated into loop entry and loop persistence after pruning. The method diagnoses those risks and repairs the damaged generation path. The first-principles problem is behavioral accounting: cheaper inference is not acceptable if it silently changes the token dynamics users experience, even when aggregate benchmarks look stable.

Mathematical object
Repetition-loop dynamics under model pruning, separated into entry and persistence behavior.
Approach
Diagnoses pruning-induced repetition failures and applies repair aimed at the damaged generation path.
Themes
Efficiency; generation reliability; compression failure modes.

TetraJet-v2

ICML 2026

TetraJet-v2 treats FP4 training as a stability problem, not simply proof that four bits can store numbers. Extreme quantization is useful only if the optimization trajectory still carries meaningful weight and activation information. The concrete object is a set of FP4 weight and activation trajectories during training. The paper identifies weight oscillation and persistent activation outliers as dominant failure modes. The first-principles problem is numerical survival: when the format is this small, training succeeds only if the update dynamics remain stable enough to learn rather than bounce between quantization artifacts.

Mathematical object
FP4 weight and activation trajectories during quantized model training.
Approach
Diagnoses oscillation and outlier mechanisms that destabilize four-bit training.
Themes
Quantized training; numerical stability; efficient model training.

EcoVLA

ICML 2026

EcoVLA treats pruning as a decision made inside a moving world, not as a one-time compression step on a frozen model. A robot policy sees objects, motion, language goals, and recent action consequences; deleting the wrong channels can remove evidence needed a few frames later. The concrete object is a channel-sparsity pattern that changes with the environment stream. The method uses temporal consistency from the physical scene to decide what computation can be skipped, keeping useful perception-action evidence while reducing the cost of vision-language-action inference.

Mathematical object
A time-varying VLA channel-sparsity pattern conditioned on physical environment consistency.
Approach
Adapts channel pruning at inference time using temporal evidence from the embodied environment.
Themes
Efficient embodied AI; VLA pruning; environment-aware computation.

Expressivity-Efficiency Tradeoffs for Hybrid Sequence Models

ICML 2026

Expressivity-Efficiency Tradeoffs for Hybrid Sequence Models asks where attention is actually needed. A cheap recurrent-style model may fail when a task requires long-range copying or association. A full attention model may solve the task but use more memory and compute than necessary. The concrete object is a hybrid architecture measured on selective-copying and associative-recall functions under resource limits. The paper combines Mamba-style components with attention to preserve the needed sequence behavior more cheaply. The first-principles lesson is that efficiency should be bought by removing unneeded expressivity, not by removing the operation the task requires.

Mathematical object
Hybrid sequence architectures measured by selective-copying and associative-recall capability under resource limits.
Approach
Combines Mamba-style components with attention to preserve specific long-range functions more cheaply.
Themes
Sequence modeling; architecture efficiency; expressivity under memory constraints.

SCOPE

ICML 2026

SCOPE splits long-video reasoning between cloud planning and edge evidence collection. A small edge system cannot inspect every frame deeply, but a larger cloud model can decide what observations would answer the question. The concrete object is a DAG of planned observations that guides edge retrieval. Semantic planning chooses what evidence to seek, and the edge system gathers it cheaply from long video. The first-principles problem is compute with evidence: reduce video processing cost without dropping the observations that make the answer justified, by separating planning from local retrieval.

Mathematical object
A DAG of planned observations that tells an edge system which video evidence to retrieve.
Approach
Uses cloud semantic planning to steer low-cost edge evidence collection for long-video reasoning.
Themes
Efficient multimodal reasoning; edge-cloud systems; video evidence routing.

CAT-Q

ICML 2026

CAT-Q treats quantization as controlled replacement of weight values, not blind rounding. A pretrained language model becomes cheaper if weights are ternary, but the reduced model is useful only if it preserves the computation stored in full precision. The concrete object is a ternary-weight approximation of a pretrained LLM with learnable modulation parameters. Softened ternarization and a small calibration set guide the replacement. The first-principles problem is economical preservation: compress the model by shrinking the value set while keeping the behavior those values were carrying.

Mathematical object
A ternary-weight approximation of a pretrained LLM with learnable modulation parameters.
Approach
Calibrates softened ternary weights from 512 examples to preserve model quality after post-training quantization.
Themes
Quantization; efficient deployment; low-bit LLM inference.

Flex-Forcing

ICML 2026

Flex-Forcing treats video generation as a schedule conditioned on device budget. A fixed chunk size or decoding order is brittle when memory, latency, and compute differ across deployment settings. The concrete object is a budget-conditioned generation path over global plans and local autoregressive chunks. The method adapts chunking to available resources while keeping bidirectional global planning tied to local visual synthesis. The first-principles problem is planning under capacity: the generator must preserve long-range coherence and frame quality while changing how much work each device can afford at each step.

Mathematical object
A budget-conditioned video generation schedule over global plans and local autoregressive chunks.
Approach
Changes chunking and synthesis order to fit device limits while preserving coherent generation.
Themes
Video generation; budget-adaptive inference; efficient multimodal systems.

ThreadWeaver

ICML 2026

ThreadWeaver asks which parts of a reasoning trace truly have to wait for earlier parts. A language model emits tokens in a line, but the work behind an answer may contain independent subproblems that could be prepared in parallel. The concrete object is a reasoning trace with dependencies: some steps require previous results, while others only need the original question or shared facts. The method trains for correctness and parallelizable structure on ordinary autoregressive engines. The first-principles point is that reasoning cost depends on how work is organized, not only on how many words are generated.

Mathematical object
A reasoning trace structured for parallel execution while preserving answer-relevant dependencies.
Approach
Optimizes reasoning behavior for both correctness and parallelizable execution on existing generation engines.
Themes
Reasoning efficiency; test-time compute; parallel execution structure.

MuonSSM

ICML 2026

MuonSSM treats state-space sequence modeling as a promise to keep linear-time serving while improving accuracy. SSMs are attractive because they avoid full attention cost, but cheap inference is not enough if long-context behavior becomes weak or brittle. The concrete object is a linear-time state-space update with parallel scan structure. The method improves training and robustness while preserving that efficient computation. The first-principles problem is memory under a serving constraint: change the model enough to carry useful long-range information without giving up the scan rule that makes it practical.

Mathematical object
A linear-time state-space sequence update with parallel scan structure.
Approach
Improves SSM training and robustness while preserving the efficient scan-based computation.
Themes
Sequence modeling; efficient long-context inference; SSM robustness.

SSMoE

ICML 2026

SSMoE deals with the failure mode where a sparse expert model stops using its experts as distinct capacity. If routing collapses, the system may still be called mixture-of-experts, but conditional computation no longer buys the intended division of work. The concrete object is expert routing and specialization patterns in a pretrained sparse MoE. The method performs post-hoc control to reduce collapse without retraining the full system. The first-principles question is whether sparse computation is still real: are tokens being sent to useful different processors, or has the model become sparse only in name?

Mathematical object
Expert routing and specialization patterns in a pretrained sparse MoE model.
Approach
Adjusts expert behavior post hoc to reduce collapse without retraining the full system.
Themes
Sparse computation; MoE reliability; efficient model repair.

SmartFed

ICML 2026

SmartFed's core concept is federated adaptation by recombining low-rank pieces already learned elsewhere. In federated LLM fine-tuning, clients cannot cheaply move full models or reveal all local data, yet they still need task-specific adaptation. The first-principles problem is choosing the transferable unit: instead of sending full weights, send small update components that can be reused. SmartFed treats LoRA ranks as experts and assembles them across clients, making adaptation a composition problem over low-rank parts. The evidence is lower communication and efficient personalization while preserving useful local specialization, not just a smaller parameter count.

Mathematical object
Rank-level LoRA components treated as reusable experts in federated fine-tuning.
Approach
Assembles existing low-rank modules across clients to reduce communication and adaptation cost.
Themes
Federated learning; efficient adaptation; low-rank model updates.

CLEAR

ICML 2026

CLEAR's core concept is parameter-efficient media editing that preserves the pretrained visual prior. Removing text from video is a localized editing task: the model should erase or replace written regions while keeping motion, background, and object appearance stable. The first-principles problem is controlled adaptation: change the behavior needed for one edit without moving the broad visual knowledge that made the pretrained model useful. CLEAR trains only a tiny parameter fraction, about 0.77 percent, so the edit enters through a small control surface. The evidence is text removal quality with preserved video content, not just fewer trainable weights.

Mathematical object
A small trainable parameter subset controlling video text removal while the visual prior stays mostly fixed.
Approach
Learns a parameter-efficient editing interface that changes text-removal behavior without overwriting broad visual structure.
Themes
Efficient adaptation; video editing; pretrained-prior preservation.

LiME

ICML 2026

LiME treats multimodal multitask adaptation as expert modulation over a shared lightweight base. A model facing many tasks does not need a full separate adapter for each one, but it does need some task-specific movement to avoid one-size-fits-all failure. The concrete object is a shared PEFT module modulated by expert vectors and routing choices. Zero-parameter routing selects cheap expert directions instead of training heavy modules. The first-principles problem is economical specialization: share the adaptation machinery while still letting the active direction change with the task.

Mathematical object
A shared PEFT module modulated by expert vectors and routing choices.
Approach
Keeps adaptation lightweight by routing through expert vectors instead of training separate heavy modules.
Themes
Multimodal adaptation; PEFT; modular efficient computation.

APB

ICML 2026

APB asks which part of a policy actually has to learn. A random shared backbone sounds useless if the backbone is assumed to contain the skill, but reinforcement learning may depend more on the adaptive interface that reads and reshapes that backbone's features. The concrete object is a policy with a fixed random core and lightweight trainable components around it. The paper reports standard reinforcement-learning performance and out-of-distribution gains from that setup. The first-principles lesson is that useful adaptation can live in the interface that controls behavior, not only in a pretrained representation.

Mathematical object
A reinforcement-learning policy with a shared random backbone and lightweight adaptive components.
Approach
Keeps the backbone fixed and random while adapting a smaller policy interface for task performance.
Themes
Efficient RL adaptation; policy interfaces; OOD generalization.

ECHO

ICML 2026

ECHO treats speculative decoding as a balance between proposing tokens and verifying them. A draft model can generate many candidates, but those candidates are useful only if the verifier can check and accept them quickly enough. The concrete object is a depth-width speculation budget constrained by verifier compute. ECHO chooses how much branching and lookahead to use around that bottleneck, improving wall-clock serving speed rather than only draft-model throughput. The first-principles lesson is that inference efficiency is a joint property of candidate generation, acceptance checking, and the cost of wasted proposals.

Mathematical object
A depth-width speculative decoding budget constrained by verifier compute.
Approach
Chooses speculative expansion to match the verifier bottleneck and improve wall-time serving speed.
Themes
LLM serving; speculative decoding; verification-aware efficiency.

GR-LoRA

ICML 2026

GR-LoRA's core concept is recycling gradient information that ordinary low-rank projection throws away. LoRA is cheap because it restricts adaptation to a small subspace, but the projection can discard task-specific movement that does not align cleanly with the chosen low-rank directions. The first-principles problem is preserving useful update signal while keeping the adaptation small. GR-LoRA saves the non-orthogonal gradient components and turns them into separate lightweight modules. The evidence is better incremental adaptation under the same efficiency pressure, showing that projection loss is recoverable information rather than unavoidable waste.

Mathematical object
Non-orthogonal gradient components discarded by low-rank projection during incremental LoRA adaptation.
Approach
Turns recycled gradient components into task-specific lightweight modules.
Themes
Efficient adaptation; LoRA; gradient reuse.

WLA/ERA5-Latent

ICML 2026

WLA/ERA5-Latent treats climate data as something that can be stored in the representation space where later weather models actually use it. Pixel-space fields are expensive to store and move, and they may carry detail that is not the useful substrate for prediction. The concrete object is a latent climate field that preserves downstream weather-prediction structure. ERA5-style data is processed in latent space to reduce storage and compute. The first-principles problem is scientific compression: keep the physical and predictive structure of the atmosphere while removing the burden of raw-grid storage.

Mathematical object
Latent climate fields that preserve downstream weather-prediction structure.
Approach
Stores and processes ERA5-style weather data in latent space instead of pixel space.
Themes
Scientific data systems; efficient climate modeling; latent representations.

Quantized Consistency Docking

ICML 2026

Quantized Consistency Docking makes molecular docking fast enough for repeated scientific search. A docking model that is accurate but slow cannot sit inside an agent loop that tests many protein-ligand hypotheses. The concrete object is a quantized conformation generator for docking complexes. Consistency-style generation and low-bit execution reduce the inner-loop cost while preserving useful conformational proposals. The first-principles problem is callable science: a model becomes part of discovery only when it is fast enough to be invoked many times without losing the structural signal that makes the result chemically meaningful.

Mathematical object
A fast quantized conformation generator for protein-ligand docking complexes.
Approach
Uses consistency-style generation and quantization to make docking calls cheap enough for repeated use.
Themes
Scientific generation; efficient docking; agent-callable models.

WBMM

ICML 2026

WBMM asks how to keep the benefit of a large-kernel vision operation while making the hardware see an efficient computation. The mathematical operator may be clear, but GPUs care about memory layout, batching, and tensor-core-friendly shapes. The concrete object is large-kernel depthwise convolution rewritten as windowed batched matrix multiplication. This preserves the receptive-field behavior while changing the execution form. The first-principles point is that the same model operation can have very different practical cost depending on its systems representation; deployment speed depends on the layout the hardware actually executes.

Mathematical object
Large-kernel depthwise convolution rewritten as windowed batched matrix multiplication.
Approach
Changes the computation layout to match hardware-efficient BMM while preserving receptive-field behavior.
Themes
Kernel design; efficient vision operators; hardware-aware ML systems.

WeDLM

ICML 2026

WeDLM treats parallel language-model inference as a deployment claim, not only an algorithmic claim. A decoding method is not useful because it has more parallel steps on paper; it has to beat a production-style autoregressive baseline under the same serving constraints. The concrete object is a parallel inference schedule evaluated against vLLM-served generation. The method changes the generation schedule while preserving output quality, with larger gains on low-entropy cases. The first-principles issue is fair comparison: speed means less wall-clock cost for the same useful behavior in the environment where the model will run.

Mathematical object
A parallel LLM inference schedule evaluated against a production-style autoregressive serving baseline.
Approach
Uses deployment-matched decoding changes to improve speed while preserving useful generation behavior.
Themes
Parallel LLM inference; serving efficiency; deployment-aware evaluation.

FeatJND

ICML 2026

FeatJND defines compression by what downstream vision tasks can notice. Some feature directions can be perturbed heavily without changing classification, detection, or segmentation, while small changes in other directions break the result. The concrete object is a per-feature perturbation tolerance map measured by task preservation. The method learns where distortion is harmless and where the representation must stay precise. The first-principles idea is that efficient features should not be compressed uniformly. The allowable error depends on the task's own decision boundary and the parts of the feature space that actually affect behavior.

Mathematical object
Per-feature perturbation tolerances measured by downstream visual-task preservation.
Approach
Learns where visual features can be perturbed without changing classification, detection, or segmentation outcomes.
Themes
Feature compression; visual representation robustness; task-aligned efficiency.

Flowers

ICML 2026

Flowers treats nonlocal physical interaction as something that should be selected, not computed densely by default. Many PDE-scale fields need information from faraway locations, but full global interaction can become too expensive as the field grows. The concrete object is a sparse set of source coordinates, one per warp head, used to approximate long-range influence. The method keeps global reach while making the cost linear. The first-principles question is which distant points must be consulted for the field update to remain physically meaningful, and which possible interactions can be skipped.

Mathematical object
Sparse warp-head source coordinates used to approximate nonlocal PDE field interactions.
Approach
Samples one source coordinate per warp head to preserve global interaction at linear cost.
Themes
Scientific computing; PDE models; sparse adaptive nonlocality.

SmoothSpike

ICML 2026

SmoothSpike's core concept is preventing spike-efficient Transformers from losing information through saturation. Spiking models can save energy by using sparse event-like activity, but saturated spikes can make different inputs look too similar. The first-principles problem is efficient representation preservation: keep the low-power spike computation while maintaining separable information for downstream tasks. SmoothSpike applies randomized or learnable orthogonal transforms to smooth spike activity and reduce homogenization. The evidence is better accuracy at spike-efficient inference, showing that efficiency is useful only when the sparse event code still carries the distinctions the model needs.

Mathematical object
Spike-Transformer activation patterns transformed to reduce saturation and information homogenization.
Approach
Applies orthogonal smoothing so spike-efficient inference keeps more useful representation structure.
Themes
Spiking Transformers; efficient inference; representation preservation.

Brain Encoding Scale

ICML 2026

Brain Encoding Scale treats compression damage as dependent on which evidence channel is measured. Quantization and pruning can hurt linguistic probes while leaving neural predictivity largely intact, so one benchmark number cannot say what survived. The concrete object is brain-response predictivity of compressed language-model representations. The study compares compressed models on neural alignment and linguistic degradation. The first-principles problem is representation evidence: to know what compression removed, test whether the model still predicts human brain responses and not only whether it answers text probes correctly.

Mathematical object
Brain-response predictivity of compressed language-model representations.
Approach
Compares quantized and pruned models on neural alignment versus linguistic probe degradation.
Themes
Compression evaluation; neuroscience and cognition; representation evidence.

FlashOptim

ICML 2026

FlashOptim treats optimizer state as a main memory cost of training, not a bookkeeping detail. AdamW stores auxiliary moments in addition to weights and gradients, and those states can dominate memory at large scale. The concrete object is AdamW state represented with bounded splitting and companded 8-bit storage. The method compresses this state while preserving enough update information for stable optimization. The first-principles problem is approximation of training memory: reduce bytes per parameter without changing the optimizer state so much that the learning trajectory becomes a different one.

Mathematical object
AdamW optimizer states represented with bounded splitting and companded 8-bit storage.
Approach
Compresses optimizer memory while preserving the update information needed for stable training.
Themes
Optimizer systems; memory-efficient training; low-bit state representation.

Lottery Prior

ICML 2026

Lottery Prior treats compression as a prior for restoration rather than only a way to save bits. A restoration model with too much freedom can explain corrupted input in many arbitrary ways, including ones that overfit noise. The concrete object is a rate-distortion constrained estimator whose compression limit narrows the solution space. Non-asymptotic bounds show when that limit improves restoration by regularizing the reconstruction. The first-principles question is what information should be allowed through: compression helps when it removes degrees of freedom that would otherwise fit corruption instead of signal.

Mathematical object
A rate-distortion constrained restoration estimator whose compression limit acts as a prior.
Approach
Proves bounds showing when compressed representations improve restoration through implicit regularization.
Themes
Rate-distortion; restoration; compression as regularization.

ME Ensemble

ICML 2026

ME Ensemble asks how to keep the distributional benefit of an ensemble without paying for every model at every token. Full ensembles can improve robustness because they mix different model beliefs, but simultaneous forward passes are too costly for many serving paths. The concrete object is a token-level mixture distribution over component language models. The method samples one component model per token, so generation follows a stochastic mixture process rather than a full stack of models. The first-principles trade is between belief diversity and compute: preserve enough mixture behavior while changing the execution path.

Mathematical object
A token-level mixture distribution over component LLMs.
Approach
Chooses one ensemble component per token to approximate mixture behavior without full ensemble compute.
Themes
Efficient ensembling; LLM inference; mixture distributions.

FedPissa

ICML 2026

FedPissa's core concept is avoiding redundant low-rank adaptation in federated PEFT. Federated fine-tuning must pay for local computation and communication, so duplicate LoRA structure wastes the scarce resource even if each client update is small. The first-principles problem is lean expressivity: keep enough low-rank movement for adaptation while removing adapter components that carry repeated information. FedPissa redesigns the federated update path to avoid dual-LoRA redundancy and reduce cost. The evidence is lower communication and computation, with adaptation utility preserved, so efficiency is measured against behavior rather than parameter count alone.

Mathematical object
A federated PEFT update path with redundant LoRA components removed.
Approach
Redesigns low-rank client updates to reduce communication and compute without losing adaptation utility.
Themes
Federated learning; PEFT efficiency; communication-aware adaptation.

Incremental BPE

ICML 2026

Incremental BPE treats tokenizer state as a streaming computation. Standard BPE is straightforward when the full string is available, but interactive systems receive bytes over time and still need exact prefix tokenization. The concrete object is the exact BPE state maintained for every streaming prefix. Incremental updates achieve worst-case logarithmic-squared work per byte while preserving the tokenizer's output. The first-principles problem is semantic invariance under execution change: the system may process text online, but the token sequence must remain the same one the batch tokenizer would have produced.

Mathematical object
Exact BPE tokenization state maintained over every streaming prefix.
Approach
Updates tokenization incrementally with worst-case O(log^2 t) work per byte.
Themes
Tokenizer systems; streaming inference; exact incremental computation.

ReQAT

ICML 2026

ReQAT asks whether reasoning survives the exact numerical format used at serving time. A low-bit model can still produce fluent text while losing the small distinctions needed for multi-step inference, especially when weights, activations, and KV cache are all quantized. The concrete object is a W4A4KV4 FP4 reasoning model, not a partially compressed proxy. Quantization-aware training exposes the model to those constraints while it learns, so the reasoning computation adapts to the representation it will actually use. The evidence is whether low-bit inference preserves or improves reasoning behavior relative to BF16.

Mathematical object
A W4A4KV4 FP4 quantized reasoning model with weights, activations, and KV cache all constrained.
Approach
Trains with quantization awareness so low-bit inference preserves or improves reasoning accuracy.
Themes
Reasoning quantization; efficient deployment; low-precision training.

MACKO-SpMV

ICML 2026

MACKO-SpMV asks when unstructured sparsity produces real speed instead of only fewer nonzero weights. Pruning half of an LLM is not useful if the sparse format and GPU kernel spend more time gathering data than dense inference would have spent computing it. The concrete object is unstructured sparse matrix-vector multiplication for pruned LLM inference. The method co-designs storage and kernel execution so the sparse operation matches hardware realities. The first-principles point is that compression is only operationally meaningful when the mathematical sparsity becomes lower wall-clock cost.

Mathematical object
Unstructured sparse matrix-vector multiplication for pruned LLM inference.
Approach
Co-designs sparse storage and GPU kernels to turn pruning into real wall-clock speedup.
Themes
Sparse inference; GPU kernels; practical LLM pruning.

EMP

ICML 2026

EMP asks how a pruning method should decide how much to remove. A fixed sparsity percentage ignores the fact that importance scores can be sharply concentrated in one layer and spread out in another. The concrete object is the distribution of importance scores summarized by effective sample size through the inverse Simpson index. When importance is concentrated, fewer components carry most of the evidence; when it is diffuse, aggressive pruning is riskier. EMP turns pruning into a measurement of concentration, so sparsity is adapted from the model's own evidence rather than imposed as a global compression target.

Mathematical object
Importance-score concentration summarized by effective sample size through the inverse Simpson index.
Approach
Uses concentration of importance scores to set adaptive sparsity levels for pruning.
Themes
Model pruning; adaptive sparsity; compression diagnostics.

FlashSketch

ICML 2026

FlashSketch's core concept is sketching that respects both the mathematical guarantee and the GPU execution path. A sparse random projection is useful only if it preserves the geometry needed by downstream linear algebra and runs fast enough to justify replacing the original matrix. The first-principles problem is co-design: change the sketch layout for CUDA without losing oblivious-subspace-embedding behavior. FlashSketch designs BlockPerm-SJLT sketches and kernels together, so the random projection is shaped by memory access and parallelism. The evidence is speed with preserved embedding guarantees, not speed gained by weakening the mathematical object.

Mathematical object
BlockPerm-SJLT sparse sketches with oblivious subspace embedding guarantees.
Approach
Designs sketch structure and CUDA kernels together to improve speed without losing OSE behavior.
Themes
Randomized linear algebra; GPU systems; sketching guarantees.

POET-X

ICML 2026

POET-X's core concept is memory-efficient training under an orthogonal-equivalence constraint. Some optimization paths try to preserve spectrum-related structure, but the tensors and state needed to enforce that property can be too large at LLM scale. The first-principles problem is constraint preservation under hardware limits: keep the intended geometry while making the training step fit in memory. POET-X scales spectrum-preserving orthogonal-equivalence training to billion-parameter pretraining on a single H100. The evidence is not only lower memory use; it is that the theoretical constraint remains active when the method becomes a usable system.

Mathematical object
An orthogonal-equivalence training path that preserves spectrum-related structure under memory limits.
Approach
Reduces memory enough to run spectrum-preserving billion-parameter pretraining on one H100.
Themes
Memory-efficient training; orthogonal constraints; LLM optimization systems.

WaterSIC

ICML 2026

WaterSIC's core concept is allocating quantization bits where a layer's input statistics say precision is worth most. A uniform bit budget wastes resolution on directions that carry little information and starves directions where quantization error changes the output. The first-principles problem is rate allocation: choose per-layer and per-direction precision so the low-bit model approaches the information-theoretic limit under a fixed memory budget. WaterSIC uses activation covariance and waterfilling-style allocation for linear-layer quantization. The evidence is better low-bit behavior because bit assignment follows measured signal structure, not a blanket rule applied across layers.

Mathematical object
Layerwise quantization bit rates allocated according to activation covariance.
Approach
Uses waterfilling-style rate allocation to approach the information-theoretic quantization limit.
Themes
Quantization theory; low-bit deployment; information-aware compression.

QAT Scaling

ICML 2026

QAT Scaling treats quantization error as something to forecast before paying for full training and deployment. Low-bit models are not damaged by bit width alone; error also depends on model size, training tokens, grouping, and how quantization-aware training changes the weights. The concrete object is quantization loss as a function of those resource variables. A scaling relationship predicts when lower precision is tolerable and when it will dominate quality. The first-principles problem is resource planning: choose bits, data, and model scale by expected error, not by treating compression as an afterthought.

Mathematical object
Quantization error as a function of model size, training tokens, and quantization group size.
Approach
Fits a scaling relationship that predicts how quantization damage changes with model and training resources.
Themes
Quantization; scaling laws; deployment planning.

CONTINUUM

ICML 2026

CONTINUUM separates the tensor view a model wants from the physical memory layout a server can actually maintain. LLM serving creates changing allocations, fragmented GPU memory, and workloads that do not fit a neat contiguous picture. The concrete object is a virtual contiguous tensor address space mapped onto dynamic physical memory. Driver-level mapping lets model code keep simple tensor assumptions while the system handles the scattered layout underneath. The first-principles point is that memory contiguity should be an interface supplied to computation, not a physical condition that every serving workload must satisfy.

Mathematical object
Virtual contiguous tensor address spaces mapped onto dynamic GPU memory layouts.
Approach
Uses driver-level mapping to preserve tensor abstractions for dynamic LLM serving workloads.
Themes
LLM systems; tensor memory; GPU virtualization.

FFOLayer

ICML 2026

FFOLayer's core concept is differentiable optimization without expensive implicit differentiation. Bilevel layers are useful because a model can contain an optimization problem as one of its components, but differentiating through that solver can dominate cost. The first-principles problem is preserving the trainable optimization layer while avoiding Hessian-heavy machinery. FFOLayer provides Hessian-free bilevel solver components as a reusable library, so the model can include constrained or nested optimization without making gradients impractical. The evidence is cheaper end-to-end training with solver behavior intact, making differentiable optimization a deployable layer rather than a research-only construction.

Mathematical object
A bilevel optimization layer with gradients computed without expensive implicit Hessian operations.
Approach
Implements Hessian-free solver components for differentiable optimization workflows.
Themes
Differentiable optimization; bilevel learning; efficient solver layers.

ThunderAgent

ICML 2026

ThunderAgent treats agent training throughput as a property of the whole runtime loop. Tool-using agents do not spend time only on language tokens; they wait on tools, prepare calls, reuse or discard caches, and generate rollouts for reinforcement learning. The concrete object is an agent serving and rollout pipeline with KV-cache reuse and asynchronous tool setup. By overlapping tool preparation with model execution, the system increases the rate at which useful trajectories are produced. The first-principles problem is that agent learning scales only when the environment, tools, cache, and model are optimized together.

Mathematical object
An agent serving and RL rollout pipeline with KV-cache reuse and asynchronous tool setup.
Approach
Overlaps tool preparation with model serving and coordinates cache reuse to increase rollout throughput.
Themes
Agent infrastructure; RL rollouts; serving efficiency.

STAR-KV

ICML 2026

STAR-KV's core concept is KV-cache compression by adaptive rank, not fixed deletion. Long-context inference becomes expensive because each layer and head accumulates memory, but not every cached block has the same rank or future value. The first-principles problem is memory reduction with attention preservation: shrink the cache while keeping the directions later tokens still need. STAR-KV uses differentiable soft-thresholding for attention-head and block-level rank selection, turning compression into learned low-rank preservation. The evidence is lower memory with stable long-context quality, showing that cache size should follow useful rank rather than a uniform budget.

Mathematical object
Layer, head, and block-level KV-cache matrices with adaptive low-rank thresholds.
Approach
Uses differentiable soft-thresholding to choose how much rank each cache region should keep.
Themes
Long-context inference; KV-cache compression; low-rank memory.

OPUS

ICML 2026

OPUS's core concept is online token utility scoring with sketches. Dynamic data selection only helps if token value can be estimated while training or serving is already moving; a perfect but expensive scoring pass would defeat the purpose. The first-principles problem is streaming evidence: keep enough information about which tokens are useful without storing or recomputing the full history. OPUS combines Ghost, CountSketch, and Boltzmann sampling to approximate token utility at low overhead. The evidence is better data selection under real cost constraints, making usefulness a maintained estimate rather than an offline label.

Mathematical object
Sketch-based online estimates of token utility for dynamic data selection.
Approach
Combines Ghost, CountSketch, and Boltzmann sampling to choose useful tokens cheaply.
Themes
Data selection; sketching; efficient training signals.

NorMuon

ICML 2026

NorMuon's core concept is optimizer updates that control both direction and neuron-scale balance. In LLM pretraining, a useful gradient direction can still be harmful if different neurons receive updates with poorly matched magnitudes or conditioning. The first-principles problem is not just where to move in parameter space, but how the update is shaped across rows, columns, and neurons. NorMuon keeps the orthogonalized movement of Muon-style optimization while adding neuron-wise second-moment normalization. The evidence is improved pretraining behavior when the update itself is treated as the main object: a direction with scale discipline, not a raw gradient step.

Mathematical object
Neuron-wise normalized, orthogonalized parameter updates for LLM pretraining.
Approach
Combines Muon update orthogonalization with per-neuron second-moment normalization.
Themes
Optimization dynamics; LLM pretraining; update geometry.

Excited Pfaffians

ICML 2026

Excited Pfaffians' core concept is reusing samples across nearby quantum or physical states. If every state overlap is estimated with a fresh Monte Carlo run, the cost grows with the number of states even when those states share much of the same probability mass. The first-principles problem is sample reuse: one draw should inform several related estimates whenever the importance weights remain stable. The method uses multi-state importance sampling so overlap estimates share samples with near-constant sample size. The evidence is reduced sampling cost without biased overlap estimates, making shared statistical support the object being engineered.

Mathematical object
Importance samples reused to estimate overlaps across multiple states.
Approach
Shares samples across state estimates instead of drawing independent samples for each overlap.
Themes
Scientific computing; importance sampling; multi-state estimation.

DHSA

ICML 2026

DHSA's core concept is sparse attention chosen online at two resolutions. A frozen LLM can run more cheaply if attention skips irrelevant chunks and tokens, but a fixed sparsity mask can delete the evidence needed by the current prompt. The first-principles problem is dependency-preserving reduction: spend attention only where the present input needs it. DHSA predicts chunk-level and token-level sparse attention online, making efficiency a hierarchical routing decision rather than a static mask. The evidence is lower attention cost while prompt-specific dependencies still reach the layers that need them.

Mathematical object
Dynamic chunk-level and token-level sparse attention masks over a frozen LLM backbone.
Approach
Predicts hierarchical sparsity online so attention compute follows current dependency structure.
Themes
Sparse attention; long-context efficiency; frozen-backbone inference.

MoE Compression

ICML 2026

MoE Compression's core concept is pruning experts by preserving attributed channel coverage rather than deleting whole experts. A mixture-of-experts model is modular, but an expert is still a coarse unit: it can contain useful channels beside redundant ones. The first-principles problem is compression at the right granularity: remove conditional computation without cutting away the channels that actually explain model behavior. The approach uses attribution to keep high-contribution channel coverage, making the compression unit smaller than an expert. The evidence is retained capability under pruning, showing that expert count is not the same as functional coverage.

Mathematical object
Attributed MoE channels whose coverage should be preserved under compression.
Approach
Prunes experts by retaining high-attribution channel coverage instead of dropping experts wholesale.
Themes
MoE compression; attribution-guided pruning; sparse modular computation.

TabSwift

ICML 2026

TabSwift begins with the structure of a table. A table is not just a long token sequence: rows are examples, columns are features, and prediction depends on how row evidence and feature interactions are organized. The concrete object is a row-wise attention state stabilized by gates and register tokens. The method makes tabular in-context learning cheaper by matching computation to the row structure rather than forcing a full general-purpose transformer pattern. The important constraint is that efficiency cannot discard the examples the prediction needs to compare, summarize, and reuse.

Mathematical object
A row-wise attention state over tabular examples, stabilized with gates and register tokens.
Approach
Reduces tabular ICL cost by using a lightweight backbone that keeps row evidence addressable.
Themes
Tabular learning; efficient in-context learning; structured data systems.

XDLM

ICML 2026

XDLM treats language-model design as a frontier among understanding, generation speed, and memory cost. A model can improve zero-shot understanding, reduce generation steps, or lower posterior memory pressure, but deployment needs the combination. The concrete object is a capability frontier over those three quantities. The method optimizes the tradeoff rather than treating any single surface as the whole goal. The first-principles problem is coupled efficiency: a cheaper model is useful only if the savings do not destroy the understanding and generation behavior that made the model worth serving.

Mathematical object
A capability frontier over zero-shot understanding, few-step generation, and posterior-memory cost.
Approach
Optimizes the model toward better understanding-generation tradeoffs with lower memory pressure.
Themes
Efficient language modeling; Pareto tradeoffs; memory-aware generation.

PoLar

ICML 2026

PoLar asks whether a shorter computation can sometimes beat the full forward pass. Efficiency methods often try to approximate the standard route, but the standard route is not always the best route for every input. The concrete object is an alternative layer-execution path through an LLM. Searching those paths finds cases where fewer executed layers preserve useful behavior or correct errors from the ordinary pass. The first-principles problem is adaptive computation: the question is not how to always run less, but which route through the model performs the answer-relevant transformation for this input.

Mathematical object
An alternative layer-execution path through an LLM, shorter than the standard forward pass.
Approach
Searches for shorter computations that preserve useful behavior and can correct some ordinary-pass mistakes.
Themes
Inference-time computation; efficient LLM execution; adaptive depth.

ConFlux

ICML 2026

ConFlux's core concept is shortening time-series attention by grouping channels into useful patches. Forecasting models waste attention when the time context is long but the strongest signals are channel-local or cross-channel in a compact pattern. The first-principles problem is dependency-preserving compression: reduce the sequence seen by attention while keeping the relationships that drive future values. ConFlux uses channel patching to shorten effective context and improve both zero-shot and fine-tuned forecasting. The evidence is better forecasting per unit of attention, showing that the right sequence for a model is often a structured summary, not the raw timeline.

Mathematical object
Channel-patched time-series attention states that preserve forecasting dependencies with shorter context.
Approach
Groups channel information so attention sees a smaller but more task-relevant sequence.
Themes
Time-series forecasting; attention efficiency; structured context compression.

Any-Order GPT

ICML 2026

Any-Order GPT's core concept is language generation without a fixed left-to-right commitment. Autoregressive decoding is easy to define, but it turns token order into a serial bottleneck even when many positions could be decided in parallel. The first-principles problem is order freedom: can a model refine unknown tokens in a flexible order while keeping language quality comparable? Any-Order GPT uses decoder-only masked diffusion with temperature annealing, making token positions mutable during inference. The evidence is large speedup at similar perplexity, showing that generation order is an algorithmic choice, not a law imposed by text itself.

Mathematical object
A decoder-only masked diffusion language process with arbitrary-order token refinement.
Approach
Uses temperature-annealed masked diffusion inference to reduce serial decoding cost.
Themes
Diffusion language models; inference speed; non-autoregressive generation.

LatentMAS

ICML 2026

LatentMAS's core concept is multi-agent communication through latent state instead of verbose text. Agent teams often pass natural-language messages that are useful for humans but wasteful when another model only needs the coordination content. The first-principles problem is communication compression: preserve the information needed for shared work while removing output-token overhead. LatentMAS moves inter-agent messages into latent representations, reducing output-token usage by roughly 70.8-83.7 percent and speeding multi-agent inference by about 4x. The evidence is preserved team performance under cheaper communication, showing that language is not always the right internal channel.

Mathematical object
Latent inter-agent messages that preserve coordination information without full text output.
Approach
Moves communication into latent representations to reduce token cost and speed agent-team inference.
Themes
Multi-agent systems; token-free communication; efficient agent inference.

WIRE

ICML 2026

WIRE's core concept is graph positional encoding that remains compatible with linear attention. Graph models need relational position, but many bias-based encodings break the attention approximations that make large graph processing efficient. The first-principles problem is interface compatibility: inject graph structure without destroying the computation path chosen for scale. WIRE encodes graph position through a route that avoids bias mechanisms incompatible with linear attention, preserving both relational signal and efficient attention. The evidence is stronger graph modeling under linear-attention constraints, showing that positional information must be designed for the operator that will carry it.

Mathematical object
Graph positional information represented without attention-bias terms that break linear attention.
Approach
Injects graph structure through a linear-attention-compatible encoding path.
Themes
Graph learning; linear attention; efficient relational modeling.

FFCC

ICML 2026

FFCC's core concept is replacing expensive activation functions with fast approximations after training. Activation kernels can be a serving bottleneck, but a faster nonlinear function is only useful if the model's learned behavior stays nearly the same. The first-principles problem is local substitution under functional preservation: speed up one operation without reopening the whole training process. FFCC provides drop-in activation approximations with large kernel gains and little accuracy loss. The evidence is end-to-end model stability after replacement, making post-training acceleration a controlled operation-level change rather than a new model design.

Mathematical object
Post-training activation-function approximations used as drop-in kernel replacements.
Approach
Substitutes faster activation kernels while measuring whether model behavior remains stable.
Themes
Kernel optimization; activation approximation; post-training inference speedups.

Relational Lottery Tickets

ICML 2026

Relational Lottery Tickets' core concept is sparse temporal graph computation that keeps relational expressivity. Temporal graph neural networks can be expensive, but naive sparsification may remove exactly the message-passing paths that let the model represent relations across time or across graphs. The first-principles problem is compression with an expressivity guarantee: reduce computation while preserving the class of relational functions the model can express. The approach reformulates TGNNs and cross-graph message passing as relational GNNs with sparse expressivity guarantees. The evidence is theorem-backed sparsity, where fewer edges or messages do not mean a weaker relational model.

Mathematical object
Sparse relational GNN structures preserving temporal and cross-graph message-passing expressivity.
Approach
Rewrites TGNN computation into a sparse RGNN form with inherited expressivity guarantees.
Themes
Graph learning; sparse computation; temporal relational expressivity.

IO-Aware GNNs

ICML 2026

IO-Aware GNNs focus on a cost that is easy to miss when graph algorithms are described only as message passing equations. The expensive step may not be multiplying features; it may be materializing edge-wise tensors and moving them through memory. The concrete object is the same graph computation counted by data movement, intermediate storage, and reuse. The paper redesigns execution around IO behavior, so scalability is not treated as an implementation footnote. It shows that a mathematically simple layer can be systemically wasteful unless the memory path is part of the algorithm.

Mathematical object
Graph message-passing computation measured by edge-wise intermediate materialization and memory traffic.
Approach
Redesigns GNN execution to avoid costly intermediate tensors and improve scaling.
Themes
Graph systems; IO-aware algorithms; scalable message passing.

EntroKV

ICML 2026

EntroKV treats the KV cache as stored evidence with different future value. Keeping every token wastes memory, but dropping the wrong token can break long-context reasoning. The concrete object is a layer-, head-, and task-specific retention budget guided by attention entropy. High or uncertain attention use suggests that a cached item may still matter; low-value items can be removed more safely. The first-principles question is what memory is still live for the next decisions. Cache compression becomes selective evidence retention, not a blind rule about age or position.

Mathematical object
Layer-, head-, and task-specific KV-cache retention budgets guided by attention entropy.
Approach
Allocates cache retention dynamically where attention entropy suggests information may still matter.
Themes
KV-cache compression; long-context inference; entropy-guided memory.

SECNet

ICML 2026

SECNet's core concept is event-stream feature extraction in the frequency domain. Event cameras produce sparse changes over time, so the signal is not a normal image sequence and can become expensive if processed as dense space-time blocks. The first-principles problem is compression without losing timing: keep the motion evidence that events carry while reducing multiply-accumulate growth. SECNet moves feature extraction into Fourier space, where repeated temporal and spatial patterns can be represented compactly. The evidence is whether event recognition keeps accuracy while computation drops, making the frequency representation the working object rather than an implementation trick.

Mathematical object
Frequency-domain features for spatiotemporal event streams.
Approach
Moves event feature extraction into Fourier space to reduce MAC growth while preserving temporal structure.
Themes
Event vision; efficient feature extraction; spatiotemporal compression.

Mamba-3

ICLR 2026

Mamba-3's core concept is judging sequence architectures at a fixed inference budget. A model with better asymptotic cost can still lose in practice if hardware utilization, memory movement, or quality tradeoffs erase the advantage. The first-principles problem is budgeted capability: given a real device and latency target, how much useful sequence modeling does each architecture buy? Mamba-3 treats subquadratic decoding as a measured frontier problem, not a slogan about complexity. The evidence is quality at matched inference cost, making deployment conditions part of the scientific object rather than a benchmark detail left outside the method.

Mathematical object
A quality frontier for sequence decoding under a fixed hardware inference budget.
Approach
Optimizes subquadratic sequence modeling around measured quality under deployment-relevant budget constraints.
Themes
Sequence models; hardware-aware inference; subquadratic decoding.

TileLang

ICLR 2026

TileLang's core concept is closing the gap between programmable fused kernels and high-performance GPU code. Kernel fusion can be fast, but hand-writing tuned kernels is brittle because tile sizes, memory layout, and parallel work division all interact with hardware. The first-principles problem is programmer-interface design under performance constraints: expose a shorter language while preserving low-level control. TileLang uses tile inference and recommendations to reduce kernel code size while improving speed. The evidence is faster fused kernels from less code, making tiling decisions the bridge between algorithm intent and GPU execution.

Mathematical object
Fused GPU kernels expressed through inferred and recommended tile structures.
Approach
Infers tile choices and recommends implementation structure to improve performance with less kernel code.
Themes
GPU kernels; ML systems; programmability-performance tradeoff.

DCFold

ICLR 2026

DCFold treats protein generation speed as part of the design method, not merely an engineering convenience. Binder design and structure search require many candidate evaluations, so a slow generator can make the scientific loop too expensive even when its samples are accurate. The concrete object is a consistency-model protein generator judged by structure prediction and binder-design utility. The method accelerates inference while checking that the generated structures remain useful for downstream biological tasks. The first-principles constraint is that speed only counts when the faster model still preserves the physical structure the design loop depends on.

Mathematical object
A consistency-model protein generator evaluated by structure prediction and binder design utility.
Approach
Uses consistency-style acceleration to reduce protein-design inference time while preserving task validity.
Themes
Protein generation; scientific design loops; efficient inference.

ThinKV

ICLR 2026

ThinKV treats the KV cache as reasoning memory with unequal value across tokens. A long generation stores many past states, but only some carry the evidence, plan, or intermediate thought needed for the next step. The concrete object is a set of cache entries with precision and eviction priority assigned by reasoning importance. Attention sparsity estimates which states deserve retention or higher precision. The first-principles problem is memory triage: shrink the cache without deleting the small set of past tokens that still control the answer, search path, or proof state.

Mathematical object
KV-cache entries with precision and eviction priority assigned by reasoning importance.
Approach
Uses attention sparsity to decide which reasoning-relevant cache states deserve higher precision or retention.
Themes
Reasoning memory; KV-cache compression; adaptive precision.

HyCa

ICLR 2026

HyCa caches diffusion-transformer features according to how each hidden dimension evolves. During generation, some features change quickly while others remain stable across denoising steps, so one global caching rule can waste work or reuse stale values. The concrete object is a dimension-wise hidden feature trajectory modeled by mixture-of-ODE behavior. The method assigns caching strategies per dimension based on local dynamics. The first-principles problem is reuse without distortion: computation can be skipped only where the feature is stable enough that reusing it preserves the denoising path rather than corrupting it.

Mathematical object
Dimension-wise hidden feature trajectories in diffusion Transformers, modeled by mixture-of-ODE behavior.
Approach
Chooses feature caching policies per dimension according to how that feature evolves during generation.
Themes
Diffusion Transformers; feature caching; generative inference efficiency.

Prophet

ICLR 2026

Prophet's core concept is shortening diffusion-language decoding without retraining the model. Diffusion language models refine tokens through repeated steps, but not every step carries equal new information; some parts of the path may be predictable from the current state. The first-principles problem is schedule compression: remove low-value refinement work while keeping the final text distribution close enough to the original process. Prophet reduces decoding steps on LLaDA-8B and Dream-7B through training-free step reduction. The evidence is speedup with preserved quality, making the denoising schedule itself the object being optimized.

Mathematical object
A diffusion-language refinement schedule with fewer denoising steps.
Approach
Skips or compresses refinement steps without training a new model while monitoring generation quality.
Themes
Diffusion language models; training-free acceleration; decoding schedules.

LPD

ICLR 2026

LPD's core concept is patch generation scheduled by dependency structure. Image and video patches are spatially and temporally related, so generating them in parallel can save time but also remove context needed for consistency. The first-principles problem is to decide which patches can be generated together without breaking dependencies. LPD treats patch scheduling as a graph-like problem: group patches to minimize within-group dependence while preserving the contextual support needed across groups. The method is useful when it reduces decoding latency without creating seams, object discontinuities, or inconsistent temporal motion. The evidence must include both speed and preservation of the visual relationships that patch independence would otherwise damage.

Mathematical object
Patch dependency groups for parallel generation with preserved contextual support.
Approach
Schedules patches by dependency structure so parallel groups do not erase needed context.
Themes
Generative scheduling; parallel decoding; dependency-aware inference.

LST

ICLR 2026

LST's core concept is balancing modality compute by aggregating long speech-token streams. Speech produces many more tokens than text, so a multimodal model can spend most of its budget on audio length rather than useful cross-modal reasoning. The first-principles problem is speech compression with alignment preservation: reduce sequence length while keeping timing, acoustic content, and text correspondence. LST aggregates speech tokens into latent patches and reports improved speech and text performance under compute-controlled training. The evidence is better multimodal performance per compute budget, making latent speech state the object to preserve, not every raw token.

Mathematical object
Aggregated latent speech-token patches aligned with text under a compute budget.
Approach
Compresses long speech-token sequences into latent patches to balance multimodal compute.
Themes
Speech-language modeling; multimodal efficiency; token aggregation.

MFP

ICLR 2026

MFP treats policy speed as a constraint on movement, not as a crude reduction of the action space. A faster policy is useful only if it still contains the trajectories needed to solve the task. The concrete object is an action path whose instantaneous velocity is bounded in a way that preserves expressive motion. By adding a boundary-condition-like velocity rule, the method reduces training and inference cost while keeping the policy able to make meaningful movements. It connects efficiency to the shape of allowable trajectories rather than to arbitrary model shrinking.

Mathematical object
A policy trajectory constrained by instantaneous velocity while preserving expressiveness.
Approach
Adds boundary-condition-like constraints that speed policy training and inference without collapsing action flexibility.
Themes
Action generation; policy efficiency; constrained movement.

FlashRNN

ICLR 2026

FlashRNN treats nonlinear recurrence as a numerical problem that can be solved more parallelly. RNNs are attractive because they carry compact state, but ordinary recurrence makes each step wait for the previous one. The concrete object is a nonlinear recurrent state equation solved through Newton iterations and custom reductions. The method preserves the recurrent relation while changing how the computation is executed on hardware. The first-principles problem is serial dependence: keep the state equation that gives recurrence its meaning, but solve it in a form that modern accelerators can process efficiently.

Mathematical object
A nonlinear recurrent state equation solved through Newton iterations and custom parallel reductions.
Approach
Reformulates RNN training as a parallel recurrence solve while preserving the recurrent state relation.
Themes
Sequence modeling; RNN systems; parallel training.

Equal-Resource MoE

ICLR 2026

Equal-Resource MoE asks whether sparse experts still win when the comparison is fair. A mixture-of-experts model can look better simply because it uses more total parameters, compute, or data than the dense baseline. The concrete object is a scaling comparison where those resources are held fixed while activation rate varies. The paper shows when conditional computation gives a real capability advantage under the same budget. The first-principles issue is resource accounting: sparse architecture should be credited only for useful routing and activation choices, not for quietly receiving more capacity than the model it is compared against.

Mathematical object
A sparse MoE scaling comparison with total parameters, compute, and data held fixed.
Approach
Varies activation rate under equal resources to identify when MoE sparsity genuinely improves capability.
Themes
Sparse scaling; MoE architecture; resource-fair comparison.

CoTAR

ICLR 2026

CoTAR begins with the shape of physiological time series. Long biosignal streams contain dependencies that matter medically, but full attention can spend too much memory and time to be practical. The concrete object is a linear-complexity representation that preserves the central structure of the signal. The method reduces cost by matching that structure instead of treating every timestep as equally expensive context. The first-principles question is what temporal information must remain for diagnosis or prediction to stay meaningful. Efficiency is valuable only if the compressed state still behaves like the physiological process being measured.

Mathematical object
A linear-complexity physiological time-series representation preserving centralized signal structure.
Approach
Matches the central structure of medical signals while reducing memory and inference complexity.
Themes
Healthcare time series; efficient sequence modeling; physiological representation.

MotionStream

ICLR 2026

MotionStream treats long video generation as a streaming memory problem. If every new frame keeps all prior attention state, generation slows down and eventually becomes impractical. If old state is discarded too aggressively, objects, camera motion, and scene dynamics drift. The concrete object is a bounded video-generation state maintained by sliding attention, attention sinks, self-rollout, and rolling KV cache. The method asks what must remain in memory for motion to stay coherent while runtime stays constant, turning long video generation into controlled state maintenance rather than unlimited context growth.

Mathematical object
A fixed-context video generation state maintained by sliding attention and rolling KV cache.
Approach
Combines attention sinks, self-rollout, and cache rolling for constant-speed long video generation.
Themes
Long-video generation; streaming inference; temporal memory compression.

PGM

ICLR 2026

PGM's core concept is clean-token sampling for faster masked generation. A masked generator spends inference work deciding which unknown tokens should be filled or revised, but some positions become sufficiently certain before the full schedule finishes. The first-principles problem is to stop paying for tokens that no longer need work while preserving the dependencies that still matter. PGM makes the selected clean-token set the efficiency object: the system changes the sampling schedule rather than the final task. The reported throughput gains matter only if the skipped or accepted tokens are truly stable, so the evidence must compare speed against output quality and failure cases where early token confidence is misleading.

Mathematical object
A masked-generation token set selected by clean-token sampling decisions.
Approach
Samples or refines only the tokens that still need work, reducing masked-generation steps.
Themes
Masked generation; decoding acceleration; token-level scheduling.

MetaEmbed

ICLR 2026

MetaEmbed's core concept is late-interaction retrieval with controllable granularity. A single vector can be too coarse for retrieval because different parts of a document may match different parts of a query, but many vectors raise storage and search cost. The first-principles problem is to choose the representation resolution at which evidence is still recoverable. MetaEmbed uses Matryoshka Multi-Vector Retrieval training so retrieval can operate with nested granularities: cheaper coarse vectors when enough, finer multi-vector interaction when the query needs detail. The useful object is not one embedding size, but a ladder of retrieval evidence with predictable cost and accuracy tradeoffs.

Mathematical object
Nested multi-vector retrieval representations with adjustable granularity.
Approach
Trains retrieval vectors so late interaction can operate at different granularities.
Themes
Retrieval; efficient embeddings; late interaction.

Layer Pruning Reassessment

ICLR 2026

Layer Pruning Reassessment asks whether simple final-layer removal can beat elaborate layer selection when repair is matched to the damage. Pruning methods often focus on which layers to remove, but the real question is whether the remaining network can recover useful behavior afterward. The concrete object is a pruned final-layer stack repaired by targeted fine-tuning. The study finds that this simple choice can outperform more complex heuristics. The first-principles problem is depth removal with recovery: compression should be judged by the repaired function, not by the cleverness of the pruning rule.

Mathematical object
A pruned final-layer stack repaired by targeted fine-tuning.
Approach
Uses simple final-layer removal and task-focused repair instead of complex layer-choice heuristics.
Themes
Model pruning; efficient fine-tuning; depth compression.

TiTok

ICLR 2026

TiTok asks what exactly a LoRA adapter has learned that can survive a move to another backbone. An adapter is not a free-standing skill; it stores task-specific movement relative to the base model it was trained on. The concrete object is token-level contrastive excess between the source base and its LoRA-adapted version. By extracting that excess, the method tries to transplant the adapter-specific signal rather than copying all parameters blindly. The first-principles issue is portability: preserve the change that represents the new skill while separating it from coordinates that only made sense in the original model.

Mathematical object
Token-level contrastive excess between a source base model and its LoRA-adapted version.
Approach
Extracts and transplants the adapter-specific signal so PEFT knowledge transfers across model backbones.
Themes
PEFT transfer; efficient adaptation; adapter portability.
BATCH 21

Multimodal and Embodied Grounding

LIMSSR

ICML 2026

LIMSSR treats action-quality assessment as reasoning from incomplete multimodal evidence. Real evaluations may lack aligned views, sensors, or labels, so pretending the full record exists gives false confidence. The concrete object is a conditional sequence-to-score map over incomplete multimodal action observations. LLM-driven reasoning and mask-aware aggregation extract cross-modal patterns while marking what is missing from the observed record.
