The first-principles problem is compression with structural preservation: keep the evidence that defines communities while discarding redundancy. CoCo combines local and global graph views so compact embeddings retain cluster information instead of becoming a low-rank shortcut. The evidence is better clustering from smaller representations, showing that useful compression must preserve both close relationships and broad graph organization.

Mathematical object
A compact graph representation that preserves local neighborhoods, global separation, and community consistency.
Approach
Uses local/global view alignment and denoising to remove redundancy while keeping clustering structure.
Themes
Graph representation; clustering geometry; compression without erasure.

GNN Exchangeability

ICLR 2026

GNN Exchangeability's core concept is that graph similarity should not depend on arbitrary node coordinates or ordering accidents. If an embedding comparison changes meaning when equivalent graph elements are permuted, the retrieval system is partly matching labels in the representation rather than graph structure. The first-principles problem is invariant efficient search: preserve exchangeable graph identity while still using fast similarity machinery. The method approximates transportation graph similarities with Euclidean order-statistic similarities, giving locality-sensitive hashing a compatible geometry. The evidence is retrieval that remains efficient while respecting the symmetries that make two graph descriptions represent the same object.

Mathematical object
Graph embeddings compared through order-statistic similarities that approximate transportation distances.
Approach
Maps exchangeable graph similarity into Euclidean structure suitable for efficient LSH retrieval.
Themes
Graph retrieval; exchangeability; invariant embedding geometry.

HyperDepth

ICML 2026

HyperDepth's core concept is preventing contrastive learning from flattening hierarchy in higher-order relational data. Hypergraphs express relations among groups, not just pairs, so their embeddings must carry both local discrimination and semantic depth. A uniformity-heavy contrastive objective can push everything apart evenly and erase which concepts sit above, below, or inside others. The first-principles problem is preserving hierarchy while still separating nearby alternatives. HyperDepth uses adaptive spectral gating and prototype-tree alignment to keep global depth visible in the representation. The evidence is whether embeddings remain useful for local tasks without losing the tree-like structure that explains the data.

Mathematical object
A hypergraph embedding space balancing local uniformity against global prototype-tree hierarchy.
Approach
Uses spectral gating and hierarchy alignment to repair semantic flattening in hypergraph contrastive learning.
Themes
Hypergraph representation; hierarchy preservation; contrastive geometry.

Shared Semantics Divergent Mechanisms

ICML 2026

Shared Semantics Divergent Mechanisms separates what an output means from how the model produced it. Two continuations can be semantically similar while relying on different internal mechanisms, and two mechanistic clusters can produce outputs that serve the same function. The concrete object is a continuation cluster balancing semantic coherence, attribution consistency, and compression granularity. A rate-distortion tradeoff finds groups useful for interpretation and intervention. The first-principles problem is choosing the right unit: behavior should be grouped where meaning and mechanism are both visible enough to act on.

Mathematical object
Continuation clusters balancing semantic similarity, attribution-mechanism consistency, and compression granularity.
Approach
Applies rate-distortion style clustering to expose modes with shared meaning but divergent mechanisms.
Themes
Mechanistic interpretability; behavior clustering; semantic-mechanistic alignment.

HELIX

ICML 2026

HELIX treats missing time-series channels as named variables with meaning, not anonymous blanks. In clinical and scientific records, each feature can correspond to a physiological or physical quantity whose identity changes how missingness should be handled. The concrete object is a time-series representation with learned feature identities and cross-dimensional dependencies. Cross-dimensional synthesis lets imputation use latent semantic and physical relations across channels. The first-principles problem is identity preservation: imputing a missing value requires knowing what variable is missing and how that variable relates to the others, not only filling an empty slot.

Mathematical object
A time-series representation with learned feature identities and cross-dimensional dependency structure.
Approach
Anchors each channel with a learnable identity and synthesizes dependencies across dimensions for imputation.
Themes
Time-series representation; feature identity; structured imputation.

Real-World Unsupervised Models

ICML 2026

Real-World Unsupervised Models asks what unsupervised learning gains from real sensory life. A model trained on tidy or synthetic data may learn useful features, but it misses the statistics that living systems actually receive: clutter, continuity, language use, infant visual experience, and uneven exposure. The concrete object is a representation learned from natural streams and tested against brain responses. The paper uses auditory and visual cortical prediction as evidence that the representation carries transferable structure. The first-principles claim is that the training environment shapes the geometry of what the model can later recognize.

Mathematical object
Unsupervised sensory representations evaluated by transfer to cortical response prediction under naturalistic shifts.
Approach
Uses real-world sensory training and out-of-distribution brain-response prediction as evidence of learned structure.
Themes
Self-supervised representation; brain alignment; natural data distribution.

Top-W

ICML 2026

Top-W asks decoding to respect geometry in token space, not only probability rank. A truncation rule can keep likely tokens while producing a retained set that is semantically narrow, scattered, or poorly shaped for the next step. The concrete object is a candidate token set optimized over probability mass, entropy, and embedding-space geometry. Wasserstein-style structure helps derive efficient crops of the output distribution. The first-principles idea is that sampling choices define what meanings remain reachable; the candidate set should preserve both likelihood and useful semantic spread.

Mathematical object
A token candidate set optimized over retained mass, entropy, and embedding-space semantic geometry.
Approach
Uses Wasserstein token geometry to derive efficient truncation sets for inference-time decoding.
Themes
Decoding geometry; inference-time control; token-space representation.

FacRNN

ICML 2026

FacRNN asks how a low-rank recurrent model can remain interpretable while still explaining neural population dynamics. Compressing activity into a small latent state is useful, but the dimensions can mix unrelated dynamical roles until the model becomes another opaque embedding. The concrete object is a low-rank recurrent latent model with group-wise partial-correlation structure. By adding penalties inside a VAE lrRNN, the method encourages separable connectivity factors. The first-principles goal is to keep enough dynamical expressivity to model neural activity while making the latent groups distinct enough to explain what each part controls.

Mathematical object
A low-rank recurrent latent dynamics model with group-wise partial-correlation structure.
Approach
Adds partial-correlation penalties inside a VAE lrRNN to disentangle interpretable dynamical factors.
Themes
Neural dynamics; low-rank interpretability; latent disentanglement.

ENGNN

ICML 2026

ENGNN separates two roles of noise in graph learning. Random node noise can give identical-looking nodes different labels long enough for message passing to distinguish graph structures it would otherwise merge. But the actual numeric noise coordinates are arbitrary, so a model that memorizes them has learned the wrong thing. The concrete object is a noisy graph representation considered up to transformations of that noise. ENGNN keeps the extra expressive power while enforcing equivariance, so predictions can use symmetry-breaking information without treating the sampled coordinates as part of the graph's meaning.

Mathematical object
A graph representation augmented with nodewise noise but equivariant to noise-coordinate transformations.
Approach
Uses noise to break indistinguishability while enforcing transformation equivariance so coordinates remain nonsemantic.
Themes
Graph expressivity; equivariance; coordinate quotienting.

KL-Minimal Visual MI

ICML 2026

KL-Minimal Visual MI treats visual explanation as a constrained information problem. A feature visualization can be faithful but unnatural, or natural but driven by a prior that adds structure unrelated to the feature. The concrete object is a posterior over natural images constrained by feature activation and minimal visual information. Energy-guided diffusion posterior sampling balances image naturalness against activation faithfulness. The first-principles question is what visual evidence is necessary: show enough structure to explain the feature, but not extra detail that makes the explanation look convincing for the wrong reason.

Mathematical object
A posterior over natural images constrained by feature activation and KL-minimal visual information.
Approach
Uses energy-guided diffusion sampling to trade off natural image prior and activation faithfulness.
Themes
Visual interpretability; feature visualization; naturalness-faithfulness tradeoff.
BATCH 39

Reward Evidence, Policy Search, and Closed-Loop Credit

MaxRL

ICML 2026

MaxRL asks how to learn from a final yes-or-no outcome. A binary success signal is easy to define but gives no direct credit to the earlier choices that made success likely. The concrete object is a rollout distribution conditioned on terminal correctness. MaxRL reframes reinforcement learning from terminal feedback as maximum-likelihood estimation over successful trajectories. Instead of treating the final reward as a brittle scalar pushed backward through the whole episode, it asks the policy to increase the probability of complete rollouts that end correctly. The first-principles gain is turning sparse outcome evidence into a trajectory-level learning signal.

Mathematical object
A rollout distribution conditioned on binary terminal correctness.
Approach
Maximizes likelihood of correct trajectories, converting terminal success into a trajectory-level learning signal.
Themes
Sparse rewards; trajectory evidence; likelihood view of RL.

SOAR

ICML 2026

SOAR builds a curriculum when the original reasoning task gives almost no successes. In sparse binary-reward environments, a learner may see only failure, leaving ordinary reinforcement learning with no useful gradient of progress. The concrete object is a teacher-generated curriculum over tasks just beyond the student's current ability. Asymmetric teacher-student meta-RL creates reachable challenges while preserving the final target. The first-principles problem is making progress measurable: the learner needs intermediate problems that are close enough to solve, hard enough to teach, and connected enough to the original task to matter.

Mathematical object
A teacher-generated curriculum over reasoning tasks with sparse success feedback.
Approach
Uses asymmetric self-play so one policy generates learnable challenges while another policy learns to solve them.
Themes
Curriculum learning; sparse reward recovery; self-play for reasoning.

VOTP

ICML 2026

VOTP asks how a few human preference labels can teach from many unlabeled videos. The key assumption is that a video foundation model already gives trajectories a useful geometry: similar behavior lands nearby, unrelated behavior does not. The concrete object is a trajectory embedding space where sparse preference labels can be transported to nearby unlabeled rollouts. The method uses optimal transport to turn distance into a controlled pseudo-labeling rule. The first-principles constraint is not to invent rewards freely, but to move preference evidence only where the representation gives a reason to share it.

Mathematical object
A trajectory embedding space where sparse preference labels can be transported to similar unlabeled rollouts.
Approach
Uses optimal transport over video foundation model features to produce pseudo-labels for preference RL.
Themes
Preference propagation; trajectory geometry; label-efficient RL.

Posterior Behavioral Cloning

ICML 2026

Posterior Behavioral Cloning keeps demonstration uncertainty instead of collapsing imitation into one averaged policy. A demonstrator may choose several valid actions, and a cloned model that learns only the mean can leave later reinforcement learning with poor action support. The concrete object is a posterior distribution over demonstrator policies and action choices. Pretraining preserves that action coverage for finetuning. The first-principles problem is support preservation: demonstrations should teach the range of plausible behavior available from the data, not narrow the policy so much that later exploration has no useful alternatives.

Mathematical object
A posterior distribution over demonstrator policies and action choices.
Approach
Pretrains from demonstrations while preserving posterior action coverage for later RL finetuning.
Themes
Behavior cloning; action support; pretraining for exploration.

Role of Computation in RL

ICML 2026

Role of Computation in RL treats decision-time compute as part of the policy. A policy is often described by its learned parameters, but two agents with the same parameters can differ if one is allowed to search, simulate, reason, or refine longer before acting. The concrete object is a policy class indexed by both stored weights and available computation. The paper formalizes how task coverage can expand as compute increases. The first-principles distinction is between knowledge stored in the policy and knowledge made usable by computation, making inference-time budget a capability variable rather than an implementation detail.

Mathematical object
A policy class indexed by both fixed parameters and available decision-time computation.
Approach
Formalizes how additional computation lets a fixed-parameter policy solve more tasks.
Themes
Compute-bounded control; test-time scaling; policy capability.

Nevo-CRL

ICML 2026

Nevo-CRL treats continual reinforcement learning as controlled activation of shared policy parts. New tasks can overwrite old skills if all weights keep moving, but freezing everything prevents adaptation. The concrete object is a task-specific activation mask over a fixed policy network. Evolving those masks lets each task select and recombine reusable substructures without destructive updates to the whole policy. The first-principles problem is controlled plasticity: a continual agent needs parts that can change for the current task and parts that remain stable enough to preserve earlier behavior.

Mathematical object
Task-specific activation masks over a shared policy network.
Approach
Evolves masks that route computation through reusable policy components for new tasks.
Themes
Continual RL; skill reuse; forgetting control.

Faire

ICML 2026

Faire treats generated visual artifacts as evidence that must support later reasoning. In geometry, a plot can be present yet decorative, misleading, or disconnected from the conclusion. The concrete object is an interleaved reasoning trajectory whose generated visual artifacts must support later inference steps. Reinforcement-learning constraints reward plots when they functionally help the geometric reasoning process. The first-principles problem is artifact responsibility: if a model draws a figure while solving a problem, that figure should carry information used by the reasoning, not merely make the trace look more convincing.

Mathematical object
An interleaved reasoning trajectory whose generated visual artifacts must support later inference steps.
Approach
Applies RL constraints that reward plots when they functionally help the geometric reasoning process.
Themes
Process supervision; artifact grounding; multimodal reasoning RL.

NonZero

ICML 2026

NonZero makes multi-agent tree search spend computation where agents actually affect one another. A joint action space grows as a Cartesian product, but many combinations differ in ways that do not change strategic outcome. The concrete object is a search tree prioritized by local deviations and mixed-difference interaction scores. Instead of expanding every joint move, MCTS follows branches where changing one agent's action changes the value of another's action. The first-principles problem is interaction sparsity: in a large game, useful search is about consequential coupling, not exhaustive enumeration.

Mathematical object
A multi-agent search tree prioritized by local deviations and interaction scores.
Approach
Uses mixed-difference interaction estimates to guide MCTS toward consequential joint-action changes.
Themes
Multi-agent RL; strategic interaction; search efficiency.

RLVepsR

ICML 2026

RLVepsR asks when a verifier reward is good enough to train against. A verifier that often marks correct work as wrong or wrong work as correct is not merely a weak teacher. It can push the policy away from reasoning that actually works. The concrete object is the verifier's discrimination power, captured through its true-positive and false-positive behavior. The paper analyzes reinforcement learning with verifier rewards through this noise model. The first-principles boundary is whether the reward signal carries more useful direction than misleading direction; below that point, optimization can become anti-learning.

Mathematical object
A verifier-noise model controlling the reward signal used for RL with verifier feedback.
Approach
Characterizes learning regimes through verifier discrimination quality, including anti-learning under bad noise.
Themes
Verifier rewards; noisy supervision; RL phase transitions.

R2VPO

ICML 2026

R2VPO's core concept is preserving useful high-return policy updates without letting policy ratios become unstable. Hard clipping protects reinforcement learning from large policy changes, but it can also remove the gradient signal from rare actions that produced strong returns. The first-principles problem is trust-region control: allow improvement while bounding how violently the new policy departs from the old one. R2VPO replaces hard clipping with policy-ratio variance constraints, limiting distributional volatility while retaining informative high-return ratios. The evidence is more stable policy improvement because the update is controlled by ratio spread, not by a blunt cutoff.

Mathematical object
A distribution of policy likelihood ratios with constrained variance during policy optimization.
Approach
Controls policy-ratio variance instead of hard-clipping every large ratio, preserving informative gradients.
Themes
Policy optimization; trust regions; variance-controlled updates.
BATCH 40

Scientific Generators, Physical Constraints, and Native-State Evidence

Modified SINNs

ICML 2026

Modified SINNs treats high-dimensional PDE learning as a spectral-structure problem. A neural solver can match pointwise samples while missing the frequency behavior that controls stability, smoothness, and long-range field structure. The concrete object is a high-dimensional PDE solution field represented through spectral coefficients and basis embeddings. Spectral residuals, coefficient-decay scaling, and basis-aware embeddings guide the approximation. The first-principles problem is basis-level physics: the solver should learn the field in the representation where the equation's structure can be controlled, not only fit scattered values.

Mathematical object
A high-dimensional PDE solution field represented through spectral coefficients and basis embeddings.
Approach
Adds spectral residual structure, coefficient decay, and basis-aware embeddings to neural PDE solving.
Themes
Scientific computing; PDE generation; spectral invariants.

Lagrangian Action

ICML 2026

Lagrangian Action treats population dynamics as paths that spend effort, not only as snapshots that match observed marginals. Knowing where a population appears at several times does not uniquely say how mass moved between them. The concrete object is a time-indexed population distribution path in Wasserstein space. The method fits temporal marginals by minimizing action over possible trajectories. The first-principles problem is plausible motion: infer a mechanism of movement that respects transport cost, instead of allowing arbitrary jumps that happen to match each observed distribution.

Mathematical object
A time-indexed population distribution path in Wasserstein space.
Approach
Fits temporal marginals by minimizing Lagrangian action over population trajectories.
Themes
Population dynamics; optimal transport; physical path evidence.

TD3B

ICML 2026

TD3B separates binding from intervention. A molecule can attach tightly to a protein and still fail, because the useful question is not only whether it sticks but what state it pushes the protein toward. The concrete object is a binder tied to a desired conformational transition, such as agonist or antagonist behavior. The method designs allosteric binders with a directional objective, so candidates are judged by their effect on protein motion and state. The first-principles shift is from static fit to controlled biological change: a drug-like molecule is an action, not just a shape.

Mathematical object
A binder candidate coupled to a desired protein-state transition direction.
Approach
Optimizes binder generation toward specified agonist or antagonist transition behavior.
Themes
Protein design; allosteric control; functional molecular generation.

UDM-GRPO

ICML 2026

UDM-GRPO treats diffusion alignment as reward learning along the same probability path that creates the image. A reward model can prefer better images, but an update that ignores the denoising process may optimize a mismatched shortcut. The concrete object is a text-to-image diffusion probability path whose sampled images receive reward feedback. GRPO is adapted to the UDM path so credit follows the generative trajectory. The first-principles problem is attached feedback: reward should shape the process that actually produced the sample, not a detached score layered on afterward.

Mathematical object
A text-to-image diffusion probability path whose sampled images receive reward feedback.
Approach
Applies GRPO in a way matched to UDM probability paths instead of an external reward-only shortcut.
Themes
Diffusion alignment; generative RL; probability-path credit assignment.

Local Diffusion Composition

ICML 2026

Local Diffusion Composition asks when local denoising rules are enough to define a global generator. If the target structure is sparse, every variable should not need to consult every other variable. The concrete object is a set of local conditional diffusion scores over sparsely dependent groups. The paper proves conditions under which those local scores compose into a coherent projective diffusion model. The first-principles issue is consistency: local pieces are useful only if they agree on the shared variables and form one valid global distribution, rather than a collection of incompatible denoisers.

Mathematical object
Local conditional diffusion scores over sparsely dependent variable groups.
Approach
Proves when local score functions compose into a coherent projective diffusion model.
Themes
Structured diffusion; conditional independence; compositional generation.

Flow Sampling

ICML 2026

Flow Sampling starts from targets we can score but cannot normalize. In many scientific problems, an energy function tells us which states are costly or plausible, while the full probability distribution is hard to compute. The concrete object is an unnormalized target density defined by that energy. The paper builds denoising drifts for diffusion or flow-matching samplers so particles move toward the target without needing its partition function. The first-principles move is to use the energy landscape directly as guidance for transport, instead of first replacing it with a separate learned density.

Mathematical object
An unnormalized target density specified by an energy function and sampled through learned flows.
Approach
Builds energy-informed denoising drifts for diffusion and flow-matching samplers.
Themes
Energy-based sampling; flow matching; scientific posterior generation.

DiBO

ICML 2026

DiBO treats offline black-box design as generative improvement over discrete candidates. The model sees limited scored examples of molecules, proteins, prompts, or other symbolic objects, then must propose better ones without interactive trials. The concrete object is a discrete design sequence distribution conditioned by offline labels and improvement pressure. Bidirectional diffusion language modeling and reinforcement learning push generation toward higher-value candidates while preserving valid sequence structure. The first-principles problem is valid improvement: search should raise the score without breaking the discrete form of the object being designed.

Mathematical object
A discrete design sequence distribution conditioned by offline labels and improvement pressure.
Approach
Combines bidirectional diffusion language modeling with RL that rewards label improvement in small-data settings.
Themes
Offline black-box optimization; discrete diffusion; design generation.

NeuronCtrl

ICML 2026

NeuronCtrl treats neural intervention as closed-loop control of a living dynamical field. A stimulation policy can look effective in latent space while violating timing, safety, or morphology constraints in the physical system. The concrete object is a neural activity field with morphology-aware dynamics and safety-constrained control actions. Observers, neural operators, conditional flows, and barrier filters produce low-latency control policies. The first-principles problem is bounded intervention: choose actions that move neural activity toward a target while respecting the hard limits of the tissue and measurement system.

Mathematical object
A neural activity field with morphology-aware dynamics and safety-constrained control actions.
Approach
Uses observers, neural operators, conditional flows, and barrier filters to produce safe low-latency control.
Themes
Scientific control; neural fields; safe generative intervention.

SurvDiff

ICML 2026

SurvDiff asks what synthetic data must preserve for survival analysis to remain valid. A survival row is not just covariates plus a label. It records a measurement process: either an event happened at a time, or observation stopped before the event was seen. The concrete object is mixed covariates together with event times and right-censoring indicators. SurvDiff generates those pieces jointly with a time-to-event loss. The first-principles requirement is to keep the meaning of censoring intact, because realistic-looking tables can still destroy the statistical question survival models are meant to answer.

Mathematical object
A mixed-covariate survival dataset with event times and right-censoring indicators.
Approach
Trains diffusion generation with a survival-aware time-to-event objective.
Themes
Synthetic clinical data; survival modeling; censoring-aware generation.

KPE/KTS

ICML 2026

KPE/KTS evaluates a flow model by the path it takes from noise to data. A final sample can look good even if the trajectory is suspicious: too little movement may ignore structure, while an overly tight route may copy training examples. The concrete object is a flow-matching trajectory with kinetic path energy and trajectory statistics. KPE and KTS measure how much effort the model spends while transporting mass. The first-principles diagnostic is path energy: generation quality is not only an endpoint property, because the route can reveal whether the model learned structure or memorized examples.

Mathematical object
A flow-matching trajectory with kinetic path energy and trajectory statistics.
Approach
Measures trajectory effort to diagnose the balance between sample fidelity, diversity, and memorization.
Themes
Flow diagnostics; generative evaluation; memorization boundary.
BATCH 41

Memory Editing, Workflow Data, and Data-Value Accounting

AI Engram

ICML 2026

AI Engram asks what data governance means after information has become model memory. Removing a document or filtering a corpus acts outside the model, but learned information may already live inside the weights. The concrete object is a memory direction that can be composed or erased through representation arithmetic. The method treats memory subsets as editable internal objects rather than requiring repeated retraining for every update. The first-principles shift is from source control to memory control: deletion and composition must operate on the representation that now carries the information, not only on the dataset that originally supplied it.

Mathematical object
Linear memory directions inside a model that support subset composition and erasure.
Approach
Uses representation arithmetic to compose or remove memory subsets without repeated optimization loops.
Themes
Model memory governance; unlearning; internal data control.

Scientific Annotation BC

ICML 2026

Scientific Annotation BC treats annotation as a workflow that contains transferable judgment, not just a final label. A completed annotation hides the hesitations, rejected choices, corrections, and rules that produced it. The concrete object is an annotation trajectory with task state, decisions, mistakes, and fixes. Multi-task pretraining over those traces lets shared mistake representations transfer across annotation tasks. The first-principles problem is supervision loss: when only the final label is kept, the model loses the procedure that made the scientific judgment reliable and reusable.

Mathematical object
Annotation trajectories with task states, decisions, mistakes, and corrections.
Approach
Pretrains on workflow traces so shared annotation mistakes and fixes transfer across tasks.
Themes
Workflow supervision; scientific annotation; process data.

Procedural Pretraining

ICML 2026

Procedural Pretraining treats early data order as a way to teach reusable operations before broad language learning. A small amount of algorithmic data can shape how later examples are processed, even if it is tiny compared with the full corpus. The concrete object is a pretraining curriculum where an early procedural slice changes later learning dynamics. A brief algorithmic warmup improves later language, code, and math behavior. The first-principles problem is curriculum timing: some data matters because it teaches the model how to process later data, not because it adds volume.

Mathematical object
A pretraining curriculum where an early algorithmic-data slice changes later learning dynamics.
Approach
Uses a 0.1-0.3% procedural warmup before ordinary pretraining to seed reusable computational skills.
Themes
Curriculum data; procedural skill formation; data timing.

daVinci-Dev

ICML 2026

daVinci-Dev treats code-agent training data as a record of work, not just a final patch. A successful software task depends on file reads, searches, tool calls, failed attempts, tests, edits, and corrections. The concrete object is a software-agent trajectory containing tool calls, code edits, test results, and information flow. The dataset preserves full execution traces for mid-training. The first-principles problem is procedural evidence: to teach a developer agent, the training data must show how the solution was found and verified, not only what the finished answer looked like.

Mathematical object
A software-agent trajectory containing tool calls, code edits, test results, and information flow.
Approach
Uses full tool-execution traces as mid-training data for code agents.
Themes
Agent data curation; developer tools; trajectory supervision.

LM Memorization Capacity

ICML 2026

LM Memorization Capacity measures how much raw information a model can store when ordinary generalization is removed. Privacy and copyright risk depend on storage capacity, not only on whether a benchmark catches a model regurgitating. The concrete object is a model-parameter storage channel measured in memorized bits per parameter. Experiments designed to suppress generalization estimate capacity for GPT-style models. The first-principles problem is retention accounting: if a model can encode many bits of training data directly, governance needs a quantitative storage measure rather than relying only on visible extraction examples.

Mathematical object
A model-parameter storage channel measured in memorized bits per parameter.
Approach
Estimates memorization capacity under setups designed to remove ordinary generalization explanations.
Themes
Memorization; privacy risk; data retention capacity.

OU Identifiability

ICML 2026

OU Identifiability treats experimental design as a graph-governed data collection problem. Observational trajectories can leave causal dynamics ambiguous, while too many interventions may be costly or impossible. The concrete object is a dynamical causal graph with strongly connected components and chosen intervention targets. The result shows that one intervention per component can generically identify Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics up to scale. The first-principles problem is intervention placement: collect the minimum evidence that breaks the right ambiguities, instead of adding experiments without knowing which graph component they identify.

Mathematical object
A dynamical causal graph with strongly connected components and intervention targets.
Approach
Proves that one intervention per component can generically identify dynamics up to scale.
Themes
Causal data design; dynamical systems; intervention efficiency.

Unpaired Causal IV

ICML 2026

Unpaired Causal IV asks how causal evidence can accumulate across many sparse environments. Classical intuition often demands repeated observations within each environment, but scientific and policy settings may offer breadth across environments instead. The concrete object is a collection of sparse environments with instrumental variation and limited observations per environment. The analysis proves consistency as the number of environments grows while within-environment repetition stays fixed. The first-principles problem is evidence allocation: identify when diversity of environments can replace depth of repeated samples for recovering a causal effect.

Mathematical object
A set of sparse environments with instrumental variation and limited observations per environment.
Approach
Analyzes consistency when the number of environments grows despite fixed sparse repetition within each one.
Themes
Causal experiment design; sparse environments; instrument evidence.

RoTS

ICML 2026

RoTS treats GUI-agent robustness as recovery from wrong turns, not only clean task completion. An agent trained on ideal demonstrations may collapse after one wrong click, stale screen, unexpected widget, or partial form state. The concrete object is a tree of GUI trajectories containing normal paths, errors, and recovery actions. Tree-based discovery synthesizes diverse deviations and repairs at scale. The first-principles problem is state repair: interactive competence means knowing how to return from a bad state to a useful path, not only following the path when nothing goes wrong.

Mathematical object
A tree of GUI trajectories containing nominal paths, errors, and recovery actions.
Approach
Generates large-scale recovery trajectories by discovering diverse GUI error modes.
Themes
Agent robustness data; GUI recovery; trajectory synthesis.

Identity Bridge

ICML 2026

Identity Bridge treats reverse relational knowledge as something the data may need to teach explicitly. Seeing A-to-B pairs does not guarantee that an autoregressive model will answer B-to-A queries, because the training evidence is directional. The concrete object is a relation-training dataset augmented with identity bridge examples. Adding A-to-A examples encourages the model to preserve entity identity while learning reverse use of relations. The first-principles problem is relational symmetry: if a system should use a relation both ways, the training data must make the preserved identity visible, not assume sequence learning will infer it.

Mathematical object
A relation-training dataset augmented with identity bridge examples.
Approach
Adds A-to-A data so autoregressive models learn to preserve entity identity across reverse relational queries.
Themes
Knowledge data design; relation reversal; autoregressive asymmetry.

NS/IF Attribution

ICML 2026

NS/IF Attribution measures data value through local model movement. Influence estimates can look exact while depending on curvature assumptions that fail once the model moves too far from the point being approximated. The concrete object is a Newton-step approximation to the parameter change caused by removing training data. The paper analyzes that removal effect under local curvature conditions. The first-principles boundary is locality: the attribution is strongest as a statement about nearby optimization geometry, not as a global story that one example has the same importance everywhere in training or deployment.

Mathematical object
A local Newton-step approximation to parameter movement caused by removing training data.
Approach
Derives attribution behavior under local curvature assumptions around the first Newton update.
Themes
Data attribution; influence functions; local optimization geometry.
BATCH 42

Feedback Objects, Reward Design, and Preference Credit

ClinTutor-R1

ICML 2026

ClinTutor-R1 treats clinical tutoring as feedback to two states at once. The tutor must understand the individual trainee's current misconception, but it must also stay anchored to accepted clinical reasoning. If it only personalizes, it can drift away from medical standards; if it only gives the canonical answer, it may fail to teach the learner in front of it. The concrete object is a trainee belief state coupled to a group clinical-consensus target. The first-principles problem is Socratic update under standards: move the learner's reasoning without moving the domain truth to fit the learner.

Mathematical object
Individual trainee belief states coupled to a group clinical-consensus target.
Approach
Uses learner-state and consensus modeling to guide Socratic clinical feedback.
Themes
Personalized alignment; clinical education; belief-state feedback.

RLR

ICLR 2026

RLR asks how a reward should train a model whose sample is made through many denoising steps. In diffusion post-training, the final reward belongs to an object, but the object came from a recursive stochastic path. The concrete object is that sampling chain together with an estimator that assigns reward credit back through it. If the estimator is too biased, it teaches the wrong denoising behavior; if it has too much variance, learning becomes unstable. The first-principles problem is to design the feedback interface, because the reward only helps if credit reaches the right parts of the generation path.

Mathematical object
A recursive diffusion sampling chain with downstream reward credit assigned through an estimator.
Approach
Designs post-training estimators that trade bias against variance for diffusion reward optimization.
Themes
Diffusion alignment; estimator design; reward credit assignment.

h1

ICML 2026

h1 treats reasoning reinforcement learning as possible learning of new paths, not only selection among hidden samples the base model already could produce. The key doubt is whether RL merely elicits existing ability through more search. The concrete object is a distribution over reasoning trajectories before and after curriculum reinforcement learning. The evaluation asks whether gains remain even when base-model sampling already has high pass@k. The first-principles problem is change of reachable behavior: learning has happened only if the policy can now reach reasoning trajectories that were not practically available before.

Mathematical object
A distribution over reasoning trajectories before and after curriculum reinforcement learning.
Approach
Uses curriculum RL and evaluates whether gains persist beyond base-model sampling capacity.
Themes
Reasoning RL; capability learning; trajectory distribution shift.

ParetoPO

ICML 2026

ParetoPO treats alignment as movement along a frontier of competing objectives. Real deployments care about helpfulness, safety, latency, cost, style, and task success at the same time. Collapsing them into one scalar reward hides which objective was sacrificed. The concrete object is a multi-objective policy frontier with dominance relations and hypervolume improvement. The method uses hypervolume-guided scalarization and dominance-aware advantages so updates respect tradeoffs. The first-principles problem is not finding one natural reward; it is improving a policy while making visible which deployment values are being balanced.

Mathematical object
A multi-objective policy frontier with dominance relations and hypervolume improvement.
Approach
Combines hypervolume scalarization with dominance-aware policy advantages.
Themes
Multi-objective alignment; Pareto preference optimization; deployment tradeoffs.

Divide-and-Denoise

ICML 2026

Divide-and-Denoise treats composed generation as coordination among specialist diffusion models. If several specialists contribute to one sample, the broadest or strongest model can dominate and erase the responsibility of the others. The concrete object is a denoising process partitioned across model responsibilities. Fairness constraints decide which specialist should denoise which part of the object and prevent collapse to one contributor. The first-principles problem is responsibility assignment: a composed generator must preserve the reason each specialist was included, rather than averaging their signals until the composition becomes meaningless.

Mathematical object
A composed diffusion denoising process partitioned across specialist model responsibilities.
Approach
Coordinates specialists with fairness constraints so no one model dominates the composed generation.
Themes
Inference-time alignment; diffusion composition; specialist responsibility.

RGR-GRPO

ICML 2026

RGR-GRPO turns rubrics into dense reward structure for reasoning domains where final correctness is too sparse. A solution can fail through a wrong setup, missing constraint, bad intermediate step, or final arithmetic error, and treating those failures as identical wastes feedback. The concrete object is a reasoning trajectory scored by rubric dimensions. Rubric-guided rewards and offline guidance are used inside GRPO-style optimization across math, physics, chemistry, and general tasks. The first-principles problem is diagnostic reward: train from the reason a solution failed, not only from the fact that it failed.

Mathematical object
A reasoning trajectory scored by rubric dimensions rather than only final correctness.
Approach
Uses rubric rewards and offline guidance inside GRPO-style policy optimization.
Themes
Process rewards; rubric alignment; multi-domain reasoning.

Complex Reasoning/TRM

ICML 2026

Complex Reasoning/TRM treats reasoning reward as a judgment about the path, not only the final answer. Test-time selection and RL both depend on a scorer, and a scorer that rewards fluency or final-answer luck can strengthen brittle shortcuts. The concrete object is a reasoning trace evaluated by a reward model over thinking quality. Thinking reward models score decomposition, intermediate logic, and verification behavior. The first-principles problem is process credit: the feedback signal should prefer reasoning that earns the answer, not text that merely resembles a good solution.

Mathematical object
Reasoning traces evaluated by a reward model over thinking quality.
Approach
Trains reward models to support test-time selection and RL over complex reasoning processes.
Themes
Reward modeling; reasoning evaluation; process-level alignment.

LiDAR Sampling

ICML 2026

LiDAR Sampling treats aligned diffusion guidance as useful only if it fits the sampling budget. Gradient guidance can push images toward human preferences, but repeated gradient computation can be too slow for practical generation. The concrete object is a diffusion sampling trajectory guided toward human-aligned visual preferences under a compute budget. The method preserves guidance quality while changing the computational path to accelerate sampling. The first-principles problem is affordable alignment: the preference signal matters only when the mechanism that applies it can run at the speed and cost required by use.

Mathematical object
A diffusion sampling trajectory guided toward human-aligned visual preferences under a compute budget.
Approach
Accelerates aligned guidance while preserving performance comparable to gradient-based guidance.
Themes
Fast alignment; diffusion guidance; inference cost.

Tilt Matching

ICML 2026

Tilt Matching shifts a generative flow toward reward-preferred samples without requiring reward gradients through the full sampling path. In image generation, the reward may be a black-box preference score, and trajectory backpropagation can be expensive. The concrete object is a velocity field tilted toward a reward-weighted target distribution. Reward-velocity cumulants update flow matching in the preferred direction. The first-principles problem is preference without direct gradients: the model must change how samples move through generation using only reward observations, while keeping the flow structure that makes sampling coherent.

Mathematical object
A generative velocity field tilted toward a reward-weighted target distribution.
Approach
Uses reward-velocity cumulants to update flow matching without reward gradients or trajectory backpropagation.
Themes
Reward fine-tuning; flow matching; diffusion preference optimization.

Hista/Numca

ICML 2026

Hista/Numca improves credit assignment by valuing intermediate reasoning states. A solution can go wrong long before the final answer, but final rewards arrive too late to identify which step caused the failure. The concrete object is a hidden reasoning state or numerical span with estimated downstream value. Rollout averaging from those states gives reinforcement learning a signal at meaningful milestones without inventing arbitrary rewards for every token. The first-principles problem is where progress becomes measurable: credit should attach to states that change the chance of finishing correctly.

Mathematical object
Hidden reasoning states and numerical spans with estimated downstream value.
Approach
Averages rollouts from hidden states and numerical milestones to improve process-level value estimates.
Themes
Credit assignment; reasoning RL; milestone value estimation.
BATCH 43

Monitorability, Protected Information, and Control Boundaries

Monitoring Monitorability

ICML 2026

Monitoring Monitorability asks whether a reasoning trace actually helps a monitor catch bad agent behavior. Chain-of-thought can expose intent, but it can also be incomplete, misleading, or written after the decisive motive has already formed elsewhere. The concrete object is an agent trajectory paired with action logs and reasoning traces available to a monitor. The paper measures when traces improve detection beyond action-only evidence. The first-principles property is observability: a safety channel is valuable only if it makes the relevant hidden cause more visible before harm appears in the final action.

Mathematical object
Agent trajectories paired with action logs and chain-of-thought traces available to a monitor.
Approach
Compares misbehavior detection from reasoning traces versus action-only evidence.
Themes
Agent monitoring; CoT transparency; safety observability.

Noisy Sample Compression

ICML 2026

Noisy Sample Compression treats compression as useful only when the important structure survives corrupted samples. A small description of a distribution class can work in the clean setting and fail once samples are perturbed in l2 or total variation. The concrete object is a compressed representation of a distribution class under sample noise. The theory characterizes when the smaller representation still preserves what must be learned. The first-principles problem is noise-stable sufficiency: compression should keep the information that identifies the distribution class, not details that disappear under realistic perturbation.

Mathematical object
A compressed representation of a distribution class under l2 and total-variation sample noise.
Approach
Analyzes conditions where sample compression still preserves learnable structure after perturbation.
Themes
Robust learning theory; compression; noise-stable structure.

OPL/G-OPL

ICML 2026

OPL/G-OPL treats privacy in video anomaly detection as a representation constraint. The concrete object is a video representation partitioned into facial-attribute information and anomaly-relevant pose or motion signal. Weak face-presence supervision projects away facial attributes while retaining dynamics for detection. The first-principles problem is task-preserving privacy: remove what identifies a person while keeping the physical evidence needed to judge whether an event is abnormal.

Mathematical object
Video representations partitioned into facial-attribute information and anomaly-relevant pose/motion signal.
Approach
Projects away facial attributes using weak supervision while retaining dynamics needed for anomaly detection.
Themes
Video privacy; anomaly detection; protected-attribute removal.

Backdoor Self-Awareness

ICML 2026

Backdoor Self-Awareness asks whether a poisoned model can help expose the rule that compromises it. A backdoor is dangerous because ordinary behavior stays normal until a hidden trigger activates a different policy. The concrete object is a language model with trigger-conditioned behavior and generated explanations of that trigger. Inversion-inspired reinforcement learning trains the model to articulate the latent condition controlling its failure. The first-principles move is to turn a hidden vulnerability into an object the model can report, so diagnosis is based on recovering the trigger logic rather than only observing attacks after they fire.

Mathematical object
A poisoned language model with hidden trigger-conditioned behavior and generated trigger explanations.
Approach
Uses RL inspired by inversion to make the model describe the triggers controlling its backdoor behavior.
Themes
Backdoor diagnosis; model introspection; trigger recovery.

Fair Posthoc Control

ICML 2026

Fair Posthoc Control treats fairness as a deployment control, not a single setting chosen forever during training. A hospital, lender, or platform may need a different fairness-accuracy balance after policy, population, or legal requirements change. Retraining for every point can be unavailable. The concrete object is a representation that preserves a usable control surface after the model is learned. The method aims to let downstream users move along that surface without rebuilding the model. The protected value is not one fixed classifier, but the ability to make accountable tradeoffs under changing constraints.

Mathematical object
A learned representation with a post-training fairness-accuracy control surface.
Approach
Trains representations so deployment-time controls can adjust fairness tradeoffs without model retraining.
Themes
Fairness control; post-hoc governance; representation constraints.

Exact RL Unlearning

ICML 2026

Exact RL Unlearning treats deletion as matching the counterfactual learner that never saw the user's data. In reinforcement learning, one user's data can affect values, policies, replay state, and later behavior, so removing a row is not enough. The concrete object is an RL learner state compared with a state trained without the deleted user's contribution. The method defines exact deletion by indistinguishability and seeks cheaper procedures than full retraining. The first-principles problem is counterfactual forgetting: after removal, the system should behave as if the protected data had never shaped learning.

Mathematical object
An RL learner state compared against a counterfactual state that never used the deleted user's data.
Approach
Defines exact deletion by indistinguishability and develops cheaper-than-retraining unlearning procedures.
Themes
RL privacy; unlearning; counterfactual deletion guarantees.

Adaptive Bias

ICML 2026

Adaptive Bias studies bias created by the learner's own choices. Even if two artificial groups are truly equal, an interactive model may sample them unevenly, see different evidence, and then treat the difference as a group property. The concrete object is a feedback loop where exploration changes the data stream, and the changed data stream changes later beliefs. The paper tests whether LLMs can acquire new group biases this way. The first-principles warning is that safety cannot inspect only the original training corpus; it must also inspect the data the model creates by acting.

Mathematical object
An adaptive interaction process where exploration choices shape later group-belief updates.
Approach
Tests whether LLMs acquire artificial-group biases through exploration despite no true group differences.
Themes
Emergent bias; adaptive data collection; social safety.

Assistant Axis

ICML 2026

Assistant Axis treats jailbreak defense as control over the model's internal behavioral state. Some attacks work by pulling the model into a role or persona where ordinary assistant constraints no longer bind its answers. The concrete object is an activation-space region associated with stable assistant behavior. Constraining movement along that axis reduces harmful persona drift and keeps responses closer to the assistant contract. The first-principles problem is state identity: the model should not only refuse certain strings; it should remain in the internal mode where help, limits, and user-facing responsibility are still active.

Mathematical object
An activation-space assistant region whose movement correlates with persona drift and safety behavior.
Approach
Constrains activations along the assistant axis to keep behavior inside a safer persona state.
Themes
Jailbreak defense; activation steering; persona stability.

Conformal Policy Control

ICML 2026

Conformal Policy Control regulates an optimized policy by measuring how far it departs from a safe reference policy. Policy optimization can raise reward while silently leaving the behavioral region where available safety data is trustworthy. The concrete object is optimized-policy deviation under conformal finite-sample risk bounds. Calibration on reference-policy data defines a risk envelope for acceptable movement. The first-principles problem is bounded change: a safety guarantee is meaningful only within the evidence region that supports it, so the policy update must know when improvement has moved beyond what the data can certify.

Mathematical object
An optimized policy's deviation from a safe reference-policy distribution under conformal risk bounds.
Approach
Uses conformal calibration on reference-policy data to regulate policy updates with finite-sample guarantees.
Themes
Policy safety; conformal risk control; deployment guarantees.

GoodDiffusion

ICML 2026

GoodDiffusion treats diffusion authorization as an attack surface. A signature that unlocks high-quality generation may look like access control, but if the same signature works across many inputs, an attacker can search for it. The concrete object is the authorization signal itself: is it secret under gradient-based recovery pressure, or merely hidden until optimized against? The paper shows that universal signatures can be reconstructed by surrogate attacks. The first-principles lesson is that access control for generators needs proof objects that are input-specific or hard to transfer, not static keys embedded in the generation process.

Mathematical object
A diffusion authorization signature controlling high-quality generation access.
Approach
Uses gradient-based surrogate recovery to test whether static signatures can be reconstructed by attackers.
Themes
Generative access control; signature security; adversarial authorization.
BATCH 44

Invariant Geometry, Latent Interfaces, and Structured Model Space

Diffract

ICML 2026

Diffract asks what actually moves when a language model adapts to a new domain. Continual pretraining is often described as adding knowledge, but the representation may change in a more specific way. The concrete objects are layerwise singular values, singular vectors, and domain-specific heads. The paper finds that the size pattern of the spectrum can remain fairly stable while the directions and heads rotate toward the new domain. The first-principles picture is adaptation as reorientation inside an existing capacity geometry, not as a complete rewrite of the model.

Mathematical object
Layerwise singular spectra, singular vectors, and domain-specific output heads during continual pretraining.
Approach
Analyzes spectral preservation and directional movement to explain how LLMs adapt across domains.
Themes
Spectral representation geometry; domain adaptation; controlled subspace change.

DIGL

ICML 2026

DIGL's core concept is graph out-of-distribution generalization through a shared invariant prototype. Different graph environments can distort node features, edge patterns, or local statistics, while the task may still depend on a common relational object underneath. The first-principles problem is separating environmental distortion from graph meaning that should survive shift. DIGL treats each environment's graph representation as a deformation of a shared prototype, so learning becomes alignment around invariant relational structure. The evidence is better OOD graph performance because the model searches for what remains stable across environments instead of fitting each graph distribution separately.

Mathematical object
Environment-specific graph representations aligned to a shared invariant prototype.
Approach
Geometrizes graph OOD learning as distortion correction around a common relational representation.
Themes
Graph OOD generalization; invariant prototypes; representation distortion.

Neural Ricci Flow

ICML 2026

Neural Ricci Flow treats feature learning as a change in geometry, not only as lower loss. During training, neighborhoods in representation space can stretch, contract, merge, or sharpen, and those changes affect what the model can separate. The concrete object is a feature graph whose edges and curvature-like quantities evolve with training. Discrete Ricci-flow-style transformations describe how representation space redistributes local structure. The first-principles question is what training does to distances: learning changes which examples become near, far, smooth, or sharply separated inside the model.

Mathematical object
Feature-geometry graphs whose edge and curvature structure evolves during neural training.
Approach
Uses discrete Ricci-flow-like transformations to characterize how feature geometry changes.
Themes
Feature geometry; representation dynamics; geometric learning diagnostics.

MOG

ICML 2026

MOG treats diffusion guidance as control on a learned data manifold. Classifier-free guidance can make prompts matter more, but strong guidance can also oversaturate, distort, or collapse structure because the update points through ambient space rather than along valid data directions. The concrete object is a diffusion sample path controlled near the manifold. By recasting guidance as local manifold-aware optimal control, the method explains artifacts as geometric mismatch. The first-principles problem is steering without leaving the surface of valid images: conditioning should move a sample toward meaning, not into directions the data never supported.

Mathematical object
A diffusion sample path controlled on or near the data manifold rather than arbitrary ambient directions.
Approach
Uses Riemannian, manifold-aware guidance to steer generation without off-manifold extrapolation.
Themes
Diffusion geometry; manifold control; guidance artifacts.

1D Semantic Tokenizer

ICML 2026

1D Semantic Tokenizer treats image tokenization as an interface between visual meaning and autoregressive sequence prediction. Image tokens can be too local, too high-dimensional, or poorly matched to the order a language-model-style generator needs. The concrete object is a one-dimensional sequence of semantic image tokens. Foundation-model signals help build tokens that preserve visual meaning while remaining easy for a sequence model to predict. The first-principles problem is representation handoff: choose the unit the generator sees so image structure survives conversion into a sequence rather than becoming a grid of weak local fragments.

Mathematical object
A one-dimensional sequence of semantic image tokens used as the autoregressive generation interface.
Approach
Builds semantic tokens using foundation-model signals so sequence prediction preserves visual meaning.
Themes
Latent tokenization; image generation; sequence-compatible visual representation.

ReViT

ICML 2026

ReViT starts before attention, at the point where physical data becomes tokens. Scalar and vector fields carry local symmetries; if tokenization breaks those symmetries, the transformer is already reasoning over a distorted object. The concrete object is a locally invariant representation of physical inputs passed into self-attention. ReViT prepares features so changes of coordinate or local orientation do not masquerade as changes in the underlying field. The first-principles point is simple: attention should compare physical content, not artifacts introduced by the representation used to feed the model.

Mathematical object
Locally invariant scalar/vector representations passed into transformer attention.
Approach
Prepares physics-compatible token features before self-attention to avoid symmetry violations.
Themes
Physical representation; invariant attention; symmetry-preserving transformers.

Weight-Space Expressivity

ICML 2026

Weight-Space Expressivity treats model parameters as structured objects, not as ordinary coordinates in a flat vector. If two hidden neurons are permuted, the parameter tensor changes, but the represented function may stay the same. The concrete object is weight space with these neuron-permutation symmetries factored out. The paper asks which maps over weights are expressive while still respecting that equivalence. This matters for any model that reads, edits, or generates other models: it must understand the function represented by parameters without mistaking arbitrary neuron labels for meaningful information.

Mathematical object
Neural network parameter tensors quotienting out neuron-permutation symmetries.
Approach
Analyzes maps over weights while preserving the equivalence between permuted networks and functions.
Themes
Weight-space geometry; permutation symmetry; model representation.

TEDBench/MiAE

ICML 2026

TEDBench/MiAE treats protein representation learning as reconstruction under the right geometric invariance. A protein lives in three-dimensional space, but its biological identity should not change when the coordinate frame is rotated or translated. The concrete object is an SE(3)-invariant protein structure representation learned under high-mask-ratio autoencoding. MiAE hides much of the structure and forces the model to recover useful information, while TEDBench supplies the evaluation setting. The first-principles problem is to learn structural features at scale while ignoring arbitrary pose and preserving the geometry that biology actually uses.

Mathematical object
SE(3)-invariant protein structure representations learned under high-mask-ratio reconstruction.
Approach
Uses invariant masked autoencoding to force scalable protein-structure representations.
Themes
Protein geometry; invariant autoencoding; structural representation benchmarks.

TG-DT

ICML 2026

TG-DT grounds task language in behavior space for offline meta-RL. A description is useful only if it maps to the control behavior it requests, not if it remains a label pasted on top of trajectories. The concrete object is an alignment between text embeddings and behavior embeddings used to condition policies. Contrastive and matching losses bring the two spaces together so language can select skills from offline data. The first-principles question is whether words become a control interface: when the task says what to do, the policy should move in the behavior space that actually does it.

Mathematical object
Text embeddings and behavior embeddings aligned for conditioning offline meta-RL policies.
Approach
Uses contrastive and matching losses to align language with trajectory behavior space.
Themes
Language-conditioned control; behavior representation; offline meta-RL.

DeCoDe

ICML 2026

DeCoDe's core concept is molecular generation as coarse-to-fine pose and conformation construction. A ligand is useful only if its global position fits the protein pocket and its local chemical geometry remains plausible; treating all coordinates as one undifferentiated output can confuse those levels. The first-principles problem is staged constraint satisfaction: place the molecule in the binding site before refining detailed structure. DeCoDe guides denoising first toward pocket-level positioning and then toward fine molecular conformation. The evidence is better pocket-conditioned generation because global pose and local chemistry are solved in the order the physical problem demands.

Mathematical object
Ligand pose and molecular conformation generated in a protein pocket through staged denoising.
Approach
Uses coarse-to-fine diffusion guidance: position first, then refine detailed molecular structure.
Themes
Molecular geometry; pocket-conditioned generation; hierarchical denoising.
BATCH 45

Runtime Control, Search Budgets, and Inference-Time Adaptation

Skill Neologisms

ICML 2026

Skill Neologisms asks whether a model can learn new words that behave like callable skills. The word itself is not the point. It matters only if the token becomes a reliable handle for a behavior that can later be invoked and combined. The concrete object is a learned skill name used as a composable control symbol at inference time. The paper trains independent skill neologisms and tests zero-shot composition, including out-of-distribution combinations. The first-principles problem is reusable control: a good skill name should carry an operation that survives being placed beside other operations.

Mathematical object
Learned skill tokens or names that act as composable behavioral control handles.
Approach
Trains independent skill neologisms and tests whether they combine zero-shot at inference time.
Themes
Skill composition; test-time control; reusable behavior interfaces.

OMAC

ICML 2026

OMAC treats multi-agent collaboration as an architecture that can be searched. Changing a system is not only changing prompts; it is deciding who proposes ideas, who compares alternatives, and which design dimensions are optimized alone or together. The concrete object is a multi-agent design with initializer, comparator, and individual or joint optimization roles. Semantic Initializer and Contrastive Comparator actors make those roles explicit. The first-principles question is where reasoning work should be placed across agents so collaboration changes the computation, instead of merely multiplying the number of model calls.

Mathematical object
A multi-agent system design with initializer, comparator, and individual or joint optimization dimensions.
Approach
Uses specialized actors to search collaboration architectures under task feedback.
Themes
Multi-agent control; collaboration search; inference architecture.

SCALE

ICML 2026

SCALE's core concept is test-time control for vision-language-action models using the model's own output distribution. Many runtime control methods need verifiers, repeated rollouts, or external scores, which can be too slow for action. The first-principles problem is internal evidence: find a signal already produced by the model that indicates which action is better. SCALE uses the VLA output distribution as the control signal, steering behavior without adding a separate evaluator. The evidence is improved runtime action selection with lower overhead, showing that test-time control can come from the model's uncertainty shape rather than from extra machinery.

Mathematical object
A VLA model's output distribution used as a runtime action-control signal.
Approach
Controls inference directly from distributional evidence instead of external verifiers or repeated rollouts.
Themes
VLA control; verifier-free inference; runtime action selection.

TTT-Discover

ICML 2026

TTT-Discover treats a hard scientific or engineering problem as important enough to adapt the model during the search. Ordinary inference keeps parameters fixed and searches only over outputs, even when the local problem has its own evidence and feedback. The concrete object is a test-time search process that updates an open LLM around one scientific objective. Reinforcement learning is used during inference-time discovery. The first-principles problem is local specialization: the model should move when the current problem provides useful feedback, while keeping that movement tied to the problem rather than general retraining.

Mathematical object
A test-time search process that updates an open LLM around one scientific or engineering objective.
Approach
Applies RL during inference-time search so the model adapts to the current discovery problem.
Themes
Test-time training; scientific discovery; local model adaptation.

Skill-Pro

ICML 2026

Skill-Pro treats agent improvement as runtime behavior adaptation without changing model weights. An agent may fail because its current plan, tool choice, or task decomposition is weak, not because the base model lacks the skill. The concrete object is an agent trajectory updated by semantic gradients and verification gates. PPO-gated verification decides which behavioral edits are allowed. The first-principles problem is external control: improve the policy expressed during execution while keeping parameters fixed, so adaptation becomes a process of steering actions and plans rather than retraining the model.

Mathematical object
Agent behavior trajectories updated by semantic gradients and verification gates without parameter changes.
Approach
Uses semantic feedback and PPO-gated verification to adapt actions non-parametrically.
Themes
Agent adaptation; verifier-gated control; non-parametric improvement.

MASPOB

ICML 2026

MASPOB's core concept is making multi-agent workflow tuning sample-efficient by decomposing the search. A naive search over prompts, roles, messages, tools, and agent interactions grows combinatorially, so the best workflow can be too expensive to find. The first-principles problem is budgeted search over a structured system: choose subproblems that can be tuned without evaluating every joint configuration. MASPOB reduces multi-agent prompt search from exponential combinations to linear subproblems under limited evaluation budgets. The evidence is better workflow quality per evaluation, showing that agent design is an optimization problem over structure, not only wording.

Mathematical object
A multi-agent prompt/workflow search space decomposed into lower-cost subproblems.
Approach
Breaks combinatorial tuning into sample-efficient linear sub-searches under evaluation limits.
Themes
Workflow optimization; multi-agent systems; budgeted evaluation.

Learning Unmasking Policies

ICML 2026

Learning Unmasking Policies treats decoding order as an inference decision. In diffusion language generation, choosing which masked token to reveal changes what context later tokens receive, so a fixed schedule can lock in weak guesses or waste effort on easy positions. The concrete object is a policy over masked token positions during diffusion language decoding. The method learns adaptive unmasking schedules instead of using hand-tuned heuristics. The first-principles problem is token-level timing: reveal information when it will most improve the unfinished sequence, not when a fixed rule says to do so.

Mathematical object
A policy over masked token positions during diffusion language decoding.
Approach
Learns adaptive unmasking schedules instead of using manually designed decoding heuristics.
Themes
Diffusion language models; adaptive decoding; token-level compute allocation.

Hierarchical Thinking

ICML 2026

Hierarchical Thinking treats reasoning control as intervention at meaningful boundaries, not constant token steering. If every local token choice is adjusted, control becomes expensive and can destabilize the larger argument. The concrete object is a reasoning trajectory segmented into sentence-level decision points with Q-value steering signals. Sparse activation steering at those boundaries improves reasoning with fewer interventions. The first-principles problem is choosing the level of action: many reasoning failures come from wrong intermediate decisions, so control should act where the plan changes, not where spelling or local phrasing changes.

Mathematical object
Reasoning trajectories segmented into sentence-level decision points with Q-value steering signals.
Approach
Applies sparse activation steering at sentence boundaries to control reasoning more efficiently.
Themes
CoT steering; hierarchical control; sparse reasoning interventions.

NAD

ICML 2026

NAD asks how early a generation trajectory reveals that it is not worth finishing. Best-of-N search can improve answers, but completing many full candidates spends a large token budget on paths that may already look wrong. The concrete object is a partial generation trajectory scored for predicted final correctness. NAD estimates that signal within the first 32 tokens and prunes weak candidates before full completion. The first-principles problem is early evidence: spend computation on alternative answers only while those alternatives still have a credible chance of becoming correct.

Mathematical object
Partial generation trajectories scored early for predicted final correctness.
Approach
Uses early correctness prediction to prune best-of-N decoding before full completion.
Themes
Inference pruning; best-of-N search; token-budget control.

BlitzRank

ICML 2026

BlitzRank's core concept is ranking candidates through tournament graphs rather than exhaustive scoring. At inference time, a system may need to choose the best answer, plan, or agent output, but comparing every pair or assigning full scores to every candidate can be too expensive. The first-principles problem is ranking under a comparison budget: recover the top candidates from limited preference evidence. BlitzRank aggregates k-wise comparisons into preference graphs and uses transitive closure to infer top-m structure. The evidence is accurate selection with fewer comparisons, making ranking a graph-recovery problem over sparse judgments.

Mathematical object
A tournament-style preference graph over candidate outputs with inferred top-m structure.
Approach
Aggregates k-wise comparisons and uses graph closure to certify high-ranked candidates efficiently.
Themes
Candidate ranking; comparison-efficient selection; inference-time evaluation.
BATCH 46

Theorem Objects, Mechanism Bounds, and Engineering Explanations

Token Association Dynamics

ICLR 2026

Token Association Dynamics studies how corpus statistics become internal associations before richer semantics appear. A model first sees co-occurrence, order, frequency, and local prediction pressure, not abstract meaning by itself. The concrete object is a token association matrix and its training dynamics under natural-language statistics. The paper analyzes how those statistics organize early attention and embedding structure. The first-principles question is formation: what facts about text make certain tokens pull together, separate, or form useful directions before later layers turn those associations into higher-level concepts?

Mathematical object
Token association matrices and training dynamics induced by natural-language corpus statistics.
Approach
Analyzes how corpus-level statistics drive the initial formation of transformer token associations.
Themes
Training dynamics; corpus statistics; semantic association mechanisms.

To Grok Grokking

ICML 2026

To Grok Grokking strips away the mystery around delayed generalization. In grokking, a model first memorizes the training set and only much later learns a rule that generalizes. The concrete object is the time gap between those two events. The paper studies how hyperparameters stretch, shrink, or remove that gap and gives quantitative bounds on grokking time. This makes grokking an optimization-timescale problem: the question is which training choices make the general rule slow to appear, rather than treating the late jump as an unexplained phase change.

Mathematical object
A training-time delay between memorization and generalization controlled by hyperparameters.
Approach
Derives bounds and shows how hyperparameter choices change or remove grokking delay.
Themes
Grokking theory; optimization timescales; hyperparameter control.

SVD as Fast Interpretability

ICML 2026

SVD as Fast Interpretability uses the model's own weight subspaces as the explanation object. An interpretation can sound meaningful while describing concepts that do not match the computation actually used by the model. The concrete object is an SVD-derived subspace with a measured contribution to a prediction. Subspace Contribution Analysis asks how much each native linear component changes the output. The first-principles issue is faithfulness: an explanation should begin from the internal directions the model uses, then ask what they do, instead of attaching external stories after the fact.

Mathematical object
SVD-derived weight subspaces with quantified contributions to model predictions.
Approach
Applies Subspace Contribution Analysis to measure native subspace influence efficiently.
Themes
Mechanistic interpretability; spectral decomposition; faithful explanations.

Beyond ReLU

ICML 2026

Beyond ReLU treats GNN initialization as a choice of starting point in a dynamical system. Repeated message passing can oversmooth node representations until useful differences disappear, and ordinary initialization may place the network near that bad regime. The concrete object is a GNN message-passing system with bifurcation and oversmoothing behavior. The paper derives a closed-form initialization from the theory, choosing initial conditions that avoid collapse.
