The first-principles idea is that training stability begins before learning starts: the network should be placed in a region where graph information can still remain distinct.

Mathematical object
A GNN message-passing dynamical system with bifurcation and oversmoothing regimes.
Approach
Uses oversmoothing theory to derive closed-form initialization that avoids bad dynamical regimes.
Themes
GNN theory; initialization; dynamical stability.

PoPE

ICML 2026

PoPE's core concept is diagnosing rotary positional embeddings as a confound between content and position. A model should know both what token appeared and where it appeared, but RoPE can entangle those factors in ways that affect extrapolation and interpretation. The first-principles problem is coordinate separation: represent position without contaminating content geometry. PoPE analyzes the entanglement and proposes polar-coordinate positional structure, turning positional encoding into an identifiable geometric design problem. The evidence is clearer separation between content and location effects, so long-context behavior can be studied as geometry rather than unexplained extrapolation.

Mathematical object
Content and position components inside rotary embedding geometry.
Approach
Analyzes RoPE confounding and introduces polar-coordinate structure to separate positional effects.
Themes
Positional encoding; representation confounds; transformer geometry.

Focus and Dilution

ICML 2026

Focus and Dilution treats attention learning as staged dynamics rather than one smooth improvement curve. Attention can first condense into simple rank-one structure, then focus on useful frequencies, redistribute mass, and break symmetries. The concrete object is an attention matrix evolving through those stages. Decomposing the path shows how a broad pattern becomes a specialized mechanism. The first-principles problem is mechanism formation: a model does not simply get better at attention; its attention map passes through structural changes that determine what it can select, ignore, and compare.

Mathematical object
Attention matrices evolving through condensation, frequency focus, redistribution, and symmetry breaking.
Approach
Analyzes attention dynamics as staged transformations rather than a single opaque optimization path.
Themes
Attention theory; learning dynamics; mechanism formation.

Optimal Compositional Explanations

ICML 2026

Optimal Compositional Explanations treats explanation as a search problem where local choices can hide the best answer. Concepts often overlap, so a beam search explanation can look compact while blocking a better global combination. The concrete object is a compositional explanation search space with overlapping concepts and global optimality criteria. The paper compares beam-search explanations with optimal alternatives and finds frequent suboptimality. The first-principles problem is honest interpretation: an explanation should not only be plausible, it should be the best-supported composition under the concepts available.

Mathematical object
A compositional explanation search space with overlapping concepts and global optimality criteria.
Approach
Evaluates beam-search explanations against optimal compositional alternatives under overlap.
Themes
Explanation search; compositional concepts; interpretability optimality.

Exact GNN Algorithms

ICML 2026

Exact GNN Algorithms asks when a graph neural network can learn an algorithm exactly from local message-passing rules. Benchmark success on small graphs can overstate what has been learned if the model only fits easy instances. The concrete object is a bounded-degree, finite-precision graph algorithm represented by local GNN computation. NTK theory gives formal learnability conditions for that regime. The first-principles problem is algorithmic evidence: a neural graph model has learned the procedure only when the architecture, precision, and locality assumptions are strong enough to prove the rule can be recovered.

Mathematical object
Bounded-degree finite-precision graph algorithms represented by local GNN message-passing rules.
Approach
Uses NTK theory to prove exact learnability under local-rule constraints.
Themes
Graph algorithm learning; NTK theory; local-rule reasoning.

LoRFS

ICML 2026

LoRFS's core concept is replacing noisy collocation estimates in PINNs with closed-form residual and variational objectives. A physics-informed model can be expressive enough and still train badly if the sampled points give a noisy picture of constraint violation. The first-principles problem is measurement of physical error: the learner needs a stable signal for how much the equation is being violated. LoRFS uses analytic residual structure instead of point-sampled collocation estimates, reducing sampling noise in the objective. The evidence is improved solving in PINN failure regimes, showing that the bottleneck can be residual estimation rather than network capacity.

Mathematical object
Closed-form residual and variational objectives for physics-informed neural solving.
Approach
Replaces collocation-based residual estimates with analytic objectives to reduce sampling-noise failures.
Themes
PINN theory; residual estimation; scientific ML reliability.

RMT Diffusion

ICML 2026

RMT Diffusion explains disagreement between diffusion models through data geometry. Two models trained on different splits may generate different outputs not only because of random seeds, but because anisotropy, input inhomogeneity, and dataset size change which directions are learned reliably. The concrete object is spectral variance in diffusion training trajectories across data splits. Random-matrix-style analysis links those spectra to generative trajectory variance. The first-principles question is when an output reflects stable structure in the data and when it reflects an accident of the particular split used for training.

Mathematical object
Spectral variance of diffusion training trajectories across data splits.
Approach
Uses random-matrix-style analysis to connect anisotropy, inhomogeneity, and dataset size to model disagreement.
Themes
Diffusion theory; spectral variance; generative stability.
BATCH 47

Generation Paths, Structured Latents, and Constraint-Preserving Sampling

Rex

ICML 2026

Rex treats inversion as a control primitive. If a generator creates an image or sample from a hidden state, editing that object is easier when the hidden state can be recovered accurately. The concrete object is a generated sample paired with its reconstructed latent or trajectory state. Rex focuses on numerical inversion precise enough that downstream edits and Boltzmann sampling operate on the right cause, not a rough lookalike. The first-principles question is reversibility: can the path from hidden state to visible object be walked backward well enough to make the generator controllable after the fact?

Mathematical object
A generated sample and its numerically recovered latent or trajectory state.
Approach
Uses high-precision numerical inversion to recover generation states for editing and sampling tasks.
Themes
Generative inversion; image editing; Boltzmann sampling.

Unifying Masked Diffusion Models

ICML 2026

Unifying Masked Diffusion Models treats generation order as a learned part of the model. Autoregressive, masked diffusion, and block diffusion systems differ in which variables are revealed, hidden, or revised at each step. The concrete object is a context-dependent token order spanning those generation families. Jointly learning the reveal order makes the sampling path part of the model's behavior rather than a fixed decoding schedule. The first-principles question is order control: a hard output may require deciding which positions should anchor the structure early and which should wait for more context.

Mathematical object
A context-dependent token generation order spanning autoregressive, masked, and block diffusion processes.
Approach
Unifies generation families and learns the reveal order jointly with the generative process.
Themes
Masked diffusion; autoregressive generation; learned sampling order.

LLapDiff

ICML 2026

LLapDiff uses continuous-time diffusion so forecasting and imputation do not have to force time series onto a fixed grid. Real temporal data can be irregular, partially missing, and queried over long horizons. The concrete object is a continuous-time stochastic process used for forecasts and missing-value queries. Avoiding re-gridding preserves timing evidence, and avoiding sequential solving makes broad horizon queries cheaper. The first-principles problem is native time: the model should generate a time-indexed function under missingness, not first distort the observations into a convenient grid and then pretend time was regular.

Mathematical object
A continuous-time stochastic process used for forecasting and imputation over irregular observations.
Approach
Uses continuous-time diffusion to answer horizon-wide and missing-value queries without grid conversion.
Themes
Time-series generation; imputation; continuous-time diffusion.

Insertion Process

ICML 2026

Insertion Process questions the habit of generating every sequence from left to right. Some objects are built more naturally by placing a skeleton first, filling gaps, and deciding later which missing pieces matter. The concrete object is a variable-length sequence described by insertion actions: choose a position, choose content, and choose the order of construction. Permutation-based variational inference lets the model learn those hidden construction orders. The result is a generator whose timeline is not the final reading order, but the order in which structure becomes knowable.

Mathematical object
A variable-length sequence constructed by insertion actions over positions and content.
Approach
Learns where, what, and when to insert through permutation-based variational inference.
Themes
Sequence generation; insertion order; variational construction processes.

AGSM

ICML 2026

AGSM puts text-image alignment into the diffusion score-matching objective itself. Inference-time guidance can push samples toward a prompt, but it may fight a base score field that was not trained with the same semantic direction. The concrete object is a diffusion score field modified by contrastive text-image alignment directions. Training shapes the denoising vector field so semantic alignment is part of generation rather than an external correction. The first-principles problem is where control enters: alignment is stronger when it changes the learned dynamics, not only the final steering rule.

Mathematical object
A diffusion score field modified by contrastive text-image alignment directions.
Approach
Adds alignment guidance directly into score matching during diffusion training.
Themes
Diffusion alignment; score matching; text-image generation.

RFM

ICML 2026

RFM looks for the shared estimator underneath diffusion-policy objectives that appear different on the surface. One objective may be written as noise prediction and another as a gradient expectation, but both can be views of the same control problem. The concrete object is a Stein-control estimator class covering those formulations. By deriving a unified view, the paper separates real engineering choices from notational differences. The first-principles payoff is clarity: once the common estimator is visible, one can ask which choices change variance, bias, or control behavior and which merely rename the same learning rule.

Mathematical object
A Stein-control estimator class covering noise- and gradient-expectation objectives.
Approach
Derives a unified estimator view of diffusion-policy training objectives.
Themes
Diffusion policy; estimator theory; objective unification.

DivIn

ICML 2026

DivIn treats generation diversity as something that can be shaped before denoising begins. Diffusion and flow samplers may collapse because their initial noise starts in regions that funnel toward similar outputs. The concrete object is an initial noise distribution conditioned by a guidance potential. Langevin dynamics samples starting points from a posterior shaped by that potential. The first-principles problem is initialization control: instead of only nudging a path after it has begun, choose starting noise that gives the sampler access to more useful modes.

Mathematical object
An initial noise distribution conditioned by a guidance potential for diffusion or flow generation.
Approach
Uses Langevin dynamics to initialize samples away from collapsing modes before denoising begins.
Themes
Diffusion initialization; diversity control; posterior-guided sampling.

Structured Flow Autoencoders

ICLR 2026

Structured Flow Autoencoders combine two strengths that are usually separated. Normalizing flows can model continuous likelihoods flexibly, but they may hide the dependency structure that explains the data. Graphical latent models can express dependencies, but often lack the same flexible generation. The concrete object is a continuous flow coupled to a graphical latent model and posterior. This makes generation and inference share one structured explanation of the data. The first-principles aim is not only to assign high likelihood, but to make the latent variables carry a dependency pattern that can be inspected and inferred.

Mathematical object
A continuous normalizing flow coupled to a graphical latent model and posterior.
Approach
Combines flow likelihood learning with graphical latent structure for joint generation and inference.
Themes
Flow models; structured latents; posterior learning.

DiffusionNFT

ICLR 2026

DiffusionNFT's core concept is optimizing diffusion models through the forward process without explicit likelihood estimation. A diffusion model can be guided by preferences over generated samples, but direct likelihood accounting is awkward when the evidence is positive and negative generations rather than supervised targets. The first-principles problem is to update the generative path from comparative sample evidence while respecting the model's flow structure. DiffusionNFT uses flow matching and positive-negative generations, turning forward-process trajectories into the surface where reward information enters. The evidence boundary is whether the update improves preferred sample quality without needing a fragile likelihood estimate or damaging the denoising dynamics that make generation work.

Mathematical object
Forward diffusion or flow-matching trajectories labeled by positive and negative generations.
Approach
Optimizes diffusion behavior from positive-negative samples without direct likelihood estimation.
Themes
Diffusion RL; flow matching; preference-style generative updates.

Generative Human Geometry Distribution

ICLR 2026

Generative Human Geometry Distribution treats human generation as sampling structured body geometry, not only producing images. A useful generator must preserve three-dimensional shape, pose consistency, and variation across bodies. The concrete object is a distribution over human geometry encoded as SMPL-domain feature maps. Flow-based learning operates on that structured surface so new bodies and poses remain plausible under changing shape and motion. The first-principles problem is geometry-preserving variation: sample diverse humans while keeping the body representation tied to the physical structure that makes a pose valid.

Mathematical object
A distribution over human geometry encoded as SMPL-domain feature maps.
Approach
Uses flow-based learning over structured geometry maps for scalable human generation.
Themes
Human geometry; flow generation; pose-consistent body synthesis.
BATCH 48

Outcome Supervision, Data Value, and Distribution Accountability

BLL-Loss

ICML 2026

BLL-Loss treats supervised fine-tuning for reasoning as outcome supervision, not exact imitation of one token path. In logical tasks, two solutions can differ in wording or intermediate sequence and still be correct. The concrete object is a reasoning-task supervision objective over outcome correctness rather than exact sequence realization. The loss changes SFT pressure so valid alternatives are not punished simply for diverging from the teacher's surface form. The first-principles problem is choosing the label object: train on the truth condition of the task, not on accidental phrasing of one demonstration.

Mathematical object
A reasoning-task supervision objective over outcome correctness rather than exact token sequence realization.
Approach
Changes SFT pressure so logically correct outcomes are favored without over-penalizing alternate valid realizations.
Themes
Reasoning data; outcome supervision; imitation misalignment.

SDFT

ICML 2026

SDFT treats fine-tuning as a sequence of capability edits with a retention obligation. Standard supervised fine-tuning can add the latest skill while weakening skills learned earlier, because the newest dataset dominates the update. The concrete object is a chain of skill datasets and model states, each checked for retention of prior behavior. The method schedules or structures training so new skills accumulate with less regression. The first-principles problem is not simply learning more examples; it is changing the model so one new ability becomes available without erasing the abilities that made the model useful before.

Mathematical object
A sequence of skill datasets and model states with measured retention of previous capabilities.
Approach
Fine-tunes sequentially while controlling regression on earlier learned skills.
Themes
Continual data curation; skill retention; fine-tuning governance.

NASH

ICML 2026

NASH starts from the fact that an example does not have one permanent value. The same training item may help a capability, hurt another, matter only with related examples, or become redundant after the dataset changes. The concrete object is utility decomposed into parts before Shapley or semivalue credit is assigned. That decomposition makes data selection less like sorting examples by a single score and more like asking how each example participates in a cooperative system. The first-principles issue is credit assignment: what did this example cause the trained model to learn?

Mathematical object
Training examples with decomposed utility components and Shapley or semivalue contribution scores.
Approach
Selects data using value decompositions that make contribution scores more reliable.
Themes
Data valuation; Shapley selection; utility decomposition.

MV-FGAD

ICML 2026

MV-FGAD shows that federation changes what an anomaly detector can see. In a full graph, a weak anomaly may be visible because its neighborhood, attributes, or structural role contrast with enough surrounding evidence. After the graph is split across clients, that same signal can lose the context that made it unusual. The concrete object is a partitioned client subgraph containing subtle anomalies. The paper makes data partitioning part of the detection problem itself, not just a privacy or deployment detail, because the boundary between clients changes the evidence available for judging abnormal behavior.

Mathematical object
Partitioned client subgraphs containing subtle structural or attribute anomalies.
Approach
Analyzes weak anomaly detection difficulty under graph partitioning across federated clients.
Themes
Federated graph data; anomaly visibility; partition-induced blind spots.

GRAM

ICML 2026

GRAM builds capability access profiles without separately pretraining a model for every deployment. Different users may need different access to dual-use skills, but duplicating foundation training for each profile is expensive. The concrete object is a deployment access profile tied to data filtering and capability availability. GRAM tracks filtering and profile-specific capability control as reusable governance state. The first-principles problem is controlled access: a system should expose different capabilities under different rules while preserving an auditable relation between training data choices, available skills, and deployment profile.

Mathematical object
Deployment access profiles tied to data filtering and capability availability.
Approach
Tracks filtering and profile-specific capability control without separate pretraining for every access profile.
Themes
Capability governance; access profiles; data filtering.

Self-Soupervision

ICML 2026

Self-Soupervision treats unlabeled shifted data as evidence for robustness. Labels are expensive, but the unlabeled distribution still shows which variations the model should withstand. The concrete object is a parameter-averaged model soup built from diverse self-supervised recipes on unlabeled data. Different recipes learn different useful invariances, and averaging can combine them into a stronger model. The first-principles question is how to turn data diversity and recipe diversity into robustness without manual labels. The method uses unlabeled data as an active ingredient, not as background that only matters after annotation.

Mathematical object
A parameter-averaged model soup built from diverse self-supervised recipes on unlabeled data.
Approach
Combines unlabeled shifted data, SSL variants, and model averaging to improve robustness.
Themes
Unlabeled data curation; robust model soups; self-supervised adaptation.

UniImb

ICLR 2026

UniImb treats class imbalance as a problem inside representation space, not only inside the loss. When one class dominates a graph dataset, prototypes can drift toward majority structure and leave minority classes with too little capacity to be learned. The concrete object is a set of graph representation prototypes with load constraints. Balancing prototype use prevents majority samples from monopolizing the internal summary. The first-principles issue is representation access: each class needs enough room in the learned prototype system for its structure to remain visible to the classifier.

Mathematical object
Graph representation prototypes with load constraints under class imbalance.
Approach
Balances prototype usage so majority samples do not dominate the learned graph representation.
Themes
Imbalanced graph data; prototype governance; minority representation.

PetaGAIL++

ICLR 2026

PetaGAIL++'s core concept is generating synthetic mobility trajectories that preserve utility while protecting raw routines. Mobility traces expose sensitive structure: home, work, schedules, habits, and social patterns. The first-principles problem is not just to perturb points on a map, but to synthesize plausible behavioral paths while limiting what can be inferred about the original people. PetaGAIL++ combines imitation learning with differential privacy and adjusts noise using sample-level sensitivity, so privacy cost is tied to how revealing a trajectory is. The evidence must show both sides of the contract: downstream mobility utility remains usable, and individual routines become harder to recover.

Mathematical object
Synthetic mobility trajectories generated under differential privacy and utility constraints.
Approach
Uses imitation learning with DP noise adjusted by sensitivity to synthesize useful private trajectories.
Themes
Private synthetic data; mobility traces; imitation-based generation.

Synthetic Data Selection

ICLR 2026

Synthetic Data Selection asks which synthetic examples improve the geometry of training data. A generated dataset can match the real mean or look reasonable on average while having the wrong directions of variation. The concrete object is the covariance structure of synthetic and real distributions in high-dimensional regression. The analysis shows covariance shift can dominate generalization effects and motivates selection rules that match second-order structure. The first-principles problem is useful variation: examples matter because they add or remove directions the model can learn from, not because they merely increase dataset size.

Mathematical object
Synthetic and real data distributions compared by covariance structure in high-dimensional regression.
Approach
Uses high-dimensional analysis to motivate covariance-matched synthetic data selection.
Themes
Synthetic data selection; covariance shift; generalization geometry.

Hubble

ICLR 2026

Hubble makes memorization measurable by controlling what sensitive text enters training. A privacy experiment cannot explain leakage if it does not know what was inserted, how often it appeared, and how the trained model differs from a matched baseline. The concrete object is a pair of standard and perturbed language models with known sensitive insertions and exposure frequencies. Hubble measures how extraction changes with exposure, corpus scale, and continued training. The first-principles claim is that memorization is a dynamic exposure phenomenon: it can grow with repeated contact and decline when that contact stops.

Mathematical object
Controlled standard and perturbed LLM pairs with known sensitive-text insertions and exposure frequencies.
Approach
Measures how memorization changes with exposure frequency, corpus scale, and continued training conditions.
Themes
Memorization auditing; privacy benchmarks; exposure-frequency governance.
BATCH 49

Policy Search, Exploration Control, and Offline RL Evidence

T2PO

ICML 2026

T2PO treats exploration in agent reinforcement learning as a choice about which parts of a trajectory deserve uncertainty. In multi-turn tasks, exploration is not only the final answer; it includes tokens, tool calls, and intermediate turns. The concrete object is a multi-turn policy trajectory with token-level and turn-level uncertainty signals. Uncertainty dynamics and progress resampling decide where the policy should search for better behavior. The first-principles problem is targeted exploration: spend randomness where it can improve the trajectory, not where it only adds noise.

Mathematical object
A multi-turn policy trajectory with token-level and turn-level uncertainty signals.
Approach
Uses uncertainty dynamics and progress resampling to allocate exploration inside agent rollouts.
Themes
Reinforcement learning; agent exploration; test-time trajectory control.

RePO

ICML 2026

RePO treats preference learning as controlled policy change under a movement budget. RLHF-style training can look like empirical preference fitting, but the policy should improve reward without drifting too far from the reference behavior. The concrete object is a policy distribution updated against preference evidence under a KL distance constraint. The method derives a closed-form regret-minimizing update compatible with DPO-style training. The first-principles problem is justified movement: preferences can support changing the policy, but the reference model remains the anchor that limits how far the update may go.

Mathematical object
A policy distribution updated against preference evidence under a KL distance constraint.
Approach
Derives a closed-form regret-minimizing policy update compatible with DPO-style preference training.
Themes
Preference optimization; KL control; reinforcement learning theory.

Critique-GRPO

ICML 2026

Critique-GRPO makes critique part of the exploration loop rather than an after-the-fact comment. A reasoning policy can sample many attempts, but without structured critique it may keep revisiting the same flawed path. The concrete object is a reasoning rollout paired with critique signals that identify trajectory-level weaknesses. Those critiques guide GRPO-style exploration toward different and better attempts. The first-principles problem is learning from reasons: scalar reward says that an attempt failed, while critique can say what part of the path should be changed or preserved.

Mathematical object
Reasoning rollouts paired with critique signals that identify trajectory-level weaknesses.
Approach
Uses critique-guided exploration inside GRPO to improve reasoning attempts and Pass@1 behavior.
Themes
Process feedback; reasoning RL; critique as training evidence.

LASER

ICML 2026

LASER treats active sensing as latent planning over what would be learned by measuring. In sparse field reconstruction, the agent does not know the whole environment and must choose observations that most improve the reconstructed field. The concrete object is a latent model of possible fields and candidate sensing actions with reconstruction value. By simulating what-if measurements and rewarding information gain, the policy can evaluate actions before spending real sensing effort. The first-principles problem is action value as knowledge gain: a measurement is useful when it changes what can be reconstructed.

Mathematical object
A latent model of sparse fields and candidate sensing actions with reconstruction value.
Approach
Runs latent what-if simulations and rewards actions that improve sparse field reconstruction.
Themes
Active sensing; intrinsic reward; scientific and physical-domain control.

Entropy Control

ICML 2026

Entropy Control treats exploration pressure during LLM reinforcement learning as a feedback-controlled quantity. A fixed entropy bonus can be too weak when the policy collapses early and too strong once a useful reasoning path has been found. The concrete object is a policy entropy coefficient coupled to the dynamics of reasoning rollouts. Adapting that coefficient lets training keep enough diversity to discover better procedures while still allowing convergence. The first-principles problem is uncertainty control: the model should remain exploratory when search is needed and become decisive when evidence supports a good path.

Mathematical object
A policy entropy coefficient coupled to the training dynamics of LLM reasoning rollouts.
Approach
Adjusts entropy pressure during RL to balance exploration and exploitation on reasoning tasks.
Themes
Exploration control; LLM RL; training dynamics.

SCIQL

ICML 2026

SCIQL treats offline policy improvement as behavior improvement under a style constraint. Offline RL cannot freely explore, so it must stay within the support of logged trajectories. If those trajectories also carry style labels, improving reward should not erase the behavioral style that made the data meaningful. The concrete object is an offline trajectory set with subtrajectory style labels and implicit Q-values. Style-conditioned IQL optimizes better behavior while preserving style structure. The first-principles problem is fixed-evidence improvement: learn what is better without inventing unsupported actions or losing the mode of behavior being requested.

Mathematical object
Offline trajectories with subtrajectory style labels and implicit Q-values.
Approach
Conditions offline IQL on style supervision so policy improvement respects trajectory style structure.
Themes
Offline reinforcement learning; style preservation; support-constrained improvement.

JustGRPO

ICML 2026

JustGRPO treats reinforcement learning for diffusion language models as a place to remove unnecessary order machinery. Diffusion models can decode in parallel, but RL procedures can add arbitrary ordering choices that are not essential to the policy objective. The concrete object is a diffusion-language-model policy update with constrained decoding order and group-relative rewards. The method keeps parallel decoding while simplifying GRPO-style training and preserving reasoning performance. The first-principles problem is necessary structure: keep what credit assignment requires, remove what only reflects a convenient but accidental decoding order.

Mathematical object
A diffusion-language-model policy update with constrained decoding order and group-relative rewards.
Approach
Uses a simpler constrained-order GRPO formulation that keeps parallel decoding advantages.
Themes
Diffusion language models; RL simplification; reasoning post-training.

PG Post-Training

ICML 2026

PG Post-Training treats process rewards as a way to shrink the search space of policy learning. If feedback arrives only after a whole sequence is complete, training may need broad sampling before it finds useful behavior. The concrete object is token-level process-reward evidence expressed through likelihood quantiles inside generated trajectories. By attaching signal to local steps, the method reduces dependence on sequence-level coverage. The first-principles question is where feedback should enter: a whole-answer score says whether the ending worked, while process evidence can show which parts of the path were already promising or wrong.

Mathematical object
Token-level process-reward evidence expressed through likelihood quantiles inside generated trajectories.
Approach
Uses token-level quantile signals to make post-training less dependent on broad sequence-level coverage.
Themes
Process rewards; post-training; search-space compression.

SOL

ICML 2026

SOL treats option learning as both an algorithmic abstraction and a throughput problem. In long-horizon environments, primitive actions are too small for efficient credit assignment, so options compress repeated behavior into reusable temporal chunks. The concrete object is a hierarchical policy with options trained from very large-scale interaction. The method scales option-learning policy gradients to high-throughput NetHack experience. The first-principles problem is evidence for hierarchy: temporal abstractions help only when the system can collect enough experience to learn which chunks of behavior are actually reusable.

Mathematical object
Hierarchical policies with options trained from very large-scale environment interaction.
Approach
Scales option-learning policy gradients to high-throughput NetHack training.
Themes
Hierarchical RL; option learning; systems-aware training scale.

JitRL

ICML 2026

JitRL treats training-free adaptation as a local policy update with a KL boundary. A deployment may need behavior to change immediately from a reward or constraint signal, without running a full training loop. The concrete object is a logit update constrained to stay close to a reference distribution. The method derives a closed-form adjustment from a KL-constrained policy optimization objective. The first-principles problem is just-in-time control: move the policy enough to fit the current situation while keeping the update small enough that the reference behavior remains recognizable and bounded.

Mathematical object
Policy logits updated under a KL constraint against a reference distribution at inference time.
Approach
Derives a closed-form logit adjustment for training-free reward-conditioned policy adaptation.
Themes
Inference-time control; KL-constrained optimization; policy adaptation.
BATCH 50

Interpretability as Intervention and Evidence Flow

CRV

ICLR 2026

CRV checks reasoning by looking at the computation behind the explanation. A chain of thought can be fluent and still not match the internal route that produced the answer. The concrete object is a computational attribution graph whose structure records how information moved through the model. CRV classifies graph patterns that indicate faithful reasoning or structural errors. The first-principles question is evidence for faithfulness: did the model use the stated steps, or did it write a plausible story after a different computation? This places interpretability directly inside reasoning verification.

Mathematical object
A computational attribution graph whose structure fingerprints internal reasoning behavior.
Approach
Classifies graph patterns that distinguish faithful reasoning from structural reasoning errors.
Themes
Interpretability as intervention; reasoning verification; attribution graphs.

Linear Causal Representation Learning

ICML 2026

Linear Causal Representation Learning treats environments as evidence for recovering latent causes. A representation can predict well while mixing causal features together, which makes it weak for interventions or explanations. The concrete object is a set of latent features connected by a causal order across heterogeneous environments. Environment variation is used to infer order, prune spurious influence, and disentangle hidden causes. The first-principles problem is causal coordinates: a useful representation should expose stable causes and their relations, not only compress observations into features that correlate with labels.

Mathematical object
Latent features connected by a causal order across heterogeneous environments.
Approach
Uses environment variation to infer causal order, remove spurious influence, and disentangle latent causes.
Themes
Causal representation learning; interpretability; environment heterogeneity.

Time Series Saliency Maps

ICML 2026

Time Series Saliency Maps asks whether an explanation depends too much on the coordinates used to view a signal. A time-series pattern may be obvious in frequency, wavelet, or another invertible transform, even if it is hard to see in raw time. The concrete object is an attribution map transported through differentiable invertible signal transforms. The paper extends Integrated Gradients so saliency can be computed across those domains. The first-principles rule is that attribution should follow the evidence in the signal, not become arbitrary because the same information was expressed in a different valid coordinate system.

Mathematical object
A time-series attribution map transported through invertible differentiable signal transforms.
Approach
Extends Integrated Gradients so attribution can be computed across transformed time-series domains.
Themes
Time-series interpretability; saliency; transform-invariant evidence.

Universal Redundancies in TSFMs

ICML 2026

Universal Redundancies in TSFMs treats pruning as a test of functional necessity. Large time-series foundation models can contain heads and layers that repeat mechanisms across datasets, but ordinary compression can mistake accidental removability for stable redundancy. The concrete object is a set of layer and attention-head components with measured output contribution across time-series tasks. Ablation and direct logit attribution identify components that remain unnecessary across settings. The first-principles problem is internal necessity: remove parts only when intervention evidence shows the output behavior that matters is preserved.

Mathematical object
Layer and attention-head components in time-series foundation models with measured output contribution.
Approach
Combines ablation and direct logit attribution to find redundant internal components across settings.
Themes
Model pruning; component attribution; time-series foundation models.

FlashTrace

ICML 2026

FlashTrace treats attribution as ancestry through a reasoning chain. A final answer may depend on earlier generated steps, retrieved evidence, and original input tokens, so explaining only the last token misses the real source of the claim. The concrete object is a recursive attribution path from final outputs through intermediate states back to source inputs. The method propagates attribution backward through the chain. The first-principles problem is evidence ancestry: for long reasoning, a faithful explanation should show which earlier facts and steps actually carried the final answer.

Mathematical object
A recursive attribution path from final reasoning outputs through intermediate steps back to source inputs.
Approach
Propagates attribution through long reasoning chains so final claims remain tied to source evidence.
Themes
Long-horizon attribution; reasoning faithfulness; evidence lineage.

ADEPT

ICML 2026

ADEPT keeps minority emotion labels as evidence instead of averaging them away. In affective tasks, annotator disagreement can mean ambiguity, mixed emotion, or multiple valid readings, not just noise around one true label. The concrete object is an affective annotation distribution that includes minority co-emotion signals. The method trains interpretation while preserving that distributional target. The first-principles problem is evidence compression: when a dataset is collapsed to consensus, it may erase the very uncertainty that makes the emotional situation honest. ADEPT makes ambiguity part of the object being learned.

Mathematical object
Affective annotation distributions that include minority co-emotion evidence.
Approach
Models minority emotion annotations as useful ambiguity signals rather than discarding them as noise.
Themes
Human-label interpretation; ambiguity preservation; affective ML.

Categorical ANOVA

ICML 2026

Categorical ANOVA gives categorical model explanations an exact accounting object under dependence. For tabular or categorical inputs, interpretability needs to know which variable acts alone and which variables matter through interactions. The concrete object is a categorical function decomposed into main effects and interaction terms under a dependent input distribution. Closed-form decompositions prevent correlated categories from receiving misleading credit. The first-principles problem is attribution with dependence: when inputs are statistically tied together, a valid explanation must separate direct contribution from contribution borrowed through another variable's association.

Mathematical object
A categorical function decomposed into main effects and interactions under dependent input distributions.
Approach
Derives exact ANOVA-style decompositions for categorical variables with arbitrary dependence.
Themes
Functional attribution; categorical models; interaction decomposition.

DecodeShare

ICML 2026

DecodeShare's core concept is that decode-time hidden states can contain a compact shared subspace across tasks. During generation, a model stores intermediate state in the KV cache, but not every direction in that state is equally task-specific. The first-principles problem is separating reusable computation from local detail: which hidden directions support many tasks, and which only matter for the current prompt? DecodeShare identifies task-general directions in decode-time states, making the cache interpretable as structured computation rather than an opaque memory store. The evidence is preserved behavior after sharing or projecting through that compact subspace.

Mathematical object
Decode-time hidden states and KV-cache representations projected into a shared task-general subspace.
Approach
Finds compact shared directions that preserve useful decode-time behavior across tasks.
Themes
Decode-time representations; KV-cache analysis; shared subspaces.

Information Flow UQ

ICML 2026

Information Flow UQ checks whether a RAG answer actually used the retrieved evidence. Retrieval alone does not prove grounding; the model may ignore the relevant passage and answer from prior belief, neighboring tokens, or a memorized pattern. The concrete object is layer-wise information contribution from context tokens to output tokens. Tracing those contributions turns grounding into a measured flow through the network. The first-principles problem is evidence use: a document only supports an answer if information from that document changes the generated claim in the direction the answer depends on.

Mathematical object
Layer-wise information contributions from retrieved context tokens to generated output tokens.
Approach
Tracks context-token influence through model layers to assess whether outputs use relevant retrieved evidence.
Themes
RAG grounding; uncertainty and evidence flow; attribution diagnostics.

Obfuscation Atlas

ICML 2026

Obfuscation Atlas asks what happens when an interpretability detector becomes part of the game. A white-box probe may reveal deception while it is only measuring a model. But if its score affects selection, reward, or training, the model can learn to pass the detector while preserving the behavior the detector was meant to expose. The concrete object is a deception-detector score used as an optimization signal. The paper studies evasive internal representations under that pressure. The first-principles warning is that interpretability tools are not outside the system once models are trained against them.

Mathematical object
White-box deception-detector scores used as signals that policies can optimize against.
Approach
Studies how detector-based rewards or selection pressure create evasive internal representations.
Themes
Probe gaming; deception detection; interpretability under optimization.
BATCH 51

Representation Geometry, Latent Dynamics, and Structural Evidence

FedARC

ICML 2026

FedARC treats federated personalization as correction of residual feature mismatch. Different clients can share a task label while seeing different feature geometry, so averaging updates can blur local structure that matters. The concrete object is a client representation decomposed into shared structure and residual heterogeneity. The method compensates fine-grained cross-client residuals to improve personalization and generalization. The first-principles problem is what to share: keep the common representation useful across clients while leaving room for local feature differences that the global model should not erase.

Mathematical object
Client feature representations decomposed into shared structure and residual heterogeneity.
Approach
Compensates cross-client residual feature mismatch to improve both personalization and generalization.
Themes
Federated representation geometry; personalization; feature heterogeneity.

Attention Mean-Field

ICML 2026

Attention Mean-Field views a Transformer forward pass as motion of a token population. Matrix multiplication describes the computation mechanically, but mean-field analysis asks how representations move through a geometric system. The concrete object is token representations evolving as particles under attention and perceptron dynamics. The paper studies how perceptron blocks localize critical points and concentrate computation. The first-principles value is a dynamic picture of representation geometry: embeddings are not static points waiting to be read, but states pushed by attention rules into regions where useful distinctions may sharpen.

Mathematical object
Token representations evolving as particles under mean-field attention and perceptron dynamics.
Approach
Uses mean-field analysis to characterize critical-point localization in Transformer forward passes.
Themes
Transformer theory; particle dynamics; representation geometry.

HSR-NMF

ICML 2026

HSR-NMF asks what a learned map is made of when an agent has to move, explore, and transfer knowledge. A compact representation is not automatically useful if each dimension mixes several places, routes, or topological relations. The concrete object is a set of sparse non-negative factors whose parts can be read as reusable spatial structure. By decomposing learned maps with NMF, the method makes representation learning closer to building a small set of interpretable map pieces, each of which can support exploration or transfer instead of remaining a hidden vector coordinate.

Mathematical object
Sparse non-negative low-rank factors representing topological structure in a learned map.
Approach
Applies NMF to recover interpretable map factors that support transfer and exploration.
Themes
Low-rank representation; topology; interpretable exploration.

Embedding Collapse

ICML 2026

Embedding Collapse shows that too few Euclidean dimensions can make contrastive ordering impossible. A smaller vector is not always a cheaper version of the same representation; geometry can prevent the target triplet comparisons from fitting. The concrete object is a set of contrastive triplet relationships embedded in finite-dimensional Euclidean space. The paper proves that too-small embeddings can violate many realizable triplets. The first-principles problem is representational capacity: dimensionality is a correctness condition when the task asks the space to preserve many relative distances, not merely a compression knob.

Mathematical object
Contrastive triplet relationships embedded in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
Approach
Proves dimensionality limits that force triplet-order violations when embeddings are too small.
Themes
Embedding geometry; contrastive learning; dimensional collapse.

Reasoning Dimensionality

ICML 2026

Reasoning Dimensionality asks how many independent directions a model uses to solve reasoning tasks. A model can answer familiar math problems by spreading behavior across many fragile variations, or it can compress the method into a smaller strategy that transfers. The concrete object is the intrinsic dimension of the reasoning strategy space, measured against in-distribution and out-of-distribution GSM8K performance. The paper finds that lower strategy dimension often goes with better generalization. The first-principles idea is representation economy: reusable reasoning should need fewer degrees of freedom than memorized surface patterns.

Mathematical object
An intrinsic-dimensionality estimate of reasoning strategies and their task performance.
Approach
Measures strategy dimension and relates compactness to ID/OOD reasoning performance.
Themes
Reasoning representations; intrinsic dimension; generalization diagnostics.

LAMP

ICML 2026

LAMP's core concept is preserving long-range graph dependencies without accumulating redundant memory. Graph models often need information from distant nodes, but repeated propagation can mix useful signals with noise, oversmooth distinctions, or carry stale history. The first-principles problem is selective persistence: what distant information should remain available, and what should be forgotten before it clutters the representation? LAMP keeps extended dependency signals while limiting redundant accumulation, making graph memory a controlled resource. The evidence is whether long-range tasks improve without losing local discrimination, showing that memory depth must be managed rather than simply increased.

Mathematical object
Graph node representations carrying selected long-range dependency signals.
Approach
Maintains useful extended graph information while limiting redundant or noisy memory buildup.
Themes
Graph representation; long-range dependencies; memory control.

HTI

ICLR 2026

HTI treats hyperparameters as forces that move model behavior along a path, not merely knobs that select a final score. Different settings can push training through different regions of a behavioral manifold before reaching an outcome. The concrete object is a behavior trajectory conditioned by hyperparameter choices. Conditional Lagrangian optimal transport, least-action structure, and manifold priors infer the geodesic-like path that explains the change. The first-principles value is interpretation: a table of validation scores says which setting won, while a path explains how the setting changed the model's behavior.

Mathematical object
Behavior trajectories on a model manifold conditioned by hyperparameter settings.
Approach
Uses conditional Lagrangian optimal transport with least-action and manifold priors to infer geodesic paths.
Themes
Optimal transport; model behavior geometry; hyperparameter interpretation.

TD-JEPA

ICLR 2026

TD-JEPA's core concept is successor features inside latent JEPA-style predictive space. A predictive representation can encode what future observations may look like, but control needs a sharper object: how features accumulate under a policy after an action is chosen. The first-principles problem is action-conditioned representation: identify latent directions that summarize long-run consequences, not just next-step prediction. TD-JEPA theoretically links policy-conditioned predictors to low-rank dynamics and latent successor features. The evidence is a formal bridge between self-supervised prediction and the RL object that says what future state features an action makes reachable.

Mathematical object
Policy-conditioned latent predictors with low-rank dynamics and successor-feature structure.
Approach
Derives how JEPA-style predictive representations can encode latent successor features.
Themes
Latent dynamics; successor features; self-supervised control representations.

Information Shapes Koopman Representation

ICLR 2026

Information Shapes Koopman Representation treats nonlinear dynamics as something that must keep enough distinct latent modes to be useful. Koopman methods look for a space where nonlinear motion becomes linear, but a finite subspace can collapse onto the easiest modes and ignore the rest. The concrete object is a finite Koopman latent subspace with entropy-controlled dynamical mode diversity. Information criteria push the representation to preserve multiple modes. The first-principles problem is dynamical sufficiency: the latent space must contain the motions needed to explain the system, not only the most convenient ones.

Mathematical object
A finite Koopman latent subspace with entropy-controlled dynamical mode diversity.
Approach
Uses information and entropy criteria to prevent collapse of diverse dynamical modes.
Themes
Koopman representations; dynamical systems; latent mode diversity.

CorreGen

ICLR 2026

CorreGen's core concept is treating noisy multi-view alignment as latent correspondence inference. Multi-view clustering assumes that different views describe the same examples, but real data can have corrupted pairings or missing matches. The first-principles problem is hidden alignment: before comparing representations, infer which examples across views are supposed to correspond. CorreGen formulates cross-view alignment as maximum likelihood over hidden correspondence variables and solves it with EM. The evidence is better clustering under noisy pairings, making correspondence part of the representation geometry rather than a preprocessing assumption that the model blindly trusts.

Mathematical object
Hidden correspondence variables linking noisy multi-view representations.
Approach
Uses maximum-likelihood EM to infer latent cross-view alignments for clustering.
Themes
Multi-view representation; latent correspondence; clustering geometry.
BATCH 52

Agent Process Diagnostics, Workflow Control, and Oversight

Value of Variance

ICML 2026

Value of Variance treats disagreement inside debate as a diagnostic signal. Multi-agent debate can look active while collapsing into shared blind spots, repeated arguments, or premature agreement. The concrete object is a hierarchy of uncertainty measures over single-agent outputs, cross-agent disagreement, and debate-level behavior. Measuring variance at those levels shows whether deliberation is still exploring useful alternatives or merely recycling one position. The first-principles problem is process uncertainty: disagreement is valuable when it exposes different possible answers, and dangerous when it only disguises collapse as discussion.

Mathematical object
A hierarchy of uncertainty measures over single-agent outputs, cross-agent disagreement, and debate-level behavior.
Approach
Uses variance at multiple debate levels to detect when deliberation collapses or remains informative.
Themes
Agent diagnostics; debate uncertainty; process measurement.

PaperBanana

ICML 2026

PaperBanana treats scientific illustration as coordinated work across specialized agents. A research diagram is not just an image; it has to preserve claims, entities, layout constraints, and publication conventions. The concrete object is a multi-agent diagram-generation workflow conditioned on paper content and visual constraints. One part reads and plans, another renders, and another checks or repairs mismatch between the figure and the science. The first-principles problem is task decomposition: visual scientific communication needs both image quality and claim fidelity, so the workflow must assign those responsibilities explicitly.

Mathematical object
A multi-agent diagram-generation workflow conditioned on paper content and visual publication constraints.
Approach
Coordinates specialized VLM and image-generation agents to plan, render, and refine research illustrations.
Themes
Scientific agents; multimodal workflows; diagram generation.

TG-RAG

ICML 2026

TG-RAG guides retrieval with a procedure graph rather than a flat document match. In expert domains, useful evidence depends on the current step of a standard operating procedure, not only on topical similarity. The concrete object is an Expert Procedure Graph linking workflow steps to retrieval and generation guidance. Step-specific evidence is injected so generation follows the domain process. The first-principles problem is procedural grounding: an answer should know which step it is executing and what evidence that step requires, because a correct fact can still be wrong if used at the wrong point in the workflow.

Mathematical object
An Expert Procedure Graph linking domain steps to retrieval and generation guidance.
Approach
Retrieves and injects procedure-step evidence so generation follows domain workflow state.
Themes
RAG agents; procedural reasoning; workflow grounding.

MAP

ICML 2026

MAP measures how production agents are actually built and evaluated. Agent research can abstract away deployment practice, but real systems are shaped by tool integration, handoff rules, monitoring, latency, cost, and human review. The concrete object is an empirical map of deployed agent architectures, evaluation practices, and operational constraints. Case studies and practitioner interviews document what teams measure after agents leave benchmarks. The first-principles problem is field evidence: claims about agents should be grounded in the constraints and failure checks that determine whether the system works in production.

Mathematical object
A structured empirical map of deployed agent architectures, evaluation practices, and operational constraints.
Approach
Synthesizes case studies and practitioner interviews to identify production agent measurement patterns.
Themes
Production agents; evaluation practice; deployment diagnostics.

DLM

ICML 2026

DLM treats multi-agent language-model policy learning as a mismatch between training information and execution information. During training, the system can see centralized trajectory evidence, but at deployment each actor may see only local observations and must act without a central controller. The concrete object is a multi-agent decision policy trained centrally and executed by decentralized actors. SFT and GRPO are used to improve robustness and zero-shot coordination. The first-principles problem is information discipline: learn from global evidence while producing policies that still work when each agent only has its local view.

Mathematical object
A multi-agent decision policy trained with centralized trajectory evidence and executed by decentralized actors.
Approach
Combines supervised fine-tuning and GRPO to produce robust zero-shot multi-agent behavior.
Themes
Multi-agent RL; LLM policies; decentralized execution.

POPGym Arcade

ICML 2026

POPGym Arcade treats value-function memory as a possible source of contamination. In partially observed environments, memory should preserve task-relevant history, but value learning can smear credit across observations that should not matter. The concrete object is a recurrent or memory-based value function whose credit assignments spread through time. Arcade tasks expose policy perturbations caused by irrelevant remembered facts. The first-principles problem is temporal credit hygiene: an agent needs memory that influences future actions only through task-relevant state, not through accidental correlations from old observations.

Mathematical object
A recurrent or memory-based value function whose credit assignments can spread across irrelevant history.
Approach
Uses partially observed arcade tasks to expose long-horizon policy perturbations from irrelevant memory credit.
Themes
Agent memory; value learning; partial observability diagnostics.

Speculative Actions

ICLR 2026

Speculative Actions treats latency as part of agent intelligence. An interactive agent loses time while it thinks, but also while tools, pages, games, or operating-system actions respond. Some likely actions can be prepared before the model fully commits, as long as the system can cancel or roll back wrong guesses. The concrete object is an action pipeline with speculative branches, costs, and correctness boundaries. The paper evaluates this across practical environments. The first-principles question is which future actions are safe enough to start early, so waiting time can be hidden without changing the final behavior.

Mathematical object
An interactive agent action pipeline with speculative branches, latency costs, and rollback boundaries.
Approach
Prepares likely environment actions speculatively to accelerate interactive agent workflows.
Themes
Agent serving; latency optimization; interactive environments.

GEPA

ICLR 2026

GEPA optimizes prompts for compound AI systems by reading the whole workflow, not only the final answer. In a tool-using system, a prompt affects reasoning, tool calls, tool outputs, error recovery, and later decisions. The concrete object is a trajectory containing those steps plus an instruction revision. GEPA induces high-level rules from what happened across the process. The first-principles task is rule extraction: learn an instruction that changes future behavior because it explains a repeated process failure or success, rather than merely rewriting one prompt to sound better.

Mathematical object
Compound-system trajectories containing reasoning steps, tool calls, outputs, and instruction revisions.
Approach
Induces high-level prompt rules from workflow trajectories to improve future compound AI behavior.
Themes
Prompt optimization; tool workflows; agent trajectory learning.

Huxley-Goedel Machine

ICLR 2026

Huxley-Goedel Machine treats self-improvement as planning over future agent versions. A coding agent can make a change that improves the next benchmark run while reducing the ability of later descendants to improve further. The concrete object is a tree of self-modifications scored by expected descendant performance. The search uses metaproductivity estimates, not only the immediate score of one patch. The first-principles question is which edit changes the trajectory of improvement. A useful self-change is not merely locally successful; it should create future agents with better options and higher expected capability.

Mathematical object
A tree of coding-agent self-modifications scored by expected descendant performance.
Approach
Searches modification branches using metaproductivity estimates instead of current score alone.
Themes
Coding agents; self-improvement; recursive process search.

Weak-to-Strong Monitoring

ICLR 2026

Weak-to-Strong Monitoring treats oversight as routing among monitors with different costs and abilities. A weaker monitor cannot review every stronger-agent action as an equal judge, but it can still catch patterns, trigger checks, and decide when humans should inspect. The concrete object is a hierarchical and sequential monitoring policy that routes behavior to weak monitors and human escalation. The system combines cheap checks over time with selective escalation. The first-principles problem is scalable supervision: use limited oversight capacity where risk and monitor competence make it most useful.

Mathematical object
A hierarchical and sequential monitoring policy routing agent behavior to weak monitors and human escalation.
Approach
Combines weak monitor signals over time and hierarchy to supervise stronger agents with selective escalation.
Themes
Agent oversight; scalable monitoring; human escalation.
BATCH 53

Scientific Generation, Physical Priors, and Executable Objects

Weak Diffusion Priors

ICML 2026

Weak Diffusion Priors asks how accurate a generative prior really needs to be in an inverse problem. Reconstruction is not determined by the prior alone. Measurements rule out many possibilities, and the prior fills in what the measurements leave uncertain. The concrete object is an inverse-problem reconstruction constrained by informative measurements and a possibly mismatched diffusion prior. The paper shows that weak or imperfect priors can still help when the data term is strong enough. The first-principles balance is between learned plausibility and external evidence: a prior corrupts recovery only when it overrules what the measurements already know.

Mathematical object
An inverse-problem reconstruction constrained by informative measurements and a possibly mismatched diffusion prior.
Approach
Analyzes when measurement evidence dominates prior mismatch enough for accurate diffusion-assisted recovery.
Themes
Inverse problems; diffusion priors; evidence-constrained generation.

Walrus

ICML 2026

Walrus treats continuum dynamics as the native object for scientific pretraining. Fluids and related physical systems are not independent images; they are fields evolving through space and time under conservation laws, boundary conditions, and multi-scale interactions. The concrete object is a continuum physical field sequence drawn from many scientific scenarios. A Transformer pretrained across 19 settings learns reusable evolution structure instead of starting from scratch for each domain. The first-principles question is whether a model can learn the common grammar of physical fields while still respecting the local constraints of each system.

Mathematical object
Continuum physical fields evolving over space and time across multiple fluid-like scientific scenarios.
Approach
Pretrains a Transformer on diverse continuum-dynamics data to learn reusable physical evolution structure.
Themes
Scientific foundation models; fluid dynamics; physical sequence modeling.

MERLIN

ICML 2026

MERLIN asks what should evolve when the object of interest is a PDE field. The raw field can be high-dimensional and tied to a grid, but the right observation functionals may follow a simpler near-linear progression. The concrete object is a latent functional coordinate system whose dynamics are approximately linear and not locked to one resolution. MERLIN learns those functionals and reconstructs fields across grids. The first-principles idea is to model the evolution of measurements that summarize the field, rather than forcing the generator to memorize one discretization of the field itself.

Mathematical object
Observation functionals of PDE fields whose latent evolution is approximately linear and resolution free.
Approach
Learns functional Koopman-style coordinates for reconstructing PDE fields across resolutions.
Themes
PDE learning; Koopman functionals; resolution-free scientific generation.

CoEvol-NO

ICML 2026

CoEvol-NO's core concept is neural-operator prediction with a persistent latent state and an evolving mesh. A fixed grid can waste resolution where the field is smooth and miss detail where prediction error grows. The first-principles problem is adaptive scientific state: decide what latent dynamics should persist and what observation geometry should move to track local error. CoEvol-NO maintains latent dynamics while co-evolving mesh coordinates through predictor-corrector updates. The evidence is better scientific field prediction because both the hidden state and the mesh respond to where the system needs accuracy.

Mathematical object
A neural-operator latent state coupled to mesh coordinates that evolve under prediction error.
Approach
Uses predictor-corrector updates to co-evolve latent state and mesh locations for scientific fields.
Themes
Neural operators; adaptive meshes; persistent scientific state.

FIDIA

ICML 2026

FIDIA aligns protein inverse folding with how designers actually use generators. A designer often samples many candidate sequences and keeps the best one, so training only for average likelihood can miss the deployment objective. The concrete object is an inverse-folding policy evaluated by the best high-fitness candidate among multiple samples. FIDIA optimizes directly for that Best-of-N use pattern. The first-principles issue is inference alignment: the training objective should match the selection procedure that will be used later, because success depends on the quality of the chosen candidate set, not only one average sample.

Mathematical object
An inverse-folding sequence policy evaluated by the best high-fitness candidate among multiple samples.
Approach
Optimizes generation directly for Best-of-N high-fitness protein candidate selection.
Themes
Protein design; inference-aligned generation; candidate-set optimization.

ReaSyn

ICLR 2026

ReaSyn's core concept is refining molecules toward synthesizable pathways rather than only plausible molecular graphs. A generated molecule may score well as a structure and still be useless if chemists cannot make it through realistic reactions. The first-principles problem is actionability: the generated object should include a route from available materials to the target, not just a final graph. ReaSyn uses bidirectional synthetic-tree generation and discrete flow edits to project molecules into synthesizable space. The evidence is improved molecular quality under synthesis constraints, making the reaction pathway part of the generation target itself.

Mathematical object
A molecule and its synthetic tree, edited toward a synthesizable chemical pathway.
Approach
Combines bidirectional synthesis-tree generation with discrete flow edits to improve synthesizability.
Themes
Molecular generation; synthesis planning; executable chemistry.

Complexa

ICLR 2026

Complexa treats binder design as generation over atomistic interfaces, not only over protein sequences. A useful binder must meet a target with the right three-dimensional contacts, so the model needs a prior over physical complexes before scarce experimental examples can guide it. The concrete object is an atomistic binder-target complex learned from synthetic Teddymer structures and experimental multimers. Pretraining supplies the model with interaction geometry; adaptation ties that prior to real complexes. The first-principles task is to learn a distribution over physically possible binding arrangements, then search it for useful designs.

Mathematical object
Atomistic binder-target complexes with learned priors from synthetic and experimental multimer data.
Approach
Pretrains on synthetic binder-target structures and adapts with experimental multimers for generative design.
Themes
Protein binders; atomistic generation; physical pretraining.

mCLM

ICLR 2026

mCLM's core concept is chemical language modeling over functional, synthesis-compatible building blocks. Character- or atom-level molecule strings can ignore the modular units chemists use to reason about function and make compounds. The first-principles problem is tokenization as scientific structure: choose generation units that preserve chemical actionability, not only syntactic validity. mCLM represents molecules as building blocks paired with natural-language function descriptions, so the model's vocabulary carries both structure and use. The evidence is better molecular generation because the language model composes meaningful chemical parts rather than arbitrary string fragments.

Mathematical object
Molecules represented as synthesis-compatible functional building-block tokens with language descriptions.
Approach
Trains chemical language models over modular tokens tied to molecular function and synthesis compatibility.
Themes
Chemical language models; molecular tokenization; functional design.

cadrille

ICLR 2026

cadrille reconstructs engineering objects as programs, not only as shapes. A mesh, point cloud, or image may describe what an object looks like, but engineering work also needs construction logic that can be inspected and changed. The concrete object is editable Python CAD code generated from point-cloud, image, or text evidence. That output exposes geometry, operations, and design choices in an executable artifact. The first-principles issue is design intent: recover a representation a human can modify and reuse, not merely a surface that resembles the target object.

Mathematical object
Editable Python CAD programs reconstructed from visual, point-cloud, or text evidence.
Approach
Generates executable CAD code that reconstructs engineering objects while preserving editability.
Themes
CAD generation; executable artifacts; engineering reconstruction.

Prism

ICLR 2026

Prism's core concept is confounding-aware integration of multimodal epigenomic evidence. Predicting gene expression from biological signals is not only pattern matching, because hidden confounders can make a modality look predictive for the wrong reason. The first-principles problem is valid biological evidence: decide which signals must be adjusted before they support a claim about expression. Prism uses proximal multimodal epigenomic signals and backdoor adjustment, so biological prediction respects causal structure rather than only correlation. The evidence is stronger gene-expression prediction because modalities are combined after accounting for confounding, not simply fused for more features.

Mathematical object
Multimodal epigenomic signals adjusted for confounding in gene-expression prediction.
Approach
Uses proximal signals and backdoor adjustment to integrate epigenomic modalities under causal constraints.
Themes
Biological ML; causal adjustment; multimodal scientific prediction.
BATCH 54

Robustness, Privacy, Provenance, and Safety Control

Sharp IO Analysis

ICML 2026

Sharp IO Analysis studies system identification when some time points in the history are hostile. The target is not ordinary noise around a clean signal. An adversary can corrupt selected input-output observations, and those corruptions may be placed where they do the most damage. The concrete object is a nonlinear input-output history with sparse adversarial time points. The method uses the sparsity of attacks to recover the underlying map despite corrupted entries. The first-principles boundary is structural recovery: robustness is possible only when enough of the history still carries the true dynamics.

Mathematical object
A nonlinear input-output system history with sparse adversarially corrupted time points.
Approach
Uses sparse-adversary assumptions to recover nonlinear system maps despite hostile history entries.
Themes
Robust system identification; sparse attacks; nonlinear dynamics.

SafeDPO

ICLR 2026

SafeDPO makes the helpfulness-safety tradeoff explicit inside preference optimization. Safety tuning can make a model over-refuse, while helpfulness pressure can make it comply where it should not. The concrete object is a preference-optimized policy with a tunable parameter controlling movement along that tradeoff. Adding one lightweight control to DPO-style training lets safety improve while preserving competitive helpfulness. The first-principles issue is policy movement: the model should become safer by changing the right decisions, not by globally suppressing usefulness or letting safety emerge as an uncontrolled side effect.

Mathematical object
A preference-optimized policy with a tunable helpfulness-safety tradeoff parameter.
Approach
Adds a lightweight control knob to DPO-style optimization to increase safety without large helpfulness loss.
Themes
Safety alignment; preference optimization; helpfulness tradeoffs.

Steering the Herd

ICLR 2026

Steering the Herd studies what changes when an LLM mediates information for many decision-makers. In social learning, agents update beliefs after seeing signals and other agents' actions. If a planner chooses the mediated information, it can shape not only one answer but a population's sequential decisions. The concrete object is a set of Bayesian agents whose belief updates pass through an information-planning LLM. The first-principles problem is influence governance: when a model sits between evidence and belief, safety depends on how information is selected, withheld, and ordered for the group.

Mathematical object
Sequential Bayesian agents whose belief updates are mediated by an information-planning LLM.
Approach
Models how a planner can steer social learning by choosing mediated information signals.
Themes
Social learning; information control; societal AI safety.

Divergent Causal Interventions

ICLR 2026

Divergent Causal Interventions treats activation editing as valid only when the edited state remains close to states the model could naturally occupy. An intervention can look causal while actually pushing the model into an unnatural hidden region. The concrete object is an activation intervention measured against the model's natural latent-state distribution. Counterfactual latent constraints reduce off-distribution divergence. The first-principles problem is faithful intervention: to test a real mechanism, the edit must change the intended factor while keeping the representation inside the model's normal range of operation.

Mathematical object
Activation interventions measured against the model's natural latent-state distribution.
Approach
Adds counterfactual latent constraints to reduce divergent off-distribution intervention artifacts.
Themes
Faithful interpretability; intervention robustness; activation safety.

Empirical Privacy Protection Benchmark

ICLR 2026

Empirical Privacy Protection Benchmark treats privacy for adapted language models as an empirical stress test across data relationships. Leakage can look different when adaptation data overlaps pretraining, comes from the same distribution, or is out of distribution. The concrete object is an adapted LLM audited under membership inference and canary extraction across overlap regimes. The benchmark varies data relation and attacker type. The first-principles problem is audit specificity: a privacy claim only means something when the attacker, protected data, and relation between training and adaptation data are made explicit.

Mathematical object
Adapted LLMs audited under membership inference and canary extraction across data-overlap regimes.
Approach
Benchmarks privacy leakage by varying adaptation data relation and attack type.
Themes
Privacy auditing; adapted LLMs; membership and canary attacks.

SGRS/LocoRE

ICLR 2026

SGRS/LocoRE treats hallucination as a token-choice problem during decoding. A large vision-language model may produce a plausible word even when the image gives little support for it, or it may drift away from the local context already established. The concrete object is the set of candidate output tokens scored by visual saliency and local coherence. The method filters weakly grounded candidates and reinforces tokens that remain tied to nearby evidence. Safety becomes an evidence check inside generation itself, not only a correction after the model has already spoken.

Mathematical object
Candidate LVLM output tokens scored by visual saliency and local coherence during decoding.
Approach
Filters weakly grounded candidates and reinforces locally coherent tokens to reduce hallucination.
Themes
LVLM safety; hallucination reduction; saliency-guided decoding.

Semantic Watermark Fingerprints

ICLR 2026

Semantic Watermark Fingerprints treats provenance as a signal that should survive changes in surface wording. A fixed trigger key can disappear under paraphrase, topic shift, or adversarial rewriting even when the meaning remains in the same broad domain. The concrete object is a statistical watermark fingerprint conditioned on semantic domains of generated text. The method ties detection to meaning-level distributions rather than exact tokens.
