The first-principles problem is robust authorship evidence: the watermark should remain measurable when text changes form but still carries the semantic pattern the generator shaped.

Mathematical object
Statistical watermark fingerprints conditioned on semantic domains of generated text.
Approach
Uses semantically conditioned watermarking to improve robustness against surface-level variation.
Themes
Output provenance; watermarking; semantic robustness.

Ellipse Signatures

ICLR 2026

Ellipse Signatures's core concept is model provenance from naturally occurring constraints in log-probability outputs. A useful signature should be hard to forge without access to the producing model's internal distribution, and it should not depend only on visible text style. The first-principles problem is origin proof: what statistical trace ties an output to the model that generated it? Ellipse Signatures uses high-dimensional ellipse constraints in logprob outputs as model-specific provenance evidence. The evidence is forgery resistance through probability geometry, making authenticity a property of the generation trace rather than the wording alone.

Mathematical object
High-dimensional log-probability output traces constrained by model-specific ellipse geometry.
Approach
Detects model origin through naturally occurring ellipse signatures in output probabilities.
Themes
Provenance signatures; forgery resistance; probability geometry.

Capacity Manipulation

ICLR 2026

Capacity Manipulation's core concept is reserving model capacity for minority knowledge. Standard training can let majority patterns consume the representational budget, leaving rare but important information underfit or forgotten. The first-principles problem is internal resource allocation: decide which part of the model must be protected so minority structure survives optimization pressure. Capacity Manipulation uses low-rank decomposition and a capacity manipulation loss to reserve capacity for minority knowledge. The evidence is better fairness and robustness because the model treats representation capacity as something to allocate deliberately, not as a neutral pool automatically shared by all groups.

Mathematical object
Low-rank model capacity components allocated between majority and minority knowledge.
Approach
Adds a capacity manipulation loss to preserve minority knowledge in reserved low-rank structure.
Themes
Minority robustness; capacity allocation; representation fairness.

WGM Domain Discovery

ICLR 2026

WGM Domain Discovery treats private aggregation as a way to learn an unknown item domain without exposing user-held subsets. Each user may see only part of the domain, and central collection can violate privacy. The concrete object is an unknown item domain observed through private subsets with missing-mass uncertainty. Differentially private discovery methods estimate how much unseen mass remains. The first-principles problem is private coverage: learn what the population domain contains while quantifying what is still missing and limiting what any user's subset can reveal.

Mathematical object
An unknown item domain observed through private user-held subsets with missing-mass uncertainty.
Approach
Uses differentially private discovery methods with guarantees on unseen domain mass.
Themes
Differential privacy; domain discovery; missing-mass guarantees.
BATCH 55

Test-Time Scaling, Reasoning Control, and Runtime Search

Recurrent Diffusion Sampler

ICML 2026

Recurrent Diffusion Sampler treats inference as repeated refinement of several latent token states, not a strict one-token march. Autoregressive decoding resolves uncertainty left to right, but some parts of a sequence can be improved together if coherence is preserved. The concrete object is a block of latent token states refined recurrently while new tokens are decoded. Diffusion forcing defines the refinement schedule across parallel depth. The first-principles problem is compute placement: spend extra test-time work where uncertainty remains, while keeping the sequence tied to a single coherent output.

Mathematical object
A block of latent token states refined recurrently while new sequence tokens are decoded.
Approach
Uses diffusion forcing to refine several latent token states in parallel during generation.
Themes
Test-time scaling; diffusion decoding; parallel inference.

PLAINTAIN

ICML 2026

PLAINTAIN's core concept is interleaving plans and answers so reasoning can receive feedback earlier. If a model hides all planning until the final response, the system has no useful control point before mistakes are already committed. The first-principles problem is reasoning state exposure: decide where the agent should reveal intent so correction can happen while the answer is still forming. PLAINTAIN externalizes step-by-step plans before continued reasoning, allowing feedback to guide later steps and reduce response latency. The evidence is whether early plan visibility improves control without turning planning into extra empty text.

Mathematical object
A reasoning trajectory split into explicit plan states and answer-generation states.
Approach
Emits and uses intermediate plans so downstream feedback can steer reasoning earlier.
Themes
Planning; test-time feedback; latency-aware reasoning.

Reasoning Loops

ICML 2026

Reasoning Loops explains repetitive reasoning chains as a failure of learned action dynamics. More chain-of-thought is not always more progress; the model can repeat states, apply cyclic moves, or inherit temporally correlated mistakes. The concrete object is a reasoning trajectory with cyclic intermediate actions and correlated errors. The analysis identifies mechanisms that make loops form and persist. The first-principles problem is nontermination in thought space: a controller should detect when extra reasoning is returning to the same state instead of reducing uncertainty or moving toward a solution.

Mathematical object
Reasoning trajectories with cyclic intermediate actions and temporally correlated model errors.
Approach
Analyzes mechanisms that create repetitive chains and identifies loop-forming reasoning dynamics.
Themes
Reasoning failure modes; stopping control; chain-of-thought dynamics.

Ctrl-R

ICML 2026

Ctrl-R asks how a model can learn from exploratory reasoning without being pulled around by noisy rewards. Search can uncover useful reasoning patterns, but raw trajectory returns can have high variance and may reward brittle tricks. The concrete object is a set of exploratory reasoning trajectories reweighted by power-scaled importance weights. The method lets the policy internalize useful structure while tempering unstable update pressure. The first-principles issue is controlled learning from search: exploration should teach the model better reasoning procedures, not merely amplify whichever trajectory happened to score well once.

Mathematical object
Exploratory reasoning trajectories reweighted by power-scaled importance weights for policy learning.
Approach
Learns structured reasoning behavior from exploration while tempering unstable RL updates.
Themes
Reasoning RL; trajectory reweighting; structured inference control.

ASAG

ICML 2026

ASAG's core concept is using attention state to decide when reasoning should stop. More chain-of-thought is useful only while it changes evidence or repairs a mistake; after that, extra tokens can repeat attention patterns or drift into harmful elaboration. The first-principles problem is adaptive stopping: identify an internal signal that says further thought is no longer worth its cost. ASAG uses attention distributions to infer when additional reasoning is redundant or harmful, turning stopping into a state-dependent inference decision. The evidence is better accuracy-cost tradeoff because the model stops from its own reasoning state.

Mathematical object
Attention distributions over reasoning context used as a stopping-state signal.
Approach
Detects redundant or harmful continuation from attention-state patterns and stops reasoning adaptively.
Themes
Adaptive reasoning; stopping rules; attention diagnostics.

Reasoning with Sampling

ICLR 2026

Reasoning with Sampling uses a base model's own likelihood landscape to search for better reasoning paths. Test-time improvement often depends on verifiers, curated data, or extra training, but the pretrained model already assigns probabilities to continuations it sees as coherent. The concrete object is a distribution over reasoning paths scored by the model's likelihoods. An MCMC-style sampler explores that distribution without external supervision. The first-principles problem is self-contained search: use the model's internal preferences to move through possible chains, while recognizing that likelihood is a guide, not proof of correctness.

Mathematical object
A distribution over reasoning paths scored by the base model's own likelihoods.
Approach
Uses MCMC-style sampling to explore higher-quality reasoning paths without training or verifiers.
Themes
Training-free reasoning; sampling; test-time search.

Energy-Based Transformers

ICLR 2026

Energy-Based Transformers treat thinking as improving candidate answers under a learned compatibility score. Instead of producing one output in a single forward pass, the model scores how well an input and candidate fit together and then updates the candidate toward lower energy. The concrete object is a set of candidate outputs optimized under an input-candidate energy. Extra test-time compute is spent directly on the answer object, not only on sampling more alternatives. The first-principles question is deliberation: can reasoning be framed as convergence toward a better candidate rather than immediate emission?

Mathematical object
Candidate outputs optimized under a learned input-candidate compatibility energy.
Approach
Predicts by iteratively minimizing candidate energy instead of relying on a single pass.
Themes
Energy-based inference; scalable thinking; candidate optimization.

PAPL

ICLR 2026

PAPL focuses on the path a diffusion language model actually follows at inference. Training may teach a denoiser under one schedule, while a planner later chooses non-uniform reverse paths to decode text. The concrete object is a denoising objective over planner-chosen paths, expressed through a planned ELBO. The method aligns optimization with the trajectories the model will face when generating. The first-principles issue is train-test path mismatch: a denoiser should not only know how to clean noise in general, but how to clean along the planned route used at test time.

Mathematical object
A diffusion language-model denoising objective over non-uniform planner-chosen reverse paths.
Approach
Derives and optimizes a planned ELBO matched to inference-time planning schedules.
Themes
Diffusion language models; planner-aware training; inference path alignment.

GLASS Flows

ICLR 2026

GLASS Flows treats reward alignment as a change to sampling at inference time. A pretrained generator already defines a base distribution, and full retraining may be too expensive when the goal is only to bias samples toward preferred regions. The concrete object is a set of Markov sampling transitions shaped by an inner flow model recovered from the pretrained model. That flow steers candidate transitions toward reward without replacing the base generator. The first-principles problem is policy transport: move probability mass toward better outputs while keeping the original model as the distribution being transported.

Mathematical object
Markov sampling transitions shaped by an inner flow model derived from a pretrained generator.
Approach
Uses a recovered flow sampler to bias generation toward rewards without full retraining.
Themes
Reward-aligned sampling; flow models; efficient inference control.

AdaBlock-dLLM

ICLR 2026

AdaBlock-dLLM's core concept is adapting diffusion language-model block schedules at runtime. Semi-autoregressive diffusion decoding can refine groups of tokens together, but a fixed block size wastes work on easy spans and under-refines volatile ones. The first-principles problem is local compute allocation: decide which span deserves more refinement based on the uncertainty visible now. AdaBlock-dLLM uses confidence dynamics and volatility bands to adjust block sizes during inference. The evidence is faster or better decoding because compute follows token-state difficulty, making test-time scaling a scheduling policy rather than a fixed generation recipe.

Mathematical object
Semi-autoregressive diffusion decoding blocks governed by confidence and volatility signals.
Approach
Adapts block sizes at runtime so compute follows uncertainty and token-state volatility.
Themes
Adaptive decoding; diffusion LMs; runtime compute scheduling.
BATCH 56

Theory, Guarantees, and Optimization Boundaries

Matroid Algorithms

ICML 2026

Matroid Algorithms asks what an oracle query really costs. Standard oracle complexity often counts how many times an independence oracle is called, but checking a tiny set and checking a large structured subset may require very different work. The concrete object is a matroid independence query charged by the size of the queried set. Under that accounting, rank, basis, and partition tasks become quadratically costly up to logarithmic factors. The first-principles issue is cost realism: a theorem about algorithmic resources should charge for the work the algorithm actually asks the oracle to perform.

Mathematical object
Matroid independence queries charged by queried set size for rank, basis, and partition tasks.
Approach
Analyzes oracle lower and upper costs under size-sensitive query accounting.
Themes
Oracle complexity; combinatorial optimization; matroid theory.

MAPF via MMOT and Schrödinger Bridges

ICML 2026

MAPF via MMOT and Schrodinger Bridges looks at path finding as a coupling problem. One agent's route is easy; many agents become hard because every route changes which routes remain possible for the others. The concrete object is a joint distribution over paths, relaxed into entropic multi-marginal transport and bridge constraints. That relaxation gives a smooth, solvable version of the global coordination problem. Sinkhorn-style solutions then guide smaller linear programs, so the method keeps the shared path structure while avoiding the full combinatorial search over every agent at once.

Mathematical object
A multi-agent path distribution relaxed as entropic multi-marginal transport and Schrödinger bridge routing.
Approach
Uses entropic transport solutions to guide smaller linear programs for near-optimal MAPF routes.
Themes
Multi-agent optimization; optimal transport; routing theory.

Learning-Augmented Paging

ICML 2026

Learning-Augmented Paging's core concept is robustness when predictions are useful but unreliable. A paging algorithm should exploit good learned advice, but it cannot collapse when the predictor gives bad future requests. The first-principles problem is budgeted trust: decide how much the online algorithm may depend on advice while keeping a worst-case guarantee. Learning-Augmented Paging controls a relative prediction budget and achieves H_k + O(1) robustness. The evidence is a bound that improves with useful predictions while limiting damage from wrong ones, making advice an explicitly bounded resource rather than an unchecked assumption.

Mathematical object
A paging algorithm with learned predictions and a relative budget controlling advice use.
Approach
Balances consistency and robustness through bounded prediction-budget control.
Themes
Learning-augmented algorithms; online optimization; robustness guarantees.

BTT Algorithms

ICML 2026

BTT Algorithms's core concept is relating betweenness/transversal-style structure to correlation clustering through approximation-preserving links. Two graph objectives can look unrelated until their feasible solutions and optima are compared under the right transformation. The first-principles problem is reduction geometry: what structure must be preserved so approximation guarantees and hardness results transfer? BTT Algorithms relates BTT and correlation clustering optima within a 3/2 factor on complete graphs and proves shared hardness. The evidence is theoretical equivalence of difficulty and value, turning optimization theory into a map between problem landscapes rather than isolated algorithms.

Mathematical object
Complete-graph BTT and correlation-clustering objectives linked by approximation and hardness relations.
Approach
Proves value-preserving relations between optima and transfers hardness across graph objectives.
Themes
Graph optimization; approximation theory; hardness transfer.

DiCoLa

ICML 2026

DiCoLa's core concept is sound and complete divide-and-conquer causal discovery beyond causal sufficiency. Conditional-independence testing can become too expensive as the number of variables grows, but a careless split can lose causal information, especially when hidden confounders exist. The first-principles problem is decomposition with preserved truth: which smaller tests can be run independently while still supporting the same causal conclusions as the full problem? DiCoLa decomposes the discovery task into CI-test subproblems and proves soundness and completeness beyond causal sufficiency. The useful claim is not only speed; it is that the faster procedure keeps the formal guarantees that make the discovered graph meaningful.

Mathematical object
A causal discovery problem decomposed into CI-test subproblems under possible latent confounding.
Approach
Uses divide-and-conquer testing while proving soundness and completeness beyond sufficiency assumptions.
Themes
Causal discovery; conditional independence; formal guarantees.

DAWN

ICML 2026

DAWN's core concept is residual critic scale normalization. In residual reinforcement learning, a learned correction can be bounded and well motivated, yet still fail if the critic representation has a scale that makes small improvements invisible. The first-principles problem is value discernibility: normalize features so residual changes remain large enough to affect comparison without destabilizing the critic. DAWN adjusts critic representations so bounded residual corrections can guide policy improvement. The evidence is more stable residual RL, showing that a value function is not only an ordering of actions but also a scaled measuring instrument.

Mathematical object
Critic representations whose scale determines whether bounded residual value corrections are discernible.
Approach
Normalizes residual critic features to preserve useful value differences during policy improvement.
Themes
Residual RL; critic normalization; value optimization.

Distributional Equivalence

ICLR 2026

Distributional Equivalence treats causal discovery as recovery of what observations can identify, not as guessing one graph. Multiple causal structures can imply the same observed distribution, so a single returned graph may overclaim. The concrete object is a causal graph equivalence class constrained by edge-rank conditions and observed distributions. Rank constraints help traverse and narrow that class. The first-principles problem is epistemic restraint: the right answer is sometimes a bounded set of causal possibilities, because data can prove some structure while forcing other distinctions to remain unresolved.

Mathematical object
Causal graph equivalence classes constrained by edge-rank conditions and observed distributions.
Approach
Uses rank constraints to recover only the causal structure identifiable from distributional evidence.
Themes
Causal identifiability; equivalence classes; rank-constrained discovery.

Track-and-Stop Theory

ICLR 2026

Track-and-Stop Theory's core concept is finite-sample guarantees for fixed-confidence pure exploration. Asymptotic optimality can say an algorithm becomes good eventually while leaving open the sample sizes users actually face. The first-principles problem is non-asymptotic confidence: control the probability of choosing the wrong arm at finite time, not only in the limit. Track-and-Stop Theory proves finite-sample guarantees for reliable best-arm identification beyond asymptotic claims. The evidence is a bound on exploration error at practical sample counts, making confidence a property of the stopped decision, not a promise about eventual behavior.

Mathematical object
A fixed-confidence pure-exploration process with finite-sample error guarantees.
Approach
Proves non-asymptotic Track-and-Stop bounds for reliable best-arm identification.
Themes
Bandit theory; pure exploration; finite-sample guarantees.

Provable NAM Explanations

ICLR 2026

Provable NAM Explanations's core concept is using additivity to make explanation verification logarithmic. An explanation is only useful if a user can check that a subset of features is sufficient for the prediction, but naive subset search can be too costly. The first-principles problem is verification complexity: identify model structure that makes explanation search provably cheap. Provable NAM Explanations exploits neural additive model structure to reduce sufficient-explanation search to logarithmically many verification queries. The evidence is a formal query bound, making interpretability a property that can be proved for a model class rather than only illustrated by examples.

Mathematical object
Neural additive model feature contributions queried to verify sufficient explanations.
Approach
Uses additivity to reduce sufficient-explanation verification to logarithmically many queries.
Themes
Provable interpretability; NAMs; explanation verification complexity.
BATCH 57

Systems, Kernels, Tensor Interfaces, and Retrieval Infrastructure

mHC

ICML 2026

mHC treats a residual network as both a learning graph and a compute graph. Adding residual paths can improve optimization, but each connection also changes memory use, communication, and throughput during training. The concrete object is a residual architecture whose topological connectivity is designed together with scalable training constraints. The method diversifies residual links while accounting for the infrastructure path that must execute them. The first-principles issue is architecture-system fit: a connection is useful only if it improves learning without creating a training bottleneck that prevents the model from scaling.

Mathematical object
A residual neural architecture whose topological connectivity is co-designed with scalable training constraints.
Approach
Diversifies residual links while optimizing the infrastructure path for scalable training.
Themes
Efficient architectures; training systems; residual topology.

CMRU

ICML 2026

CMRU's core concept is low-power recurrent memory built from analog-friendly bistable units. A recurrent model needs to preserve information and pass gradients through time, but hardware-efficient memory elements can make the learning dynamics brittle. The first-principles problem is substrate-aware memory: the update rule must work as a learning algorithm and as a physical mechanism that can be implemented cheaply. CMRU restores gradient flow through cumulative temporal updates in bistable recurrent units. The evidence is whether temporal tasks remain learnable while the memory design fits low-power analog constraints, making hardware behavior part of the model object.

Mathematical object
Bistable recurrent memory units with cumulative temporal updates and analog-friendly dynamics.
Approach
Uses cumulative updates to restore gradient flow while retaining low-power recurrent memory behavior.
Themes
Analog-friendly ML; recurrent systems; low-power memory.

einx

ICLR 2026

einx treats tensor notation as infrastructure. Tensor programs often fail because the intended shape contract lives in a developer's head: which axes are named, which are broadcast, and which are reduced. The concrete object is a tensor operation specified by declarative axis expressions and vectorization semantics. einx gives those expressions consistent rules that compile into framework operations. The first-principles problem is making shape manipulation explicit enough to check. A readable tensor expression should state the computation's structure, rather than hiding it inside fragile index arithmetic or private framework habits.

Mathematical object
Tensor operations specified by declarative axis expressions and vectorization semantics.
Approach
Provides universal tensor notation that compiles consistent vectorization and shape rules into operations.
Themes
Tensor APIs; developer infrastructure; shape-safe computation.

SparseRL

ICLR 2026

SparseRL's core concept is generating sparse CUDA kernels as a reinforcement-learning policy. Sparse matrices create irregular memory access, so a hand-written kernel can be good for one nonzero pattern and poor for another. The first-principles problem is code choice conditioned on data layout: what executable schedule should be emitted for this sparsity pattern and hardware target? SparseRL treats CUDA generation as a stochastic policy conditioned on nonzero indices, then rewards kernels that run well. The evidence is faster sparse computation from generated code, making systems optimization a search over executable decisions rather than fixed templates.

Mathematical object
Sparse CUDA kernel programs conditioned on matrix nonzero-index structure.
Approach
Uses reinforcement learning to generate sparse kernels specialized to irregular sparsity patterns.
Themes
Kernel generation; sparse computation; RL for systems.

Probabilistic Angle Kernels

ICLR 2026

Probabilistic Angle Kernels's core concept is high-throughput vector similarity search through angle-aware kernels. Approximate nearest-neighbor search is a systems bottleneck because retrieval quality and query throughput must both survive at scale; a faster index is useless if it breaks the geometry of relevance. The first-principles problem is geometric acceleration: choose a kernel that preserves enough angular similarity while making search cheaper. The paper applies probabilistic angle kernels to ANNS and reports 2.5x-3x higher QPS than HNSW. The evidence is speed with maintained retrieval utility, making vector infrastructure a kernel-design problem over representation geometry.

Mathematical object
Vector similarity search kernels preserving probabilistic angular relationships for ANNS.
Approach
Uses angle-aware kernels to accelerate approximate nearest-neighbor queries while preserving search utility.
Themes
Vector search; retrieval systems; geometric kernels.

Triple-BERT

ICLR 2026

Triple-BERT models dispatch as relations among changing pools of entities. Ride or order dispatch is not one isolated prediction; it depends on drivers, orders, locations, timing, and the match between them. The concrete object is a driver-order entity pool represented through shared attention and relation triples. BERT-style modeling lets parameters be reused while the available drivers and orders change in real time. The first-principles problem is operational representation: the system must reason over who can serve what, where, and when, rather than flattening dispatch into a generic score for one pair.

Mathematical object
Driver-order entity pools represented through shared attention and relation triples for dispatch decisions.
Approach
Reuses BERT-style attention over dynamic entity pools to improve real-time dispatch outcomes.
Themes
Operational ML systems; dispatch optimization; entity-relation modeling.

CRAMF

ICLR 2026

CRAMF treats formal mathematics retrieval as knowledge infrastructure. A proof agent cannot rely on raw text search alone, because definitions, concepts, dependencies, and notation form a structured mathematical object. The concrete object is a formal knowledge base of definitions and concepts with augmented queries and hybrid rankings. Indexing tens of thousands of definitions and reranking them makes retrieval sensitive to mathematical role, not only word overlap. The first-principles problem is access to the right formal object: proof support fails when the agent finds a similar phrase but misses the concept or definition the proof actually needs.

Mathematical object
A formal math knowledge base of definitions and concepts with augmented queries and hybrid rankings.
Approach
Builds structured indexes and reranking for retrieving formal mathematical concepts and definitions.
Themes
Formal math infrastructure; retrieval systems; knowledge-base construction.
BATCH 58

Alignment, Preference Signals, and Reward Decomposition

LongWriter-Zero

ICLR 2026

LongWriter-Zero decomposes long-form writing rewards so different incentives control different parts of the output. A single scalar can confuse length, quality, and formatting: the model may write more without writing better, or obey structure while losing content. The concrete object is a long writing trajectory scored by separate rewards for length, quality, and form. Post-training can then move each behavior more directly. The first-principles problem is reward identifiability: if one score mixes several goals, the model cannot know which part of the writing should change when the score changes.

Mathematical object
Long-form writing trajectories scored by decomposed rewards for length, quality, and structure.
Approach
Separates reward components so post-training can control output length and format without collapsing quality.
Themes
Long-form alignment; reward decomposition; writing control.

RAIN-Merging

ICLR 2026

RAIN-Merging's core concept is gradient-free instruction-following improvement for large reasoning models. Instruction tuning can make a model more obedient, but moving the whole model can damage reasoning or broad capability. The first-principles problem is localized behavioral control: identify the part of the model most responsible for instruction adherence and change that part without rewriting everything else. RAIN-Merging scales instruction-attention modules, making alignment a targeted merge operation rather than a full training run. The evidence is improved instruction following with preserved reasoning, showing that behavioral adjustment can be a module-level intervention.

Mathematical object
Instruction-attention modules inside a reasoning model scaled to alter adherence behavior.
Approach
Applies gradient-free module scaling to improve instruction adherence while preserving reasoning capability.
Themes
Instruction following; model merging; localized alignment control.

TI-DPO

ICLR 2026

TI-DPO's core concept is token-importance guided preference optimization. Preference labels usually compare whole responses, but the preferred behavior may depend on a small set of tokens: a refusal phrase, a factual correction, a reasoning step, or a final choice. The first-principles problem is credit assignment inside the sequence: where should DPO apply pressure so it changes the responsible tokens most? TI-DPO combines gradient attribution, Gaussian-prior token weights, and triplet loss to weight token responsibility. The evidence is stronger preference learning because the update follows the parts of the response that caused the preference.

Mathematical object
Preference pairs augmented with token-importance weights derived from attribution and priors.
Approach
Uses weighted token responsibility and triplet-style preference loss for fine-grained DPO control.
Themes
DPO; token attribution; preference credit assignment.

SSPO

ICLR 2026

SSPO starts from the scarcity of human preference pairs. Explicit comparisons are expensive, but large pools of unpaired model responses still contain useful signal if the system can label them carefully. The concrete object is a small paired preference set plus a much larger unpaired response distribution with reward-threshold pseudo-labels. The method expands preference optimization through semi-supervised labeling while trying not to poison training with low-confidence guesses. The first-principles question is how to turn scarce judgments into a broader alignment dataset without pretending that every unlabeled response has equally reliable value.

Mathematical object
Small paired preference data plus large unpaired response pools with reward-threshold pseudo-labels.
Approach
Generates semi-supervised preference labels from reward thresholds to train with scarce human comparisons.
Themes
Preference data efficiency; semi-supervised alignment; pseudo-labeling.

P-GenRM

ICLR 2026

P-GenRM's core concept is personalized generative reward modeling. A generic reward model compresses many users and rubrics into one score, but real evaluation often depends on who is judging, what they value, and which tradeoffs matter. The first-principles problem is preference conditionality: the reward is not only about the output, but also about the evaluator's context. P-GenRM turns preference signals into adaptive personas and scoring rubrics, so the reward model acts as a conditional judge. The evidence is whether user-specific evaluation improves without pretending that one universal scalar can represent every preference.

Mathematical object
User-conditioned personas and scoring rubrics generated from preference signals.
Approach
Builds adaptive generative reward models that evaluate outputs according to personalized rubrics.
Themes
Personalized alignment; reward modeling; user-specific evaluation.

WIMHF

ICLR 2026

WIMHF asks what is inside a human-feedback dataset before it is turned into a reward signal. Chosen and rejected responses are surface labels; underneath them are preferences about helpfulness, tone, refusal style, detail, safety, and task-specific judgment. The concrete object is a feedback example represented by sparse latent preference features with natural-language descriptions. Sparse autoencoders make those features inspectable, so the dataset can be audited for what annotators actually rewarded. The first-principles point is that feedback should be understood as data with structure, not merely consumed as a training target.

Mathematical object
Human-feedback examples represented by sparse latent preference features with natural-language descriptions.
Approach
Uses sparse autoencoders to extract interpretable features from preference datasets.
Themes
Feedback interpretability; sparse features; preference data auditing.

HERO

ICLR 2026

HERO combines two kinds of evidence for reasoning post-training. A correctness verifier can be reliable but sparse, because it may only judge final answers or specific checked steps. A reward model can provide denser guidance, but it may be easier for the policy to exploit. The concrete object is a reasoning trajectory scored by both sparse verifiers and dense reward-model signals. HERO uses the two together so reinforcement learning has hard evidence and shaping feedback. The first-principles problem is evidence fusion: improve reasoning without trusting only sparse pass/fail checks or only soft reward gradients.

Mathematical object
Reasoning trajectories scored by sparse correctness checkers and dense reward-model signals.
Approach
Uses hybrid verifier and reward-model feedback for reasoning post-training.
Themes
Reasoning alignment; verifier feedback; reward-model RL.
BATCH 59

Theory, Scientific Structure, and Hardware-Aware Objects

MDM Reasoning

ICLR 2026

MDM Reasoning asks whether masked diffusion language models can reason through parallel refinement rather than left-to-right token growth. Chain-of-thought Transformers expose intermediate steps sequentially; masked diffusion models revise many positions at once. The concrete object is a masked-token denoising process compared with looped Transformer computation over formal languages. The paper proves equivalences and separations, including cases where parallel denoising can reason faster. The first-principles question is computational form: which reasoning procedures require an ordered trace, and which can be solved by repeatedly refining a partially filled structure?

Mathematical object
A masked-token denoising process compared with looped Transformer computation over formal languages.
Approach
Analyzes reasoning power through equivalence and separation results for parallel diffusion-style generation.
Themes
Reasoning; sequence modeling; parallel generation.

dnaHNet

ICML 2026

dnaHNet's core concept is adaptive genomic chunking. Fixed tokens are convenient for language, but genomes contain motifs, repeats, and functional regions whose boundaries do not have to match a tokenizer's arbitrary cuts. The first-principles problem is representation granularity: compress very long DNA while preserving the biological units that carry signal. dnaHNet uses differentiable dynamic chunking to form latent genomic units directly from raw sequence, reducing quadratic computation while avoiding motif fragmentation. The evidence is long-sequence genomic modeling that remains efficient because the model learns where meaningful chunks begin and end.

Mathematical object
Raw genomic sequences partitioned into learned latent chunks with biological and computational constraints.
Approach
Learns tokenizer-free dynamic chunks that reduce long-sequence cost while preserving useful motif structure.
Themes
Scientific ML; long context; adaptive compression.

Floating-Point Neural Networks

ICML 2026

Floating-Point Neural Networks's core concept is that neural-network theory should account for the arithmetic machines actually use. Classical expressivity results often assume exact real numbers, but implemented models use finite floating-point parameters and rounded operations. The first-principles problem is implementation realism: decide which depth, width, and expressivity claims survive when numbers are discrete and arithmetic is approximate. The paper studies ReLU networks under floating-point computation, showing that exact-arithmetic theorems do not automatically describe deployed networks. The evidence is a theory boundary where hardware-number constraints become part of the mathematical model.

Mathematical object
ReLU networks whose parameters and operations obey floating-point arithmetic rather than exact real arithmetic.
Approach
Derives depth and width behavior under machine-number constraints.
Themes
Theory; hardware-aware ML; numerical foundations.

PhenoBrain

ICML 2026

PhenoBrain's core concept is phenotype-conditioned communication in brain graphs. A functional connectome is not a generic graph whose edges mean the same thing for every subject; long-range interactions can depend on phenotype, symptoms, and clinical context. The first-principles problem is conditional graph routing: decide which brain regions should exchange information for this subject rather than for an average population. PhenoBrain injects phenotype information into multi-hop communication and attention regulation, making neuropsychiatric prediction subject-specific. The evidence is improved clinical prediction because the graph message paths are shaped by patient context, not only by connectivity.

Mathematical object
Functional brain networks with phenotype-conditioned communication kernels and attention paths.
Approach
Uses phenotype signals to regulate long-range graph routing for clinical prediction.
Themes
Healthcare ML; graph learning; subject-specific representation.

S3GNN

ICML 2026

S3GNN's core concept is practical long-range graph learning through spectral mixing plus local message passing. Ordinary GNNs can oversquash distant information because long-range dependencies must pass through narrow local paths. The first-principles problem is communication geometry: move global graph information without discarding local structure or requiring huge parameter counts. S3GNN combines global spectral operations with local propagation, giving physical meshes, KGQA, and long-range benchmarks a tractable route around the bottleneck. The evidence is better performance on tasks where distant graph signals matter, showing that spectral channels can widen communication without abandoning locality.

Mathematical object
Graph signals processed by local message passing and global spectral mixing operators.
Approach
Adds spectral communication channels that reduce long-range bottlenecks while keeping local structure.
Themes
Graph learning; scientific computing; oversquashing.

BitTokens

ICML 2026

BitTokens's core concept is treating numbers as machine-number objects rather than spelling them out as text fragments. Digit tokenization makes arithmetic a long symbolic sequence problem, even though computers already represent numbers compactly with structured binary formats. The first-principles problem is numeracy representation: choose a token form that preserves the computational structure of a number. BitTokens encodes numbers as IEEE 754 floating-point single tokens, reducing reasoning-token overhead and helping small language models learn arithmetic nearly perfectly. The evidence is that numeric reasoning improves when input format matches arithmetic structure instead of ordinary text structure.

Mathematical object
Numeric values represented as floating-point token embeddings instead of digit-token strings.
Approach
Uses IEEE-style single-token numeric encodings to align language-model input with arithmetic structure.
Themes
Long context; numeracy; hardware-aware representation.

L2G-Net

ICML 2026

L2G-Net's core concept is local-to-global spectral factorization for graph learning. Graph spectra reveal long-range structure, but full eigendecomposition becomes too costly when the graph is large. The first-principles problem is scalable spectral access: preserve the information that global Fourier coordinates provide without treating the whole graph as one expensive object. L2G-Net decomposes the graph Fourier transform into subgraph operators coupled by Cauchy matrices, so local computations still communicate global structure. The evidence is whether graph models keep long-range spectral benefits at lower computational cost, making factorization the bridge between theory and usable scale.

Mathematical object
A graph Fourier transform decomposed into local subgraph spectra and cross-subgraph coupling matrices.
Approach
Factorizes spectral computation so graph models can access long-range structure without full eigendecomposition.
Themes
Graph theory; scalable spectral learning; engineering theory.

Rational Transductors

ICML 2026

Rational Transductors's core concept is adding automata-style recurrence to Transformers for length-general state tracking. Attention can compare tokens broadly, but some sequence tasks require a stable finite state that updates step after step as length grows. The first-principles problem is to place symbolic recurrence inside a parallel neural architecture without giving up efficient training. Rational Transductors inject weighted-finite-automaton-derived matrix recurrences into attention, closing regular-language gaps while preserving logarithmic-depth parallelism. The important evidence is length generalization on structured state tasks: the model should carry the automaton-like state forward, not only interpolate patterns seen at training lengths.

Mathematical object
Transformer attention augmented with rational matrix recurrences derived from weighted finite automata.
Approach
Combines automata state tracking with parallel Transformer training to improve length generalization.
Themes
Theory; sequence modeling; neural-symbolic recurrence.

Sticky Track-and-Stop

ICLR 2026

Sticky Track-and-Stop's core concept is stopping exploration when evidence is sufficient, even when more than one answer is acceptable. Pure exploration bandits often ask for one best arm, but real decisions may accept any epsilon-optimal arm or any member of a correct answer set. The first-principles problem is evidence allocation: sample until the decision is statistically certified, then stop spending observations. Sticky Track-and-Stop extends non-asymptotic stopping analysis to multiple-answer settings. The evidence is a confidence guarantee for returning any valid answer, making success a certified set-membership decision rather than a single-arm race.

Mathematical object
A pure-exploration bandit process with multiple statistically acceptable terminal answers.
Approach
Tracks evidence and stopping conditions for identifying any valid answer under confidence guarantees.
Themes
Uncertainty; bandit theory; decision risk.

LeanHammer

ICLR 2026

LeanHammer connects the pieces of automated theorem proving into one checked pipeline. Premise retrieval, translation, and proof reconstruction can each look useful in isolation, but formal proof succeeds only when the final object is accepted by Lean. The concrete object is a Lean proof goal linked to retrieved premises, translated candidates, and reconstructed proof terms. Neural search proposes where to look; the formal verifier decides what is valid. The first-principles rule is that mathematical automation may use learned guidance, but correctness belongs to the proof object that passes the kernel.

Mathematical object
Lean proof goals linked to retrieved premises, translated candidates, and reconstructed proof objects.
Approach
Connects neural selection to formal reconstruction so suggested proofs must pass the verifier.
Themes
Neural-symbolic systems; formal verification; theorem proving.
BATCH 60

Retrieval, Long Context, Agents, and Tool Boundaries

HSR

ICML 2026

HSR's core concept is hierarchical successor representation. A successor representation predicts which states an agent is likely to occupy in the future, but a flat future summary can be brittle when policies change or when the task needs reasoning over longer temporal chunks. The first-principles problem is reusable predictive state: what future information should be stored so it transfers across policies, subgoals, and horizons? HSR incorporates temporal abstraction into successor features, making future occupancy a hierarchy rather than one uniform prediction. The evidence is whether those features support robust policy changes and long-horizon reuse, not only whether they fit a single training policy's short-term visitation pattern.

Mathematical object
Successor features organized across temporal abstractions and policy conditions.
Approach
Extends successor representation with hierarchy so future-state summaries transfer more robustly.
Themes
Reinforcement learning; representation geometry; temporal abstraction.

Linear Recurrent Memory

ICML 2026

Linear Recurrent Memory asks how much memory an agent really needs when the state is hidden. A complicated recurrent network is not always necessary; in some partially observed systems, a linear filter can preserve the information needed for action. The concrete object is a recurrent state that summarizes observations into belief-relevant quantities. The paper characterizes when linear recurrences recover useful hidden-state statistics in HMM-like or near-deterministic environments. The deeper lesson is that memory should be judged by sufficiency for control, not by architectural complexity.

Mathematical object
Linear recurrent belief filters over observations in partially observed Markov environments.
Approach
Shows when linear memory recovers useful hidden-state statistics for optimal or near-optimal control.
Themes
RL; probabilistic inference; memory state.

Q-RAG

ICLR 2026

Q-RAG treats retrieval as a sequence of decisions instead of a one-shot lookup. In very long contexts, adding more text is not the same as finding better evidence; each retrieved document should change what the system looks for next. The concrete object is a retriever policy over document selections, trained with value feedback from downstream evidence use. Reinforcement learning adjusts dense embeddings so retrieval becomes navigation through a large document space. The first-principles problem is access control over evidence: what should be read next, given what has already been found?

Mathematical object
A retriever policy over sequential document selections with value feedback from downstream evidence use.
Approach
Uses RL to train dense embeddings for multi-step retrieval on long-context benchmarks.
Themes
Retrieval; long context; evidence selection.

RefineStat

ICLR 2026

RefineStat's core concept is semantic repair for generated probabilistic programs. A statistical program can execute while still describing an invalid probability model, a malformed prior, or an inference path whose diagnostics show failure. The first-principles problem is typed scientific verification: identify which part of the statistical object is wrong, not merely whether the code parses. RefineStat checks priors, likelihoods, parameters, and diagnostics, then locally resamples the broken component. The evidence is repaired probabilistic code whose scientific meaning is valid, letting smaller language models improve through targeted verification rather than blind regeneration.

Mathematical object
Probabilistic programs decomposed into priors, likelihoods, parameters, and inference diagnostics.
Approach
Uses domain checks and local resampling to repair semantically invalid statistical code.
Themes
Scientific discovery; program synthesis; verifier-guided repair.

UALM-R1

ICLR 2026

UALM-R1 asks what reasoning should look like when the evidence is partly sound and partly language. If an audio-language model immediately collapses speech into text, it may lose timing, tone, speaker cues, or acoustic events that matter for the answer. The concrete object is an intermediate reasoning trajectory containing both acoustic representations and text tokens. The model can keep some evidence in audio form while translating other parts into language-like steps. The first-principles issue is working memory across modalities: preserve the form of evidence that still carries information, rather than forcing every thought into text.

Mathematical object
Intermediate reasoning trajectories containing both acoustic representations and text tokens.
Approach
Allows audio and text to appear inside the model's reasoning path for complex generation.
Themes
Reasoning; multimodal models; audio-language generation.

SwingArena

ICLR 2026

SwingArena's core concept is coding-agent evaluation as adversarial software work, not isolated patch generation. Real repository tasks require finding relevant code, proposing edits, and surviving tests designed to expose wrong assumptions. The first-principles problem is executable evidence under opposition: can an agent solve an issue when another agent actively improves the test of that solution? SwingArena pairs patch-generating submitters with test-writing reviewers over GitHub issues and CI pipelines, with retrieval across multi-language codebases. The evidence is pass or fail in a stronger software loop, where correctness is tested by code execution and adversarial review.

Mathematical object
A multi-agent CI loop linking code retrieval, patch generation, adversarial tests, and pass/fail evidence.
Approach
Evaluates coding agents through submitter-reviewer interaction on real repository issues.
Themes
Program synthesis; retrieval; agent evaluation.

AgentGym-RL

ICLR 2026

AgentGym-RL's core concept is long-horizon agent training as staged interaction scaling. An agent cannot learn tool use, memory, and recovery from single-turn text alone; it needs repeated action-feedback loops where early choices affect later options. The first-principles problem is exploration over workflows: train policies when useful behavior may require many steps before reward appears. AgentGym-RL provides modular RL environments and gradually scales interaction length, stabilizing learning from short tasks toward longer episodes. The evidence is stronger agent behavior on multi-step tasks because the training horizon grows with the policy's ability to use feedback.

Mathematical object
Agent trajectories over multi-turn environments with staged horizon lengths and RL feedback.
Approach
Uses modular environments and horizon curricula to train long-horizon agent policies.
Themes
Agents; reinforcement learning; process diagnostics.

In-Place TTT

ICLR 2026

In-Place TTT's core concept is updating a language model's fast weights during inference without adding a separate adaptation system. A long context can contain local rules, repeated entities, or task patterns that static weights do not immediately exploit. The first-principles problem is controlled inference-time change: adapt enough to use the current context while keeping the base model stable. In-Place TTT updates MLP final-projection fast weights with a next-token-prediction-aligned objective and chunk-wise training. The evidence is improved long-context performance up to 128k tokens, showing that some useful learning can happen inside inference itself.

Mathematical object
Fast-weight updates inside MLP projections driven by context-local next-token prediction.
Approach
Performs chunk-wise test-time training in place to adapt long-context behavior during inference.
Themes
Adaptation; long context; test-time learning.

MemAgent

ICLR 2026

MemAgent's core concept is memory management as an agent policy. A long document cannot always be handled by extending attention, because the system must decide what to keep, overwrite, and consult as later evidence arrives. The first-principles problem is state compression under future uncertainty: store a memory that may still be useful before knowing the next question. MemAgent processes documents segment by segment and uses multi-conversation RL to learn overwrite-based memory updates. The evidence is better operation beyond the original context length, making context extrapolation a workflow over persistent state rather than a larger prompt.

Mathematical object
A learned external memory state updated across document segments and conversations.
Approach
Trains memory-update policies with RL so agents can operate beyond their original context length.
Themes
Long context; agents; memory persistence.

LeanPremise

ICLR 2026

LeanPremise treats theorem retrieval as local proof support rather than static library search. A useful premise may live in a large formal library, but it may also be a lemma just written in the current file or namespace. The concrete object is a Lean goal with library premises, local lemmas, and relevance scores conditioned on the user's context. The system recommends what becomes useful for this proof, not only what was globally similar during training. The first-principles issue is access: a proof assistant must surface the rule that matters now, under the exact local assumptions in force.

Mathematical object
Lean goals with library premises, local lemmas, and user-context-conditioned relevance scores.
Approach
Adapts premise recommendation to current proof context rather than using static retrieval alone.
Themes
Retrieval; formal methods; proof assistance.
BATCH 61

Representation Geometry, Generation, and Decision Models

Neural Effect Search

ICLR 2026

Neural Effect Search turns learned features into hypotheses that still have to survive causal testing. A sparse autoencoder feature can look meaningful, but that does not make it a treatment effect or a scientific variable. The concrete object is a learned feature tested as a candidate effect modifier in trial data. Foundation-model features expand the search space, while progressive stratification and multiple-testing controls limit false discoveries. The first-principles problem is disciplined imagination: representation learning may suggest what to test, but evidence must decide whether the proposed variable changes an outcome.

Mathematical object
Sparse representation features tested as candidate causal-effect variables in trial data.
Approach
Combines SAE feature discovery with treatment-effect search and statistical controls.
Themes
Causal discovery; interpretability; scientific evidence.

CDGS

ICLR 2026

CDGS's core concept is compositional diffusion guided by search. Long-horizon plans, panoramas, and videos contain local parts that must fit together globally, but averaging local possibilities can merge incompatible modes into one weak compromise. The first-principles problem is mode-preserving composition: assemble parts while keeping distinct hypotheses alive until evidence chooses among them. CDGS embeds population search, likelihood pruning, and overlap resampling inside diffusion denoising, so local candidates are selected and coordinated as generation proceeds. The evidence is coherent long-form outputs where local agreement is enforced without flattening the alternatives that make composition possible.

Mathematical object
A diffusion denoising process over compositional samples with local likelihoods and overlap constraints.
Approach
Uses guided search inside denoising to preserve modes while composing long-horizon outputs.
Themes
Reasoning; generative modeling; compositional planning.

T-SAE

ICLR 2026

T-SAE's core concept is making sparse language features respect sequence continuity. A standard sparse autoencoder can find interpretable activations, but token-local features may mix syntax, position artifacts, and meaning that should persist across nearby words. The first-principles problem is feature identity over time: when a concept continues through a phrase, the latent representation should not fracture into unrelated local codes. T-SAE adds adjacent-token contrastive consistency, encouraging features that remain stable when the underlying meaning remains stable. The evidence is cleaner separation between semantic features and token-local artifacts, making interpretability depend on temporal behavior, not only sparsity.

Mathematical object
Sparse latent language features regularized by temporal consistency across adjacent token positions.
Approach
Uses contrastive sequence continuity so SAE features become more semantic and less token-local.
Themes
Interpretability; representation geometry; sparse features.

Revela

ICLR 2026

Revela's core concept is training retrievers without query-document labels by using the language model's own prediction problem. Specialized domains often lack explicit retrieval pairs, but their documents still reveal relevance when one passage helps predict another. The first-principles problem is pair-free supervision: what signal proves that a retrieved document contributed useful context? Revela optimizes dense retrieval through next-token prediction conditioned on similarity-weighted document context, so language-model loss becomes retrieval feedback. The evidence is better domain retrieval without labeled pairs, showing that relevance can be learned from whether context improves prediction rather than from hand-built matches.

Mathematical object
Dense retriever scores trained through language-model prediction over similarity-weighted document context.
Approach
Learns retrievers self-supervised from next-token prediction instead of labeled query-document pairs.
Themes
Retrieval; data curation; self-supervised learning.

ExDM

ICLR 2026

ExDM's core concept is exploration reward from diffusion density. In reward-free reinforcement learning, the agent must collect useful experience before it knows which states will later matter, so it needs pressure toward places the replay distribution has not covered. The first-principles problem is novelty as a density question: where is the agent's current experience sparse? ExDM fits replay-buffer state-action distributions with diffusion models and uses score-based intrinsic rewards to drive exploration, then fine-tunes diffusion policies when task rewards arrive. The evidence is better downstream adaptation with limited interaction because exploration was guided by distributional coverage.

Mathematical object
Replay-buffer state-action distributions modeled by diffusion scores for intrinsic reward shaping.
Approach
Uses diffusion density estimates to drive unsupervised exploration and later adapt policies with few interactions.
Themes
Reinforcement learning; generative decision-making; exploration.

AIGB-Pearl

ICLR 2026

AIGB-Pearl's core concept is constrained generative planning for auto-bidding. Offline ad logs reveal only the bids that were tried under past policies, so a generator that searches freely can produce bids that look profitable but are unsupported or unsafe. The first-principles problem is controlled extrapolation: explore better bidding trajectories while staying close enough to evidence that offline evaluation remains meaningful. AIGB-Pearl combines generative bidding planners with trajectory evaluation, KL-Lipschitz-constrained score maximization, and synchronous coupling. The evidence is improved bidding behavior without reckless distribution drift, making the constraint as important as the generated policy.

Mathematical object
Generated bidding trajectories constrained by offline evaluators and distributional safety bounds.
Approach
Searches generated bidding policies under KL-Lipschitz constraints and evaluator feedback.
Themes
Decision generation; offline RL; constrained policy search.

Mamba Markov ICL

ICLR 2026

Mamba Markov ICL's core concept is interpreting Mamba in-context learning as Laplacian smoothing for Markov chains. State-space models are often described by how they compute, but this work asks what statistical estimator their structure can express. The first-principles problem is architectural meaning: when a sequence model adapts from context, what inference procedure is it implementing? The paper shows a single-layer Mamba can learn Bayes- and minimax-optimal Laplacian smoothing estimators for Markov transitions. The evidence is a formal link between convolutional recurrence and optimal estimation, making architecture a statistical object rather than only an efficient sequence mechanism.

Mathematical object
Markov-chain transition estimation represented through Mamba convolutional state-space structure.
Approach
Proves Mamba can implement optimal Laplacian smoothing estimators for in-context Markov learning.
Themes
Representation geometry; theory; sequence modeling.

Neon

ICLR 2026

Neon's core concept is using synthetic-data collapse as a direction to reverse. Self-training on generated images can make a generator worse because its own sampling biases get reinforced. The first-principles problem is learning from failure direction: if an update caused collapse, the opposite direction may carry information about how to escape that bias. Neon fine-tunes on self-generated data, measures the degradation direction, and then applies negative extrapolation to improve generation without new real data. The evidence is improved image quality after reversing the self-training drift, making collapse a diagnostic signal instead of only a failure mode.

Mathematical object
Generator parameter updates induced by biased self-generated data and their reversed direction.
Approach
Treats self-training degradation as diagnostic signal and applies negative extrapolation.
Themes
Generative modeling; synthetic data governance; diagnostic training.

OpTI-BFM

ICLR 2026

OpTI-BFM's core concept is optimistic task inference for behavior foundation models. A pretrained behavior model may contain broad skills, but at test time it still must infer which reward function the current environment wants. The first-principles problem is adaptation under uncertainty: choose exploratory actions that reveal the task while avoiding wasteful interaction. OpTI-BFM models reward uncertainty and uses upper-confidence linear-bandit structure to guide a few episodes of interaction. The evidence is lower regret and better adaptation from limited trials, connecting behavior-model reuse to explicit uncertainty over the task being solved.

Mathematical object
Reward-function uncertainty over behavior-foundation-model tasks with confidence-guided interaction.
Approach
Uses optimistic task inference and bandit-style confidence to adapt policies with limited episodes.
Themes
RL control; adaptation; uncertainty.

LoongRL

ICLR 2026

LoongRL treats long-context reasoning as a procedure with planning, retrieval, reasoning, and rechecking. Long contexts fail when the model misses the right evidence, trusts a distractor, or forgets to verify the chain that produced the answer. The concrete object is a reasoning trajectory over chained evidence, distractors, and recheck steps. KeyChain tasks and RL curricula train UUID tracing, fact retrieval, question identification, and answer verification from 16K to 128K contexts. The first-principles problem is horizon discipline: the model needs a repeatable method for evidence buried far apart.

Mathematical object
Long-context reasoning trajectories over chained evidence, distractors, and recheck steps.
Approach
Trains retrieval-reasoning coupling with synthetic curricula that extrapolate to longer contexts.
Themes
Long context; reasoning; RL curricula.
BATCH 62

Final Source-Name Coverage: Tools, Safety, Physical Generation, and Latent Diagnostics

LatentFT

ICLR 2026

LatentFT's core concept is controlling music generation through latent frequency structure. A music latent should not be treated as one opaque vector if rhythm, texture, and longer form live at different spectral scales. The first-principles problem is controllable abstraction: identify which parts of the latent spectrum change which musical properties, then edit those parts without disturbing everything else. LatentFT applies Fourier transforms and frequency masking inside latent space, allowing attributes to be isolated, blended, and changed across timescales. The evidence is controllable audio change that follows spectral edits, making latent frequency a practical handle on musical structure.

Mathematical object
Music-generation latents decomposed into Fourier frequency bands with attribute-specific control.
Approach
Masks and edits latent spectral regions to control musical structure across scales.
Themes
Generative modeling; representation geometry; controllable media.

Tool-Augmented SSMs

ICLR 2026

Tool-Augmented SSMs ask where memory should live for long or unbounded tasks. State-space models are efficient because they keep a bounded hidden state, but that state cannot hold every intermediate detail needed for arithmetic, reasoning, or coding. The concrete object is an SSM policy coupled to external tool calls. Tools carry scratch work and exact operations that the model should not memorize internally. The first-principles boundary is delegation: keep the sequence model compact, but let it act on the environment when the task requires storage or computation beyond fixed memory.

Mathematical object
State-space model policies coupled to external tool calls for long or unbounded tasks.
Approach
Trains SSMs with tool access on arithmetic, reasoning, and coding tasks that exceed fixed memory.
Themes
Reasoning; long context; tool use.

LVLMs-Saliency

ICLR 2026

LVLMs-Saliency's core concept is hallucination diagnosis through gradient-aware visual-language saliency. A visual language model can start with image evidence but later answer from its own generated text or prior knowledge, which makes the output fluent but weakly grounded. The first-principles problem is evidence dependence: during generation, which source is actually controlling the next words? LVLMs-Saliency combines attention and gradients to detect when saliency shifts away from relevant image regions and toward prior outputs. The evidence is earlier identification of hallucination onset, making grounding a measurable relation between tokens and visual evidence.

Mathematical object
Attention-gradient saliency maps over image evidence, current tokens, and prior generated outputs.
Approach
Combines gradients and attention to identify when visual grounding collapses during generation.
Themes
Interpretability; multimodal reliability; hallucination diagnostics.

Persistent Homology LLM Adversarial Influence

ICLR 2026

Persistent Homology LLM Adversarial Influence looks for attack evidence inside the shape of activation space. A prompt injection or backdoor may not reveal itself in one answer, yet it can change how internal states cluster, connect, or collapse across layers. The concrete object is an activation cloud summarized by persistent topological features under clean and adversarial conditions. Persistent homology gives diagnostics that are not limited to linear directions or single neurons. The paper treats adversarial influence as a change in the geometry of computation, not only as a visible failure in output text.

Mathematical object
Persistent topological summaries of LLM activation clouds under clean and adversarial conditions.
Approach
Detects adversarial influence by comparing representation topology across layers and attacks.
Themes
Interpretability; representation geometry; adversarial diagnostics.

CauKer

ICLR 2026

CauKer's core concept is causal synthetic pretraining for time-series foundation models. Synthetic data is useful only when its variation teaches distinctions that appear in real temporal systems, not artificial shortcuts from the generator. The first-principles problem is source design: which generated processes expose enough causal and temporal diversity to make pretraining transfer? CauKer combines Gaussian-process kernel composition with structural causal models to create classification pretraining data, then studies scaling across synthetic sample and model sizes. The evidence is better time-series transfer because the synthetic source was built around mechanisms, not just random curves.

Mathematical object
Synthetic time-series distributions generated from composed kernels and structural causal mechanisms.
Approach
Pretrains TSFMs on causally varied synthetic data and studies scaling across data and parameter sizes.
Themes
Data governance; causal generation; time series.

ScaleCUA

ICLR 2026

ScaleCUA's core concept is scaling computer-use agents through a closed-loop GUI data pipeline. GUI agents need demonstrations across operating systems, applications, and task domains, but manual data alone is expensive and too narrow. The first-principles problem is environment-native data: collect real screen states, actions, human corrections, and agent execution traces in the same interface where the model must act. ScaleCUA combines automated agents and human experts to build a large cross-platform dataset across six operating systems and three task domains. The evidence is broader GUI competence because data capture follows the actual computer-use loop.

Mathematical object
Computer-use trajectories over GUI states, actions, human corrections, and task outcomes.
Approach
Uses a closed-loop human-agent pipeline to scale GUI-agent training data across platforms.
Themes
Agents; data curation; computer use.

RedTeamCUA

ICLR 2026

RedTeamCUA treats the computer-use agent's environment as a possible attacker. The agent reads pages, files, dialogs, and application state; malicious text or visual content inside those surfaces can become an indirect instruction. The concrete object is a computer-use trajectory exposed to hybrid web and operating-system prompt injection. VM and Docker sandboxes make the attacks realistic and repeatable through RTC-Bench. The first-principles problem is authority separation: decide which content is evidence about the task and which content is trying to control the agent's actions without permission.

Mathematical object
Computer-use agent trajectories exposed to malicious GUI and web-environment content.
Approach
Red-teams CUA systems with sandboxed indirect prompt-injection tasks across web and OS surfaces.
Themes
Agent safety; process diagnostics; environment-originated attacks.

LiveMoments

ICLR 2026

LiveMoments restores moving frames by using the high-quality still photo paired with them. A Live Photo contains blurry or low-quality video frames, but the key photo holds texture, identity, and structure that should guide restoration. The concrete object is a video-frame restoration conditioned on a reference photo and motion-aligned latent state. The method aligns motion at latent and image levels so detail can be borrowed without breaking temporal consistency. The first-principles problem is reference-conditioned fidelity: use one sharp moment as evidence while preserving how the scene moves across nearby frames.

Mathematical object
Video-frame restoration conditioned on a high-quality reference photo and motion-aligned latent structure.
Approach
Aligns latent and image motion to transfer reference detail while preserving frame fidelity.
Themes
Generative restoration; representation geometry; motion alignment.

PLAGUE

ICLR 2026

PLAGUE treats jailbreaks as processes that unfold through conversation state. A harmful request may fail as a single prompt but succeed after earlier turns shape the context, make the model accept assumptions, or prepare a later instruction. The concrete object is a multi-turn adversarial trajectory with primer, planner, and finisher roles. The method searches over that trajectory rather than over isolated strings. This matters for safety because the defended object is not just an input message; it is the evolving state of the dialogue and the decisions that state makes possible.

Mathematical object
Multi-turn adversarial conversation trajectories optimized across primer, planning, and finishing phases.
Approach
Generates staged jailbreaks that adaptively optimize context rather than relying on a single prompt.
Themes
Robustness; agent process diagnostics; jailbreak search.

OrbEvo

ICLR 2026

OrbEvo's core concept is equivariant rollout of electronic wavefunctions under time-dependent fields. A quantum trajectory is not valid just because it changes smoothly; electronic states must respect symmetry, density interactions, and stability over repeated prediction. The first-principles problem is physics-preserving temporal generation: predict wavefunction evolution without accumulating dynamics that violate the structure of the system. OrbEvo learns time-dependent electronic wavefunction coefficients under external electric fields with autoregressive training designed to reduce rollout error. The evidence is accurate long-horizon evolution because the model's predictions remain tied to quantum constraints, not only short-term fit.

Mathematical object
Electronic wavefunction coefficients and density interactions evolving under external fields.
Approach
Uses equivariant autoregressive quantum rollouts tailored to preserve physical evolution over time.
Themes
Scientific generation; dynamical systems; quantum ML.

SI-VAE

ICLR 2026

SI-VAE's core concept is visual representation learning with spatial-statistical structure. Microscopy images are not just textures to reconstruct; protein organization contains point patterns, clustering, dispersion, and spatial relations that biology needs to measure. The first-principles problem is an interpretable latent space: a VAE should preserve organization that supports scientific analysis, not only produce good-looking reconstructions. SI-VAE adds point-process self-supervision so latents carry spatial organization patterns in human-cell protein images. The evidence is whether the learned representation supports statistical biological interpretation, making spatial arrangement a supervised object rather than an accidental visual feature.

Mathematical object
Spatially informed visual latents linked to point-process organization patterns in microscopy data.
Approach
Adds spatial-statistical self-supervision to autoencoding for interpretable biological image analysis.
Themes
Interpretability; scientific ML; spatial representation.

What Full Source Coverage Means

The atlas now covers all 781 source paper names from the local ICML/ICLR evidence map with no exact-name gaps and no extra atlas titles. It anchors the main conceptual lanes, the deep safety/evaluation lane, the concept-layer bridge batch, measurement instruments, agent processes, spatial geometry, world generation, optimization, representation, generative modeling, strategic games, constrained decisions, structured control, probabilistic inference, uncertainty, scaling, theory, efficiency/systems, multimodal and embodied models, robustness/safety/privacy, scientific and physical generation, data governance, reinforcement learning, alignment and preference optimization, retrieval, long-context reasoning, computer-use agents, formal proof tools, and interpretability diagnostics.

The next useful pass is no longer adding missing paper names. It is quality review: read the cards for consistency, strengthen any overly compressed explanations, and improve cross-links from paper lenses to the theme and math concept pages.
